### 274. **A default branch that moves while a task is paused at Ready is never re-checked, so the resume puts the task at Ready with a rebase judgement older than the target branch** (**RESOLVED** at `41158cb`, WP-105, session 11 — TODO, **small — not a major**: the commits at Ready are the ones CI, review and the rebase gate judged; only the *target* moved, so this is a stale re-check rather than an unjudged head; **live** since WP-73a made a pause at Ready resumable (backlog 244), on any manual pause or take-over at Ready that spans a push to the default branch; **read off the tree, not measured**; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (nearest is WP-79's successor: the same duty and column); found by WP-79, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-105** — option (c): a resume from a pause at Ready always re-enters `rebase_gate`, no loop spent.**
> **WP-105 (session 11, in the working tree for review):** closed as ruled — the `ready_head_check` duty sends an unmoved head to `rebase_gate` (`readyEntryFor`, `ready-head.ts`) for a resume, a hand-back and a retry-stage alike; measured before the fix on the e2e tier (the resume reached Ready with no second `task.rebase.checked`). The sentence *"the duty's own docblock states the gap"* is no longer true: the docblock now lists every way into Ready. See `#### WP-105`.

**What is wrong.** The rebase gate's re-check on a moving default branch is taken only for a task whose **state** is `ready_for_merge`: `defaultBranchHandler` lists tasks at stage `ready_for_merge` and skips any whose state is not (`packages/application/src/pipeline/saga.ts:1539-1546`), so a task paused at Ready drops the `default_branch.moved` it is delivered and nothing records that it arrived. On resume, WP-79's `ready_head_check` duty compares only the task's **own** branch head with `tasks.ready_head_sha` (`readyHeadVerdict`, `packages/application/src/pipeline/ready-head.ts:120-129`); that head did not move, so the verdict is `ready` and the task re-enters Ready without the rebase gate. The duty's own docblock states the gap (`ready-head.ts:59-64`). A hand-back or resume whose branch head **did** move is not exposed: it re-enters `ci_gate` and falls through the rebase gate again. (Line numbers are on WP-79's working tree, uncommitted at filing.)

**What it costs to leave.** A task can sit at Ready claiming *applies cleanly* against a target it was never compared with, and WP-26's conflict warning for that move is never raised. What still holds: the provider computes mergeability itself and a human performs the merge, and the **next** `default_branch.moved` after the resume re-checks normally.

**Done.** Either (a) the resume re-enters `rebase_gate` when a `default_branch.moved` for the project arrived after the Ready entry recorded its head (the event log already orders both), or (b) the rebase gate records the target branch head it judged beside `ready_head_sha` and the duty compares that too — (b) needs checking that `GitProviderPort.getMergeRequest` carries a target head at all, which was **not** checked; or (c) a resume from a pause at Ready always re-enters `rebase_gate` when its own head is unmoved, at the cost of one mergeability read. No loop spent (the same `enter` decision WP-79 uses). Both directions asserted: a default-branch move during the pause re-enters the gate; no move enters Ready directly. **Depends on** WP-79 (the duty and migration 0056). Related: **267**, **244**, **275**.

### 275. **A push between the CI gate's read and the rebase gate's read reaches Ready with a head CI never judged, and records that head as the one the gates judged** (**RESOLVED** at `b94a641`, WP-79, session 9 — folded by the orchestrator at review round 2, whose reviewer **measured** the deterministic path (a hand-back at `rebase_gate` after a push reached Ready with `readyHeadSha` = the pushed head); closed by `tasks.ci_head_sha` and the rebase gate passing only for the head CI passed — TODO, **major** by M5's criterion — a fail-open past `ci_gate` at the **front** door, the same class as **267** — but **a hypothesis: read off the tree by WP-79, not measured**; **live** on the shipped ticket templates whenever anything pushes to the merge request's branch while the task is at a reviewer stage (the reviewer roles hold no push, so in practice a human or a provider-side bot); the ordering predates WP-79, which only made the recorded head visible; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (nearest is WP-79's successor; WP-81 touches the CI gate but its scope is failure feedback, not head identity); found by WP-79, session 9)

**What is wrong.** The two gates read the head at different moments, with the reviewer stages between them (`ci_gate → code_review → business_review → rebase_gate → ready_for_merge` on the shipped templates, per `ready-head.ts:47-48`). The CI gate asks the pipeline status of the **live** head at its own read (`packages/application/src/pipeline/gates.ts:185-189`; `ci-settle.ts:93-94` compares the finished pipeline's head with the live one, again only at CI time). The rebase gate reads the merge request later and reports **its** head as the judged one (`gates.ts:248-249`), which `applyDecision` records as `tasks.ready_head_sha` on the Ready entry (`transitions.ts:514-515`). Nothing in between reacts to a push: the saga subscribes no push or merge-request-updated event (the handler list at `saga.ts` has `ci.pipeline.finished`, `mr.merged`/`mr.closed`, `mr.review.comment` and `default_branch.moved`), and the `ci.pipeline.finished` handler acts only for a task waiting at a gate that listens for it (`saga.ts:1333-1345`), so the provider's pipeline on the new head is dropped while the task is at `code_review`. The rebase gate compares its head with nothing. Result: Ready, with a head that neither CI nor the reviewers saw, recorded as judged — so WP-79's resume check will later treat it as unmoved.

**What it costs to leave.** The platform's *CI passed* and *reviewed* claims at Ready describe an older commit than the one a human is asked to merge. What still holds: the provider's own CI runs on the push and shows its status on the merge request, and a human merges.

**Needs measurement before starting:** one e2e (or saga case) with a fake git that moves the head during `code_review`, to confirm the task reaches Ready with no second CI evaluation; and whether any provider sends an event on a push that the inbound normalisers already map (none is subscribed, per the list above).

**Done.** The CI gate's settlement records the head it judged (a column beside `ready_head_sha`, or carried on the task), and the rebase gate — or the Ready entry — refuses a head different from it and re-enters `ci_gate` with an `enter` decision spending no loop, so the fall-through carries the new commits through review again (WP-79's mechanism). Both directions asserted: a head moved between the gates re-enters `ci_gate`; an unmoved head enters Ready and records the head CI judged. A canary on the comparison fails the moved-head case by name. **Depends on** WP-79 (migration 0056, `GateSettlement.headSha`). Related: **267**, **274**.

### 276. **A run credential minted under a custom prefix is redacted by its shape in another process only from that process's next refresh, up to 5 s later, so text quoting it that reaches `app` inside the window is stored unredacted** (**RESOLVED** at `1065d70`, WP-107, session 11 — TODO, **small — a stated residual, not a major**: the window is bounded and is the design TD-012's M5 amendment accepted, not a check skipped; the default `glpat-` shape is covered whatever the refresh by the `gitlab-token` rule; **latent with a named trigger**: a GitLab binding with `mint_credentials: true` **and** a custom `token_prefix`, and a quote of the fresh value reaching a non-minting process within one interval of the mint; **a hypothesis — read off the tree, not measured**: the implementer argues the path (agent writes, pushes, provider delivers a webhook) is far longer than the interval, and nobody measured it; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (nearest is **WP-85**, which builds TD-028 decision 9's per-process `pg_notify` listener; a shape notify could ride the same connection); found by WP-80, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-107**, per TD-012's M6 amendment (1): notify on commit in every `ROLE`, the timer as the guarantee, persistent failure at `error`, and the per-role check.**

**What is wrong.** The shape rules are module state (`mintedShapeRules`, `packages/infrastructure/src/redaction/pattern-redaction.ts:162`), replaced wholesale by `installMintedCredentialShapes` and read at call time through `currentPatternRules` (`pattern-redaction.ts:200-203`). The minting process writes the shape in the audit row's transaction, but every **other** process learns it only from `startMintedCredentialShapeRefresh`, a read at start plus an unref'd `setInterval` of `MINTED_CREDENTIAL_SHAPE_REFRESH_MS = 5_000` (`packages/infrastructure/src/redaction/minted-credential-shapes.ts:28`, the timer at `:109-117`; composed for every role at `apps/server/src/runtime.ts:234`). The module's docblock states the window itself (`minted-credential-shapes.ts:14-19`): a value quoted into text the second process stores within that interval *"is covered by the `glpat-` pattern rule and nothing else"* — and that rule is `gl(?:pat|dt|…)-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}` (`pattern-redaction.ts:82-83`), which a custom prefix does not match. Two further facts widen it: a **failed** refresh keeps the last rules and logs a warning every interval (`minted-credential-shapes.ts:110-115`), so a process whose refreshes keep failing holds a stale set indefinitely; and technical/05's WP-80 amendment says only *"on a refresh timer"*, without the window.

**What it costs to leave.** In the trigger case, one unredacted run credential in an `inbox` row, event payload or transcript row written by a process that did not mint it. The credential is run-scoped and revoked at teardown (or lives to its 24–48 h expiry when the revoke fails), so the stored copy is usually dead by the time anyone reads it.

**Needs measurement:** the shortest realistic interval between a mint and a webhook delivery quoting the value (one e2e with a fake git that echoes a pushed comment back), which decides whether this is theoretical.

**Done.** Either (a) the audit transaction that writes the shape issues `pg_notify` on commit and every process's refresher listens and re-reads on it, keeping the timer as the backstop, with one integration case asserting a second pool holds the rule before the timer fires; or (b) the orchestrator records the window as accepted, and technical/05's amendment states it with the number. The persistent-failure half gets a bound either way: after N consecutive failed refreshes the process reports at `error`, not `warn`. **Depends on** WP-80 (migration 0057); for (a), WP-85's listener if shared. Related: **259**, **277**.

> **Residual added by the orchestrator from WP-80's review (session 9).** The two-process e2e cannot see *which* instance's refresher installed the shape rule, because the tier runs both `apps/server` instances in one Node process and the rules are module state: a refresh started only for `ROLE=runner` would pass it by construction. What holds it today is that `startMintedCredentialShapeRefresh` is called unconditionally in `apps/server/src/runtime.ts`; nothing pins that call site per role. **Done** additionally means a check that the refresh is installed for every `ROLE`.

> **Cross-reference (refiner, from WP-85's discovered work, session 9) — option (a)'s connection now exists; the inbox is not it.** WP-85 reported that *"the holder already listens on the broadcast every process holds. A shape notification would need no new connection."* Read off the tree, not measured: the half that is true is the **broadcast** — `eventing.broadcast` (the `PostgresBroadcast` `LISTEN` connection) is handed to the pipeline composition in every role (`apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:915`) and WP-85 publishes `run.commands:<digest>` through it in the command's transaction. The holder itself, `createRunCommandInbox`, is composed **only** where runs can be held (`runsAgents`, `pipeline.ts:915`, `:929-930`), so a shape notification must subscribe its own channel on the broadcast in every `ROLE` — riding the inbox would reproduce the per-role gap the residual above names. What (a) can reuse from WP-85 is the shape: notify on commit through the transactional broadcast, the timer kept as the guarantee (WP-85's heartbeat poll is the same argument). No new number: this remains **276**, and WP-85 is now its dependency for (a) rather than a candidate owner.

### 277. **The write-content guard does not apply the minted-credential shape rules, so an agent may write its own run credential into a file under a custom prefix and the guard allows it** (**RESOLVED** at `505251e`, WP-104, session 10 — TODO, **small — a decision nobody has taken, not a major**: the guard is defence in depth over the Edit/Write tools only (a `Bash` redirect never meets it), the value is revoked at teardown, and a quote of it read back from the provider is redacted by shape (backlog **276**'s window aside); **latent with a named trigger**: a custom GitLab `token_prefix` — the default `glpat-` is refused today by the `gitlab-token` rule; **read off the tree, not measured**; the agent **can** obtain the value, since git's credential helper is a process *"the agent can also run directly"* (`packages/infrastructure/src/runlet/credential-helper.ts:21`); **unowned — for the orchestrator** (nearest is **WP-81**, the next consumer of the shape rules in the WP-80 → WP-81 serialisation, but its scope is the CI gate); found by WP-80, session 9)

**What is wrong.** `guardWriteContent` refuses secret-shaped content through `detectSecrets(content)` (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/path-guard.ts:253-254`), and `detectSecrets` defaults to `GITLEAKS_DERIVED_RULES` (`packages/infrastructure/src/redaction/pattern-redaction.ts:245-248`), while `patternRedactor()` with no list applies `currentPatternRules()`, the shape rules first (`pattern-redaction.ts:200-203`). ### 279. **The planner never fills `plannedProtectedPaths`, so the workspace write guard refuses every Edit/Write under a protected path — a new test file included — and a Developer's only other route to a test file is a shell redirect the command policy floors at `ask`** (**RESOLVED** at `68ecbec`, WP-99, session 9 — the *needs measurement* item answered by WP-99 (yes: four `implementation`-baseline verbs write a protected path with no `ask`), filed as **281** — TODO, **major** by M5's criterion — the product asks the Developer for tests (BD-024 §3: *"the fix must include a test"*) and the guard refuses the tool meant to write them, so a run either stops at a human approval or routes around the guard; **live** on every delivery run since WP-12 with the default `protected_paths`, and wider since WP-81's `**/` fix (a root-level `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `__tests__/` or `migrations/` path is now refused too); **confirmed by the refiner off the tree, not run**; **folded into WP-99**; found by WP-81's pre-review round, session 9)

**What is wrong.** The stage planner hands the run spec an empty exception list with a comment that says so (`packages/application/src/pipeline/planner.ts:1245-1248`: *"The ImplementationPlan's `protected_path_changes` fills these once the plan carries them"*, then `plannedProtectedPaths: []`). The plan **has** carried the field since the artifact schema was written (`packages/contracts/src/artifacts.ts:124`), and since WP-81 the Architect prompt (v3) is told to fill it. The hook passes the empty list straight through (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/hooks.ts:162-166`, matcher `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` at `hooks.ts:91`), and `guardWritePath` denies any relative path matching a protected pattern that no planned pattern matches (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/path-guard.ts:219-230`), with the reason *"the approved plan does not list it (BD-024)"* — a sentence that is true of every plan. The default list (`packages/domain/src/config/effective-config.ts:108-123`) is `tests/**`, `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`, `**/__tests__/**`, `**/migrations/**` and nine configuration paths, so with no project override every test file in a conventional layout is unwritable through the write tools. The only production callers are this planner and the ask planner, which passes `[]` for both lists (`packages/application/src/ask/planner.ts:314-315`, a run with no write tool); no test outside `path-guard.test.ts` ever passes a non-empty list.

**Two refinements of the report.** (1) *"A Developer can write a test only through `Bash`"* overstates the escape: the Developer holds `Bash` (`planner.ts:351`), but a redirection that writes a path floors an otherwise allowed line at `ask` (`packages/domain/src/policies/command-policy.ts:26-28`), and `ask` goes to `canUseTool`, a human approval with a timeout (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/permission.ts:73-103`). **Needs measurement:** whether any verb on the `implementation` baseline (a `cp`, `sed -i`, `git apply`, `git checkout -- <path>`) writes a protected path without an `ask` — if one does, the guard is bypassed silently rather than stalled; if none does, every test a Developer writes waits on a human. (2) **The guard and BD-024 now disagree on policy, not only on wiring.** BD-024 §2 as amended at WP-81 flags *"modifications or deletions of existing tests and of CI/lint configuration"*, and `changedExistingPaths` (`packages/application/src/pipeline/tamper.ts:92`) excuses additions; the guard refuses additions too. Once exceptions are wired, a plan that follows the v3 Architect prompt (*"a new test needs no entry"*) still has its new tests refused.

**What the guard must know, and where it cannot look.** Allowing a new file means knowing the file does not exist — and the hook runs on the **platform** side, outside the run's container, which is why it does not follow symlinks (`path-guard.ts:15-19`): a `stat` from the hook answers about the wrong filesystem. So "exists" has to be supplied, and the definition that matches the CI gate is *tracked at the run's checkout ref* (the gate reads the provider's `new_file` against the merge request's base). A file the agent itself created earlier in the run is then still new, as it is in the diff.

**What it costs to leave.** Every delivery run that writes or edits a test stalls on a human approval or on the `ask` timeout, or (if (1)'s measurement finds a verb) writes around the only enforcement protected paths have — the guard's own docblock says protected paths have no container backstop (`path-guard.ts:21-25`). The first real Developer run on a repository with tests hits it.

**Done.** (a) The planner feeds the latest ImplementationPlan's `protected_path_changes[].path` into `plannedProtectedPaths` for the Developer's stages (an absent or unparsable plan contributes nothing — the stricter direction); (b) the spec carries the set of **existing** protected paths — the tracked files at the checkout ref that match the effective protected patterns — computed by the platform, not the agent, bounded, and **fail closed**: a listing that could not be read, or was cut at its bound, marks the spec so that every protected path counts as existing (today's behaviour); (c) the guard allows a write to a protected path absent from that set, and allows one present in it only when a planned pattern matches; (d) a symlinked target counts as existing, and case folding uses the guard's existing fold; (e) technical/04 and technical/05 state the rule before the code, and the denial reason stops claiming an approved plan when none declared anything. **Depends on** WP-81 (the prompt v3 declaration, the `**/` matcher, `changedExistingPaths` as the policy to match). Related: **95**, **277**, **Q109**.

### 281. **Four `implementation`-baseline spellings write or delete a protected path with no `ask` — `pytest --basetemp=<dir>`, `pytest --junitxml=<path>`, `go test -c -o <path>`, `cargo test --target-dir <dir>` — so the WP-99 write guard is bypassed at write time, though not the CI gate** (**RESOLVED** at `505251e`, WP-104, session 10 — TODO, **small — not a major**: a bypass of the *write-time* guard, and WP-81's tamper check still returns every committed modification or deletion of an existing protected file; **live** since WP-54 put `PROJECT_COMMAND_ALLOW` on the `implementation` baseline (and on the `verification` baseline the Reviewer, Acceptance Tester and Discovery run); the `allow` verdicts are **measured** by WP-99 (`evaluateCommand` over `DEFAULT_IMPLEMENTATION_ALLOW`/`ASK`, 2026-09-28); what each tool then does to the tree is **documented tool behaviour, not measured in a run container**; answers backlog **279**'s *needs measurement* (WP-99 criterion 5); **unowned — for the orchestrator** (no M5 row owns a command-policy change; WP-82 edits the same baselines but its scope is egress); found by WP-99, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-104** — the four flags floored at `ask` always, in every spelling.**

**What is wrong.** The four spellings are `allow` because `PROJECT_COMMAND_ALLOW` carries `pytest *`, `go test *` and `cargo test *` (`packages/domain/src/policies/command-policy.ts:249-264`), spread into `DEFAULT_IMPLEMENTATION_ALLOW` (`command-policy.ts:288`) and into the verification baseline (`command-policy.ts:328`), and no `HAZARDOUS_ARGUMENTS` entry (`command-policy.ts:443`) floors a path argument. The list's docblock already names three of them and calls them *"contained by the workspace-only writable mount"* (`command-policy.ts:234-239`). That is true of the mount and not of BD-024: the workspace is where protected paths live, and the path guard's own docblock says protected paths have no container backstop (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/path-guard.ts:24-26`). WP-99's measurement, quoted from its notes: *"`pytest --basetemp=tests` (pytest clears the directory it is given …), `pytest --junitxml=tests/report.test.xml`, `go test -c -o tests/x.test` and `cargo test --target-dir tests` are all **allow**"*; every other writer measured (`cp`, `mv`, `ln`, `sed -i`, `git checkout --`, `git restore`, `git apply`, `git stash`, a redirection, `git diff --output`, `find -fprint`, `rg --pre`) is `ask`.

**What still holds and what does not.** *Holds:* a modification or deletion of a file tracked at the base that is committed and pushed is returned by the CI gate, because `changedExistingPaths` (`packages/application/src/pipeline/tamper.ts:92-101`) reads the provider's diff regardless of which tool wrote the bytes. *Does not hold:* (a) **an uncommitted effect** — `--basetemp=tests` empties the run's own `tests/`, so the run's later test commands execute fewer tests than the branch carries, and nothing records it; the gate never sees a write that is not committed; (b) **an artefact under a protected path that is committed reads as an addition** — `tests/report.test.xml`, a `go test -c` binary or a cargo target tree under `tests/` passes the gate by policy (BD-024 §2 as amended excuses additions), so the only check left is a human reading the diff at Code review; (c) the guard's steering — the agent gets no BD-024 reason, so it is not told it did anything.

**What it costs to leave.** Mostly a wasted round: a model that deletes a test directory and commits the result is returned by `ci_gate` and spends a `ci_fix` loop. The uncommitted case (a) can put wrong local evidence in front of a Reviewer or Acceptance Tester that runs the suite in its own workspace. **Needs measurement:** whether any verdict or artifact the pipeline stores relies on a test run made inside the workspace rather than on the provider's CI (BD-024 says CI is the only green; if nothing relies on it, (a) costs only the run's own confusion).

**Not filed separately, stated.** The *repository-content* route (`make *`, `npm run *`, `pnpm test`, a `conftest.py`, lockfile lifecycle scripts running whatever the tree says after the agent edits it, including an `ln -s` the guard cannot see) is BD-025's accepted residual (`command-policy.ts:217-224`) and is not a new finding.

**Done.** (a) `HAZARDOUS_ARGUMENTS` floors the four flags at `ask` in every spelling the CLIs accept (`--basetemp=x`/`--basetemp x`, `--junitxml`/`--junit-xml`, `go test -c -o`/`-o=`, `cargo test --target-dir`/`--target-dir=`), either always or only when the argument names a path matching a protected pattern — the second needs the planner to hand the protected patterns to the policy, which the domain evaluator does not take today, so **always** is the smaller change and the over-block is stated at the entry as `make … V=1`'s is; (b) the docblock at `command-policy.ts:234-239` stops calling the three *"contained"* and says what the mount does not contain; (c) one `command-policy.test.ts` case per spelling, and a canary that removes the floor fails by name; (d) technical/04's WP-99 amendment sentence *"Some verbs … write a protected path without an `ask`"* is narrowed to the repository-content route. The docblock's own warning applies: this is an enumeration and can be incomplete. **Depends on** WP-99 (landed uncommitted at the time of filing). Related: **279**, **282**, **283**.

### 282. **`.git/` is neither protected nor flagged, so a run's `Write` to `.git/config` is allowed, and a `core.fsmonitor` set there turns the read-only `git status` into an arbitrary command outside the command policy** (**RESOLVED** at `505251e`, WP-104, session 10 — TODO, **small — pre-existing, not a protected-path question**: the effect stays inside the run container, bounded by its non-root user, workspace mount and egress allow-list, the same boundary as BD-025's accepted repository-content residual; **live** on every run that holds `Write`/`Edit` (the Developer's stages) since WP-12; **a hypothesis for the run container — read off the tree by WP-99, not measured there**: the analogous firing was **measured** by WP-75 in the export helper; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (nearest is a successor of WP-99, which owns the guard); found by WP-99, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-104** — `.git` segments denied at the guard, `core.fsmonitor=false` in the run's git environment, and the daemon measurement as a criterion.**

**What is wrong.** The guard's only flagged list is `['.agentic/**', '.claude/**', 'CLAUDE.md']` (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/path-guard.ts:55`), the default protected list has no `.git` entry (`packages/domain/src/config/effective-config.ts:108-123`), and `guardWritePath` allows any in-workspace path neither list matches (`path-guard.ts:327`). `git status` and `git status *` are on the read-only allow list (`packages/domain/src/policies/command-policy.ts:178-179`), which every baseline inherits; `git config` is on no allow list, so the Bash route to the same setting is `ask` — the Write tool is the side door. WP-99's note: *"A `Write` to `.git/config` (a `core.fsmonitor`, a `core.hooksPath`) is allowed by the guard, and `git status`, an allowed read-only verb, would then run the configured command."* The export helper's docblock records the measurement that makes this more than theory, on Docker 29.7.2 with `alpine/git:v2.49.1`: *"a repository-level `core.fsmonitor` and `filter.<x>.clean` ran under `git status`/`git add`"* (`packages/infrastructure/src/workspace/provider.ts:173-176`).

**What a run can do with it.** Run a command the block list refuses (`docker *`, `curl * | sh`, …) or the ask list would put in front of a human, with the transcript showing only `git status`; set `core.hooksPath` at a tracked file that is already executable, since Edit keeps its mode (the Write tool cannot create an executable file); and redirect its own `git push` with `url.*.insteadOf`/`pushurl`, which the egress allow-list bounds. **What still holds:** the push that leaves through the export helper reads *no* configuration the run wrote, because that script deletes and replaces `.git/config` and pins `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` (`provider.ts:182-190`, WP-75); and the file is never committed, so the tamper gate is not the relevant check. Whether a repository-level `credential.helper` gets the run credential adds nothing, since the agent can already run the helper directly (backlog **277**).

**What it costs to leave.** A command-policy bypass that needs no project-declared verb and no `ask`, audited as a read. Bounded by the container, so the cost is the audit's honesty rather than an escape.

**Done.** `guardWritePath` denies a write whose folded relative path is `.git`, is under `.git/`, or has a `.git` segment anywhere (a nested repository's config), with a reason that says git's configuration is not repository content; unit cases for `.git/config`, `.GIT/config` under the fold and `sub/.git/hooks/x`; technical/04's path-guard row names it. Optionally (the WP-75 docblock's argument against enumerating `-c` overrides applies) the run container's git also gets `core.fsmonitor=false` through the reserved `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment (`provider.ts:129-136`). **Needs measurement:** one fake-free check that a `core.fsmonitor` written by the run fires under `git status` in `platform-runtime`, which turns the hypothesis into a measurement. **Depends on** nothing. Related: **281**, **283**.

**Measured at WP-104 (2026-09-30), before and after the fix, Docker Engine 29.8.1 (API 1.56), `platform-runtime:dev` `sha256:69d5cc42673e6e8d42b04a14ee1d6d71d60c199fcd59a4e1996991f08af691ed`, git 2.47.3.** Method: `docker run --rm --user 1000:1000 --network none` of the image with **exactly** the environment `platformEnvironment()` returns from the repository's sources (plus `HOME=/tmp`) — that object is the `claude` process's whole environment in a run container, because the SDK spawns with `Options.env` verbatim and the shim replaces its child's environment. In the container: `git init`, one commit, an untracked file, then the line a `Write` would append to `.git/config` — `[core] fsmonitor = "echo FIRED >/tmp/fsmonitor-fired; true"` — then `git status --short`. **Before** (six keys, no `GIT_CONFIG_*`): `RESULT: fsmonitor FIRED` (git also printed `warning: Empty last update token.`, the hook's reply). **After** (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.fsmonitor`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false`): `RESULT: fsmonitor did not fire`, `?? f.txt` printed in both. The hypothesis is a measurement for git run directly with the CLI's environment; git started **by the real CLI's Bash tool** was not run (no model credential), so that the tool passes its environment to its children is read, not measured.

### 283. **A tracked directory symlink that points into a protected tree (`link → tests/`) makes `link/x` a write into `tests/` that matches no protected pattern, so the guard allows it — including an overwrite of an existing protected file** (**RESOLVED** at `505251e`, WP-104, session 10 — TODO, **small — latent with a named trigger**: a repository that tracks a directory symlink into a protected tree; **predates WP-99** (the guard has never followed symlinks); **read off the tree, not measured**; the CI gate catches a committed overwrite, because git records it under the real path; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (the natural owner is a successor of WP-99, whose listing already carries the data); found by WP-99, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-104** — a write at or under an `opaque` entry is judged a write to an existing protected path.**

**What is wrong.** Since WP-99 the listing records every tracked symlink and submodule as `opaque`, and `protectedPathExistence` treats a target at or under one as existing (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/path-guard.ts:240-249`). But that check runs only **inside** the branch taken when a protected pattern already matches the target (`path-guard.ts:296-298`); `link/conftest.py` matches no pattern, so it falls through to `allow` (`path-guard.ts:327`) and the write lands on `tests/conftest.py`. The module docblock states the general limit (*"it does not follow symlinks"*, `path-guard.ts:19-22`). WP-99's note: *"The listing now knows every tracked symlink, so a follow-up could count any write through one as protected."*

**What it costs to leave.** A modification of an existing protected file with no BD-024 reason at write time. If committed, `changedExistingPaths` sees `tests/conftest.py` modified and returns the task; if not committed, it changes only the run's own tests (backlog **281** (a)'s cost).

**Done.** A write whose path lies at or under an `opaque` entry is judged as a write to an existing protected path — denied unless a planned pattern matches it — whether or not a protected pattern matches the spelled path; under an `unlisted` listing nothing changes (every protected path already counts as existing, and an unprotected spelling through an unknown link stays invisible, stated). Unit case: `link/conftest.py` with `link` opaque is denied; a canary that restores the pattern-first order fails by name. technical/04's WP-99 amendment gets the sentence. **Depends on** WP-99. Related: **281**, **282**.

> **M6 (architect, session 9): done at `68ecbec` — Q110 implemented per recommendation (a); product/19 §2 says migrations are blocked like the rest.**

### 285. **`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` is set on the run container, but the run shim replaces the child's environment and `platformEnvironment` does not carry it, so the `claude` process never sees it** (**RESOLVED** at `505251e`, WP-104, session 10 — nit, TODO — **a false comment plus a one-line gap, not a leak**: whatever the CLI tries to reach is still refused by the egress sidecar, or has no route at all, so the cost is noise, not traffic; **live** on every containerised run since WP-14; **read off the tree and unit-tested, not measured in the image**; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (the host measurement is already **WP-33**'s via `docs/TODO.md`; no M5 row edits `platformEnvironment`); found by WP-82, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-104** — `platformEnvironment` carries the variable.**

**What is wrong.** The container gets the variable (`packages/infrastructure/src/workspace/provider.ts:1179`, under the comment *"telemetry hosts blocked, and the CLI told not to try"* at `:1178`). But the shim starts the CLI with `env: { ...frame.env }` (`packages/infrastructure/src/runlet/shim.ts:422`, commented *"`env` replaces, never merges"*), and `packages/infrastructure/src/runlet/shim.test.ts:209-222` asserts that a variable in the shim's own environment does not reach the child. The spawn environment the frame carries comes from `platformEnvironment` (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/options.ts:22-31`). It sets `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` and `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING`, and not this variable. So the comment at `provider.ts:1178` is false about the process. technical/05:21 was already corrected at WP-82 and says so, citing *"backlog, WP-82's discovered work"* with no number (this entry). Backlog **137**'s *What is wrong* (1) still says nothing sets the opt-outs. The replacement text is in the WP-82 notes and is the orchestrator's to apply.

**What it costs to leave.** Close to nothing on the network. The run's network is `internal: true`, and the only way out is the sidecar's default-deny filter (`packages/infrastructure/src/workspace/egress.ts:1-8`). A spec with no egress host gets no sidecar at all (`provider.ts:1102-1105`). The three opt-outs that do reach the process already cover telemetry, error reporting and the updater. What remains is whatever else the variable suppresses in the pinned `claude 2.1.267`, which nobody has measured. Each such attempt ends as a `403` line in the sidecar log. *(Corrected at WP-118: before WP-118 no attempt reached the sidecar at all — the CLI had no proxy variable, because the container's `HTTPS_PROXY` stopped at the shim like this one did; measured, a real `claude` retried its first request for a minute and the sidecar logged nothing (backlog **342**). Since WP-118 the CLI's traffic does reach the sidecar, so the sentence that follows describes the tree from WP-118 on.)* That pollutes the diagnostic technical/05:21 promises (*"denied hosts shown in the run detail as a hint"*): an operator looking for the host a failed run really needed has to read past hosts the CLI should never have tried.

**Done.** `platformEnvironment` carries `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC: '1'`, and an `options.test.ts` case asserts it is in the spawn environment and survives a `RunSpec.env` that sets it to `0`. The container-env copy is either removed or kept with its comment rewritten to say it reaches the shim and not the CLI. technical/05:21 and backlog 137 point at the fix. Whether it changes what the CLI contacts stays WP-33's measurement (`docs/TODO.md`, the backlog 137 line). The fix does not wait for it, because setting an opt-out cannot widen egress. **Depends on** nothing. Related: **137**, **127**.

### 286. **A run container whose create answer the runner never receives keeps running with no reaper: a replay after a launcher restart (measured) leaves one, and a create that outlives the client's 10-minute timeout, or a restart during a create, would leave one per start attempt (read, not measured)** (**RESOLVED** at `68906a5`, WP-103, session 10 — TODO, **small — not a major**: the orphan holds **no live credential with no bound** and spends no model money, because nothing ever attaches to it; what it holds is a container, a sidecar, a network, a workspace volume retention cannot reclaim and a control directory the sweep keeps as `run_alive`; **latent with named triggers**: a launcher restart while a create is in flight (`docker compose up --build` or `restart: unless-stopped` during runs), or a create slower than `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, such as a first mirror fetch of a large repository; the replay outcome is **measured**, the other two producers and the retry's behaviour are **read off the tree, not measured**; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (**WP-86** folds **138**'s `run_alive` count, which would make an orphan *visible*; no M5 row reaps one, and reaping needs a reader of `runs` the launcher is refused by TD-021); found by WP-82, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-103**, per TD-028 decision 12 (M6 amendment): measure (a)–(c) on a daemon first, then a runner-side reaper over a new list verb.**

**What is wrong.** One cause: the launcher's only record of a run it created is its in-memory map plus the handle it returns, and nothing reconciles the containers on the daemon with the runs the platform still owns. So a container whose handle never reaches the runner has no owner. Backlog **136**'s measurement, quoted from its WP-82 addendum: *"refused at the network — `409 network with name run-<id> already exists`, `workspace_failed` to the runner … no second container started … The first run's container and sidecar kept running with no launcher holding a handle — the orphan is real and nothing bounds it"* (`scripts/launcher-control-plane-check.mjs`, Docker Engine 29.7.2 / API 1.55, `linux/arm64`). `apps/launcher/src/control-plane.ts:49-53` now says the same: *"Nothing bounds that container"*. The lease sweep ends the row, WP-77 revokes the credential, and `purgeExpired` removes only volumes.

**The report's third item, answered by reading and folded here because it is the same orphan.** *"Whether a retry reuses the run id (and meets the same 409) or creates a new run and a second container"*: it creates a new run. Every `stage.execute` attempt draws a fresh id (`packages/application/src/pipeline/stage-executor.ts:949`). A retryable start failure fails the old run and leaves the task for the re-enqueue (`stage-executor.ts:1064`, `:1703-1708`), up to `MAX_RUN_START_ATTEMPTS = 3` (`:392`). The client has no retry of its own: a transport failure or timeout becomes `engine_unavailable` (`packages/infrastructure/src/launcher/client.ts:161-168`), under `AbortSignal.timeout` with `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000` (`client.ts:83`). Two consequences follow, both **hypotheses**:
1. **The measured replay may have no production producer.** The check's runner re-sends one run id on purpose (`CHECK_PHASE=replay-create`). This reading found nothing in production that re-sends a run id.
2. **The realistic producer is a lost answer, not a replay.** Suppose the runner times out, or the launcher restarts mid-create. The provisioner's `catch` then has `created === null`, so it forgets and revokes the credential and releases nothing (`packages/infrastructure/src/launcher/provisioner.ts:277-291`). The launcher, if it is still alive, finishes the create: `control-plane.ts` has no handler for the request closing early (grep for `'close'`/`aborted`: none). The retry then builds a **second** container under a new id. A create that is slow for a structural reason (the mirror) is slow on every attempt, so a task could leave up to three orphans before it escalates. A restart during a create leaves whatever partial set of objects the dead process made, which WP-82 names as unmeasured.

**Why it is not a major.** The credential is bounded three times over. The provisioner revokes on any create failure (`provisioner.ts:290`). WP-77's recovery pass revokes a terminal run's unconfirmed mint by address. GitLab's own expiry caps it at 24–48 h (technical/05:27). The container never held the value: the credential helper asks the shim, and technical/05:27 says the runner answers *"only while the run is active"*, which an unattached orphan never is. The CLI is only started by a `spawn` frame from an authenticated runner, so an orphan spends nothing. The shim's handshake window (`shim.ts:639`) is armed per connection. This reading found no deadline for *no connection ever*, so an orphan appears to wait indefinitely (a reading).

**What it costs to leave.** Leaked daemon resources per occurrence: one run container, one tinyproxy sidecar and one network, plus a workspace volume `in_use`, which retention never reclaims. There is also a control directory holding a run token that the sweep keeps as `run_alive` (backlog **138**), and nothing counts it. In the timeout case this repeats per start attempt, on exactly the repositories that are slowest to clone. **Urgent if** a deployment upgrades under load, or a project's first mirror fetch nears ten minutes.

**Needs measurement:** (a) a launcher restart **during** a create: which objects exist afterwards and whether any container runs; (b) a create that outlives the client timeout with the launcher alive: whether it completes and leaves a running container, and how many a task accumulates across its three attempts; (c) whether an unattached shim ever exits. All three need a daemon (rule 66). (a) and (b) extend `launcher-control-plane-check.mjs` the way WP-82 did.

**Measured (WP-103, session 10, before the fix was chosen).** `node scripts/launcher-control-plane-check.mjs`, extended as WP-82 extended it, on Docker Desktop, Engine **29.8.1**, `linux/arm64`, against `platform-runtime:dev`; two runs on the unchanged tree (30/30 each; the second with `--observe-shim-ms 600000`), and (a) again in the post-fix run below, which the fix does not touch — the numbers identical where the runs recorded them. **(a) A launcher restart during a create**, taken the moment the run's network appeared (1.4–1.6 s into the create): `docker stop` returned after **3.16 s** (all three runs) — the launcher logged the SIGTERM and **never** logged its close resolving, so it did not wait for the in-flight create, for a reason not established — and `docker kill` after **0.11 s**. Either way the runner was told `engine_unavailable` (`fetch failed`; underneath, recorded on the third run, `UND_ERR_SOCKET other side closed`), and the daemon then held, and still held after the launcher came back: the helper the create was running (`clone-<run>` **running** after the stop; `prep-<run>` `created` or `exited` after the kill), the network `run-<run>`, the workspace volume `ws-<run>` and — after every stop, and after two of the three kills — `/ctl/<run>` (the first stop's runner read a token file in it). **No run container and no sidecar.** So the orphan this producer leaves is not a live agent but a labelled helper, and that helper is enough: `#liveRunIds` counts any container carrying the run label, so the control directory is kept `run_alive` and the volume `in use` **for ever**. **(b) A create that outlives the client's timeout, launcher alive** (the client bound shortened to 1.5 s; each attempt a new run id, because `recordUnstarted` fails the run and re-enqueues the stage — read, `stage-executor.ts`, `MAX_RUN_START_ATTEMPTS = 3`): each of the three attempts was told `engine_unavailable` at **1.50 s** (`TimeoutError`), and **all three creates completed** — the daemon settled 18 s later with **three running run containers**, three sidecars, three networks, three `egress-<run>` volumes, three workspace volumes and three control directories. So a task accumulates one full orphaned workspace per start attempt, three per task. **(c) An unattached shim** does not exit: all three (b) containers were `running` at 120 s in the first run and at **597–600 s** in the second; read, the shim's two timers (handshake, credential) are per connection, and nothing is armed on a socket nobody connects to. **After the fix** (same check, 36/36): the three (b) creates are abandoned by the launcher — three `a create request closed before its answer was written` lines, no container, network or control directory left, the workspace volume kept for retention; the restarted launcher's `GET /v1/runs` lists the two (a) runs and the 136 replay's live one off the daemon; the production pass removes the two terminal ones (container, network and control directory gone, volume kept) and keeps the `running` one; a second pass with no row and a zero unknown-grace removes it with its sidecar, network and control directory. Written into technical/05's WP-103 amendment, `apps/launcher/src/control-plane.ts`, `packages/application/src/recovery/orphan-workspaces.ts` and `docs/TODO.md`; TD-028 and `CLAUDE.md` are the orchestrator's (texts in the WP-103 notes).

**Done.** A reaper that does not give the launcher a database. The recommended shape: a runner-side recovery row (the runner reads `runs`) asks the launcher, through a new control-plane verb, for the run ids of the containers it labels. It then ends, by run id, every one whose run is terminal or unknown and older than a stated grace, one attempt per id, and counts what it reaped. That needs a TD-028 amendment, because it adds a verb to decision 2's surface. Separately, the launcher abandons a create whose request closed before the response, or its docblock says why not. Both directions asserted: an orphan for a terminal run is removed, and a live run's container is kept (the negative). technical/05's WP-53 amendment, `control-plane.ts:49-54`, TD-028's second WP-53 amendment and `CLAUDE.md`'s WP-53 bullet state the bound in the same edit (rule 83). The last two sentences are already drafted in the WP-82 notes. **Depends on** WP-53 (the control plane), WP-77 (the recovery-row pattern), WP-86 (the `run_alive` count that makes the before/after countable). Related: **136**, **138**, **135**, **155**.

### 287. **The run transcript's `system · init` row lists the CLI's fifteen bundled skills beside `agentic:kb`, although the run can neither see nor invoke them** **RESOLVED** at `6247b41`, WP-117, session 11 — (nit, TODO — **a display that can be misread, not a leak and not a cost**: the model's own listing carries only the allowed skill and the tool refuses the rest, both **measured** by WP-83; **live** on every run since WP-83 sends `skills` always; the fifteen are **measured** (pinned CLI `claude` 2.1.267, SDK 0.3.267, 2026-09-28); whether anything reads the field as an allow-list is **read off the tree** — nothing does today; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (WP-95 is the nearest row if the run screen should label it; a documentation sentence alone would close it); found by WP-83, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-117** — option (a), the documentation sentence; no normaliser change.**

**What is wrong.** The normaliser copies the CLI's init message into the transcript verbatim, `skills: message.skills` included (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/transcript-normaliser.ts:256-273`), and the run screen renders a `system` row as raw JSON under the label `system · <subtype>` (`apps/web/src/transcript/view.tsx:157-161`). WP-83's note, quoted: *"With `skills: ['agentic:kb']` the CLI's `system`/`init` still lists fifteen bundled skills (`deep-research`, `update-config`, `run`, …) beside `agentic:kb`, while the model's own listing carries only `agentic:kb` and the tool refuses the rest"*; the refusal sentence it measured is *"Skill update-config is not in this session's skills allowlist"*, and with `skills: []` both the bundled and the platform skill are refused (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/options.ts:181-202` records the three cases).

**The report's questions, answered.** *Context tokens:* none on the evidence — the measured request to the Messages API stand-in listed only `agentic:kb`, so the fifteen are not in the model's context. *Invocation:* refused by the CLI's allow-list when `skills` is sent, which it now always is. So the row is the CLI's own inventory, stored truthfully as the CLI's message; the only error available is a reader (an operator on the run screen, or a future feature) taking it for *what this run could use*. That is why this is a nit and not rule 16's *wrong number as a fact*: the platform presents it as a raw CLI message, not as its own claim.

**What it costs to leave.** An operator reviewing a run may believe it had `update-config` or `deep-research` available. A future reader built on the init row (an audit panel, a per-run capability summary) would overstate the run's reach.

**Done.** Either (a) technical/04's transcript section and the user guide's run-screen section say the init row's `skills` is the CLI's inventory and the allow-list is `Options.skills` (the planner's `SKILLS_BY_ROLE` row), or (b) the normaliser records `skills_allowed` beside the CLI's list from the spec, and the run screen shows that; a unit case for (b). **Depends on** nothing. Related: **149** (resolved by WP-83).

### 288. **The Jira marker search reads only the oldest hundred comments, so on a ticket that already had a hundred comments when the workpad was first written, every later `upsertWorkpad` posts another workpad, and a retried marked question or lint report is posted twice** **RESOLVED** at `9a9225f`, WP-111, session 11 — (TODO, **small — latent with a named trigger**: a Jira ticket with ≥ 100 comments at the moment its first workpad, question or lint comment is written (a ticket that crosses a hundred *after* the workpad was written is unaffected — the workpad stays in the oldest page); **read off the tree, not measured**; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (WP-87 is the only M5 row in the Jira adapter, but its scope is the poller); found by WP-83, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-111** — page by `startAt` to `total` under a bound, and fail at the bound rather than answer `null`.**

**What is wrong.** `findMarkedComment` asks for one page, `{ size: MARKER_SEARCH_PAGE, orderBy: 'created' }` with `MARKER_SEARCH_PAGE = 100` (`packages/integrations/src/providers/jira-cloud/index.ts:151-157`, `:437-452`), and never follows `startAt`, although the page schema parses `startAt` and `total` (`packages/integrations/src/providers/jira-cloud/mapping.ts:113-118`). The constant's docblock justifies the oldest page by *"The workpad is written early in a ticket's life"* (`index.ts:154-156`), which is an assumption about the ticket, not a bound. Two callers: `upsertWorkpad` (`index.ts:631-641`), which POSTs a new comment whenever the search returns `null`, and `addComment` with a marker (`index.ts:677-690`), whose docblock says *"posting it twice notifies twice"*. WP-83's note: *"A workpad written after a ticket already had a hundred comments is not found again, and `upsertWorkpad` would post a second one. Read off the tree, not measured."*

**What it costs to leave.** The workpad job runs on `task.stage.entered` and `task.stage.returned` (`packages/application/src/pipeline/workpad.ts:77-78`), so on an affected ticket the cost is **one new workpad comment per stage transition**, not one duplicate — each one a notification to every watcher, and each new one also outside the oldest hundred. A marked question retried after a failed call notifies twice. Bounded by how rare a hundred-comment ticket is at intake; a long-lived or imported ticket is the likely producer.

**Needs measurement:** whether Jira Cloud honours `maxResults=100` on this endpoint or caps it lower (a lower cap moves the trigger down to that number). The replay honours `orderBy`/`maxResults` since WP-83, so the defect itself is reproducible in the contract tier without a live site.

**Done.** The search pages by `startAt` until it finds the marker or reaches `total`, under a stated page bound; a search that hits the bound without reaching `total` **fails** (rule 20) rather than returning `null`, because `null` is the direction that posts. Alternatively `upsertWorkpad` first tries the comment id the platform already stored in `tasks.workpad_ref` — that needs the port to carry it, which is a port change. A Jira replay case with 150 comments and the workpad at position 120 finds and PUTs it; a canary that restores the single page fails by name. **Depends on** nothing. Related: **290** (the same single-page read on the snapshot side).

### 289. **`get_task_context`'s `artifacts` section still answers the latest verdict of each type, so a stage WP-83 shows only the verdict that caused its return can pull the earlier verdict back through the tool, unmarked as stale** (**RESOLVED** at `41158cb`, WP-105, session 11 — nit, TODO — **a different surface, not a contradiction of the ruling as written, and not a wrong number**: the answer is labelled `latest_per_type` with each artifact's version, which is true; what it lacks is the cause link WP-83 added to the pack; **live** for every role holding `get_task_context` — the Developer, Reviewer and Acceptance Tester included (`packages/application/src/pipeline/planner.ts:93-111`); **stated by the implementer as a residual**, read off the tree; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (the ruling's scope is the orchestrator's to state, rule 83); found by WP-83, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-105** — option (b): the `feedback` section carries each return's `cause`; the tool keeps the history.**
> **WP-105 (session 11, in the working tree for review):** each return carries `cause` — `verdict` (type and version, by WP-83's `runs.task_stage_id` link), `gate`, or `other` (a person's return or rework, the dependency policy or the review window's threads, which the row does not tell apart). `returnCauseOf` in `apps/server/src/queries/task-context-queries.ts`; technical/04 says the ruling covers the pack, not the tool.

**What is wrong.** The section keeps, per `artifact_type`, the highest version (`apps/server/src/queries/task-context-queries.ts:283-323`; the table at `:29`). WP-83's ruling (the plan row) is *"a returned stage is shown **only** the verdict that caused the return … Earlier verdicts leave the pack, so fewer tokens and no ambiguity"*, and the implementer's residual, quoted: *"It is a tool the model calls on purpose, not the pack, so the ruling did not reach it; a model that asks is shown the old verdict, labelled with its version."* The planner's filter is `artifactsShownTo` (`planner.ts:733`), which the tool does not call.

**Why a nit.** The ruling's two reasons are tokens and ambiguity. Tokens: the model pays only when it asks. Ambiguity: partially back — after a review return then a CI return, the tool answers the old `request_changes` as the latest `ReviewVerdict`, and nothing in the tool's answer ties a verdict to a return: the artifact entries carry no timestamp, and the `feedback` section's returns (`task-context-queries.ts:325-336`) carry `at` and `reason` but not the `cause` WP-83 put on `ReturnFeedback`.

**Done.** Either (a) the orchestrator states that the ruling covers the pack and the tool is deliberately the whole history, in technical/04 beside WP-83's sentence; or (b) the `feedback` section carries each return's `cause` (artifact type and version, already on `ReturnFeedback`), so a model can tell which verdict it was sent back for, with a unit case. Hiding old verdicts from the tool is not recommended — a stage may legitimately need the history. **Depends on** WP-83. Related: **159**.

### 290. **The ticket snapshot's `comment_count` is the number of human comments on the one page read, not on the ticket, and reaches the prompt marker as a platform integer — and on a busy ticket `truncated` is not set although older comments were never read** (**RESOLVED** at `ce64e5d`, WP-83, session 9 (folded at review round 1: WP-83's 50-comment page had widened it to tickets with 51–100 comments; the port reports `comment_total`, an unstated or larger total is declared `truncated`, the marker says `human_comments_read`) — TODO, **small — a wrong number presented as a fact**: a marker attribute is text the platform wrote, never the ticket's (the assembler's rule, CLAUDE.md), so the model has no reason to doubt it; **live** on every Jira ticket with more comments than one page — more than fifty since WP-83, more than a hundred before; **pre-existing since WP-15f**, narrowed rather than caused by WP-83; the WP-83 residual is **stated**, the `truncated` half is **read off the tree by the refiner, not measured**; **no screen shows it** (grep of `apps/web/src` for `comment_count`: none), the prompt and `get_task_context`'s `ticket` section do; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (WP-87 is the only M5 row in the Jira adapter; the snapshot half is `packages/application`); found by WP-83, session 9)

**What is wrong.** `commentsOf` counts the human comments of whatever the port returned (`packages/application/src/pipeline/ticket-snapshot.ts:238-241`), the snapshot stores that as `comment_count` (`:278`), and `truncated` is set only when `total > comments.length` among them (`:276`). The Jira adapter's port answer is the newest fifty (`READ_TICKET_COMMENT_PAGE`, `packages/integrations/src/providers/jira-cloud/index.ts:186`). The assembler writes the count into the ticket block's marker (`packages/domain/src/prompt/assembly.ts:716-720`), and `get_task_context` serves the snapshot as stored (`apps/server/src/queries/task-context-queries.ts:275-281`). The schema's docblock says *"`comment_count` is what the provider returned before the window, so `comments.length < comment_count` says how many"* (`packages/contracts/src/common.ts:718-720`) — true of the page, and read by any consumer as the ticket. WP-83's residual, quoted: *"the snapshot's `comment_count` counts the human comments on the page read (≤ 50), not on the ticket; a ticket with more than thirty platform comments among its newest fifty shows fewer than twenty human ones."*

**The sharper half (refiner, read not measured).** On a 300-comment ticket whose newest fifty hold twelve human comments, the marker reads `comments=12 comment_count=12` with **no** `truncated` — a positive claim that nothing was dropped, while 250 comments were never read. The provider's own `total` is parsed (`packages/integrations/src/providers/jira-cloud/mapping.ts:117`) and discarded before the port.

**What it costs to leave.** A model told it has the whole thread reasons from part of it — a decision recorded in an older comment reads as never made. Rule 16's direction: a wrong count is worse than an absent one.

**Done.** The `Ticket` port carries the provider's comment total, or `null` where the provider does not say; the snapshot sets `truncated` when the page was not the whole thread, and `comment_count` is either redefined in the schema and technical/03 as *human comments read* or joined by a separate total (a wire change, so `schemas/` regenerates). A unit case with a 300-comment total and a 50-comment page asserts `truncated`, and the Jira replay case asserts the total reaches the port. **Depends on** nothing. Related: **288**, Q54 (answered by WP-83).

### 291. **A reminder timer is armed only by the `pipeline.deadlines` handler's `afterCommit`, and nothing else ever arms one: a lost arm is never recovered, the pre-WP-56 backfill arms only the expiry, and every question or approval already open when WP-84 deploys gets no reminder** (**RESOLVED** at `9a46a63`, WP-108, session 11 — TODO, **small — one missed message per occurrence, never a stranded task**: the expiry is still recovered, so the task still escalates on time. What is lost is BD-006's *"with a reminder before escalation"* for that row. **Live**, with three producers: (a) a lost arm (a process death after the dispatch commits, or an enqueue that throws); (b) the backfill of an undated row; (c) a one-off at WP-84's deploy. (a) and (b) are **stated by the implementer as residuals**; (c) is **read off the tree by the refiner, not measured**; **unowned — for the orchestrator** (no M5 row owns `recovery/deadline.ts`; the natural owner is a successor of WP-84); found by WP-84, session 9)
> **M6 (architect, session 9): folded into **WP-108** — a fourth `recovery/deadline.ts` row; a backfilled row past its reminder time is reminded on the next pass.**

**What is wrong.** One cause: the only code that enqueues a `question_reminder` or `approval_reminder` is the handler. It arms both through `context.afterCommit` (`packages/application/src/pipeline/deadlines.ts:191-202`, `:217-221`, `:237-241`), on `task.question.asked` and `task.approval.requested` only (`:187`). `afterCommit` is at-most-once (TD-004). The recovery row knows only the expiry kinds: `dataOf` maps a waiting row to `question_timeout` or `approval_timeout` and nothing else (`packages/application/src/recovery/deadline.ts:110-112`), and the backfill enqueues exactly that (`:187`). The residual, quoted from `packages/application/src/pipeline/reminders.ts:44-45`: *"A reminder timer whose arming was lost is not recovered: `recovery/deadline.ts` recovers the **expiry** (the loss that strands a task), and a lost reminder costs one message."* technical/02:206 says the same.

**The third producer (refiner, read not measured).** Take a question asked, or an approval requested, before WP-84's deploy that is still open after it. Its `pipeline.deadlines` dispatch already ran, arming only the expiry. Nothing re-dispatches it and nothing sweeps for it, so it escalates at its deadline with no reminder. With the default one-working-day timeout this lasts a day after the upgrade and then clears.

**What it costs to leave.** A human who missed the first notification hears nothing more until the escalation. That is the pre-WP-84 behaviour, for the affected rows only. The user guide says without qualification that a question gets *"one reminder"* (`docs/user-guide.md:425-428`).

**Done.** A fourth row in `recovery/deadline.ts`'s table. It finds an open question or pending approval with `reminders_sent = 0` whose `reminderTimeOf` passed more than the grace ago and whose deadline has not, and calls `remindWaitingAggregate`. That call already re-validates, its notification collapses on the name-derived cause id (`reminders.ts:69-70`), and the count moves the row out of the query, so the row needs no attempt mark (the same argument as the expiry rows, `deadline.ts:29-34`). **Needs a decision on the backfill:** `reminderTimeOf(asked_at, deadline)` for an old row with a deadline counted from now may already be in the past. Either the reminder fires on the next pass, or it is counted from the backfill instant, as the deadline is (`deadline.ts:17-22`). Cases: a lost reminder arm is found and reminded once; a row past its deadline is not reminded; a canary with the row removed fails by name. The `reminders.ts:44-45` residual and technical/02:206 are corrected in the same change (rule 83). **Depends on** WP-84. Related: **161**, **162**, **165**.

### 292. **A `question` notification is never re-checked against its question, so a retry or the WP-84 re-post can post *"… is waiting for an answer"* for a question already answered or expired; a re-posted `reminder` has the same gap for the same reason** (**RESOLVED** at `d5f7f05`, WP-84, session 9 (folded at review round 1: every question, reminder and approval notification records its aggregate and is re-checked before every send, the digest included; a settled one is closed `withheld`) — TODO, **small — a user-visible stale message, not a wrong state**. First answer wins in the aggregate, and a late reply in chat is refused (below), so nothing is answered twice. The cost is one stale line per affected question. **Live, with a named trigger**: the first post fails (a chat outage), and the question is answered or expires before a later retry or the re-post. The window was the job's own retries since WP-65 review round 1 (≈ 48 min). WP-84 widens it: the recovery pass re-posts once past that window. The question half is **stated by the implementer**, the reminder half is **stated as a residual**, and the human's view is **read off the tree by the refiner, not measured**. **Owner: foldable into WP-84 now** (see *Done*); otherwise **WP-88**, which folds **233** (an answered question's message is never edited) and posts questions through `postQuestion`; found by WP-84, session 9)

**What is wrong.** One cause: the notification row names which approval it is about (`approval_id`) and nothing else, and the duty re-checks only what the payload names. The `notify` duty drops an `approval` wake-up whose approval is no longer pending (`packages/application/src/notify/duty.ts:102-117`). It drops a `reminder` wake-up whose aggregate is settled **only when `reminder_of` is present** (`:120-139`). There is no check at all for the `question` class. The payload carries no question id: the handler builds it from `task.question.asked` with the text as detail (`packages/application/src/notify/handlers.ts:126-132`), and `PipelineOutboundData` has `approval_id` and `reminder_of` but no question field (`packages/application/src/pipeline/jobs.ts:307-313`). Both late paths post the recorded row's own text. The retry reads the row back and posts its stored title, detail and URL (`duty.ts:233-262`). The re-post rebuilds the wake-up from a row that carries `approvalId` only (`packages/application/src/recovery/notification-repost.ts:56-66`), and it fires past `IMMEDIATE_UNDELIVERED_AFTER_MS` (`packages/application/src/notify/undelivered.ts:36`), which is `(60 + 120 + 3 × 900) s` = 48 min (`undelivered.test.ts:18`). The implementer's residual on the reminder half, quoted from `notification-repost.ts:46-48`: *"the row does not record which aggregate it reminded about, so the rebuilt payload carries no `reminder_of`. A reminder re-posted after its question was answered is one stale line, at most once."*

**What a human sees (refiner, read not measured).** In the task's thread, after the answer: the title *"`<task>` is waiting for an answer"* (`packages/application/src/notify/render.ts:133`) and the question's text. For an expired question the task is by then `needs_human`, so the message contradicts the escalation above it. A human who replies through a Slack decision is refused `already_decided` (`packages/application/src/integrations/inbound-decisions.ts:129-130`). That refusal is recorded only in `inbox.error`, which no screen shows (`packages/integrations/src/providers/slack/setup-guide.md:143`). So the person who answers is silently ignored. A typed thread reply is not matched to its task on this build at all (`docs/user-guide.md:420-421`, WP-88's 195). A reminder re-posted this way (*"Still unanswered: …"*, `reminders.ts:134`) is the same kind of stale line.

**Should WP-84 fold it? Recommended yes.** WP-84 introduced the late path, and migration 0059 is still untracked, so a column can join it rather than needing a migration of its own (TD-011 forbids editing only an *applied* migration). The fix mirrors `duty.ts:102-117`. If it is not folded, it waits for WP-88, and then it needs a new migration.

**Done.** The notification row records the waiting aggregate it is about, for the `question` class and the `reminder` class both. Either a nullable `question_id` beside `approval_id`, with the reminder's aggregate recorded separately so the settled-approval edit still cannot pick a reminder up (technical/02:213), or one `(subject_aggregate, subject_id)` pair. The `notify` payload carries it from the handler, and the re-post rebuild carries it from the row. The duty skips a `question` or `reminder` whose question is no longer `open` (or approval no longer `pending`). The skip stays counted by the gauge, as `notification-repost.ts:42-45` already states for approvals. Cases each way: a question answered between the first failed post and the retry gets no second post; one still open is posted; a re-posted reminder for an answered question posts nothing; a canary with the guard removed fails by name. technical/03's notifications row is amended in the same change. **Depends on** WP-84 (the re-post row, migration 0059). Related: **233**, **236**, **195**.
