**Not done here, on purpose** (other work packages own the files): `assembly.ts` still writes *"in the language of the ticket you were given"* into discovery's system prompt — the role prompt answers it, but the sentence should not be there for a ticketless stage; the platform-written environment fact block is another agent's; the read-verb and unattended-ask fixes are others'.)

### 471. **Two `StructuredOutput` rejections regenerated ~47 KB of model output: discovery sent `documents` as a JSON string, and an architect run merged a `Skill` call's `{skill, args}` into its plan; and every ResearchReport/TicketBreakdown schema carried a `maxLength` beside a `$ref`** **RESOLVED** at `bf019928`, first local test (2026-10-05/06) — (TODO, **minor — cost and latency, no lost artifact**.

**Root causes, measured off `run_messages`.** (1) Discovery `fc3be57d`, seq 434–436: the first call (21 383 bytes) had `commands` as an array and `documents` as a **string** holding the JSON array — the CLI answered *"/documents: must be array"* and the model resent the whole draft (20 484 bytes, seq 445). The schema is not the cause: `documents` is a plain `{"type": "array"}` with object items. It is a model serialisation slip on a large nested parameter of escaped Markdown; the platform's share is that nothing told the model the lists' types and that pages ran long. (2) Architect `c2e26022`, seq 593–595: the plan's input carried `skill: "architecture"` and `args: {}` beside its sixteen fields — a `Skill` tool call's input merged into the `StructuredOutput` call (there is no `architecture` skill); the CLI refused both keys and the model resent (seq 597). A model slip; no platform text names that skill. (3) The CLI's ajv strict-mode warning *"missing type "string" for keyword "maxLength""*: `@platform/contracts` registers its value objects in zod's global registry, so zod hoists them into `$defs` regardless of `reused: 'inline'`, and a check on top of one (`nonEmptyStringSchema.max(200)`) is emitted as `{"$ref": "#/$defs/NonEmptyString", "maxLength": 200}` — seven such nodes in ResearchReport and two in TicketBreakdown, none in DiscoveryDraft.

**What was built.** `artifactJsonSchema` (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/structured-output.ts`) now inlines every definition (`inlineDefinitions`): no `$ref`, no `$defs`, sibling keywords merged with the stricter bound winning; the published `schemas/` keep their `$defs`. `structured-output.test.ts` asserts, for every artifact type, no `$ref`/`$defs` and no `maxLength`/`minLength`/`pattern`/`format`/`maxItems`/`minItems` without a type, and equality with zod's own inlining under an empty registry (so nothing was lost); the merge is `structured-output.test.ts` › "keeps the stricter bound when a $ref and its sibling both set one". The discovery prompt's *Handing in the draft* (backlog 470) states the lists are arrays of objects, never JSON strings, and keeps pages short because a refused draft is resent in full.

**Not done here.** (2) belongs to every role, so the one sentence that would answer it — *"`StructuredOutput` takes exactly the artifact's fields, never another tool's input"* — is the platform prompt's (`assembly.ts`, another agent's file). Coercing a stringified list back into an array is not possible platform-side: the CLI validates and refuses before the platform sees the call, and a `PreToolUse` rewrite would be in `hooks.ts` (another agent's file) and would widen what the model may send.)

### 480. **Every unattended `ask` was denied with a reason that read as "no network", and nothing the PostToolUse hook did reached the model for a built-in tool** **RESOLVED** at `ac082e1c`, first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **major — the product owner: *"it always runs in automode because of unattended … we will never wait for permissions so it runs in sandbox/automode"***; the design was the orchestrator's). Three defects in the same files: (1) a command-policy `ask` reached `canUseTool`, whose unattended port denied it with *"this instance cannot ask a human for approval yet (no Question surface is bound to a live run)"* — the discovery run read that as *"no network"* and wrote it into its knowledge pages (backlog 470); (2) the PostToolUse cap applied to every tool, so an `Edit`'s serialised response (`originalFile` included) logged 37 false *truncated* rows in one run and a `Read` logged *"45863 to 10000"* while the model read the whole file; (3) see *Measured*.

**Decided and built — BD-025's 2026-10-06 amendment** (technical/04 hook table and `canUseTool`, technical/05 *Command and tool policy* and *Git guards*, technical/12, product/19 §3 amended).
- **`commands.unattended: auto | deny`** in `commandPolicySchema` (organisation settings, project settings, `.agentic/config.yml`; `schemas/` regenerated), default `auto`. `deny` from any layer wins (`unattendedCommandModeOf`): `runCommandPolicy` returns it, both planners write it to the now-required `RunSpec.commandPolicy.unattended`, the effective configuration publishes it with its source, and a repository file's `auto` over a `deny` setting is reported in `not_applied` (`tightenUnattended`).
- **`decideUnattendedCommand`** (`packages/domain/src/policies/unattended-commands.ts`) is what the `PreToolUse(Bash)` hook now calls; it answers `allow` or `deny`, never `ask`. Block, an uncertain line (rule 5 not weakened) and a `command`/`trust` hazard are `deny` in both modes — every `HAZARDOUS_ARGUMENTS` entry now carries a `kind`; a `path` hazard (`--junitxml`, `-coverprofile`) runs under `auto`. An `ask` (ask-list match, unmatched fragment, redirection to a path) runs under `auto` with a `hook` row *`unattended: ask allowed in the sandbox (matched "<entry>" | no list matches it | a redirection writes <path>)`* and is refused under `deny`.
- **The git boundary** (`gitBoundaryViolation`), `deny` in both modes **and over the allow list** (so `git fetch https://…`, which `git fetch *` allowed, is now refused): a push other than `git push [-u] origin agentic/<branch>…` with literal names (no bare push, `HEAD`, `src:dst`, tags/all/mirror/follow-tags, `-o`/`--push-option` — `ci.skip` —, lease, `--repo` elsewhere); fetch/pull/`ls-remote` to a URL or another remote, `--multiple`, `--recurse-submodules`; `clone` of a non-local source or with `--template`, a guarded `-c`, `--recurse-submodules`; `git remote add|set-url|rename`; `git config` **writing** `remote.*`, `url.*`, `credential*`, `http.*`, `protocol.*`, `include*`, `alias.*`, `push.*`, `submodule.*`, `core.sshCommand|gitProxy|askPass|fsmonitor|hooksPath`, `branch.*.remote|pushRemote|merge`, or `--edit`; the same keys through `git -c`/`--config-env` and `GIT_CONFIG_*`, `GIT_SSH*`, `GIT_ASKPASS`, `SSH_ASKPASS`, `GIT_PROXY_COMMAND`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH`, `GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`; `--exec-path=`, `--git-dir`/`--work-tree` on a remote verb; `git credential*`, remote plumbing (`send-pack`, `fetch-pack`, `remote-*`, …), `archive --remote`, `submodule` beyond `status`/`summary`; anything naming `/ctl` or `agentic-runlet` (matched on the raw line, so inside a quoted script too); `.git`, `~/.gitconfig` or `.git-credentials` written by a redirection or named by a non-read verb; and a computed command name (`$X …`, `$(…) …`, a quote-aware walk that skips here-document bodies). Every fragment the scanner yields is judged through every argv candidate (`commandArgvCandidates`: `env`, `nice`, assignments, `xargs`, `sh -c`, `eval`, quoting, `/usr/bin/git`, `git-<verb>` binaries).
- **Denial text.** Every deny reads `command policy: block — …` (a block, which `VERIFICATION_PROMPT` names) or `command policy: refused (unattended run) — …`, names the command or fragment and the rule, and ends with `UNATTENDED_ALTERNATIVES`: *"This is the platform's command policy, not a network or sandbox failure. To read a file use the Read tool (with offset/limit for a range); to search use Grep or Glob; if only one part of a compound line was refused, run the other parts one command per call."* The `canUseTool` port's text for the CLI's own non-Bash questions is replaced the same way (`UNATTENDED_APPROVAL_DENIAL`). No prompt line was added (`assembly.ts` is another agent's file); the denial is where the model learns the rule.
- **PostToolUse** caps `Bash` (stdout and stderr together, stderr at most half when both are long) and MCP tools (the platform's at `PLATFORM_TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS`, backlog 464) and **never** `Read`/`Edit`/`Write`/`Glob`/`Grep`; it redacts every tool's output, and the redaction path no longer depends on the truncation path. A built-in tool's replacement is its own output object with its strings capped/redacted (keys and non-strings untouched); an MCP tool's is a string.
- `fake-claude-runner.ts` divergence 4 now refuses a scenario production would refuse (`decideUnattendedCommand`), and `fake-spawn.ts` honours a Bash replacement only in the tool's shape, as the CLI does.

**Measured, not assumed** (CLI 2.1.267 in `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64@0.3.267`, the pinned SDK driven against a stub Messages API on 127.0.0.1 that returned one `tool_use` and recorded the `tool_result` the CLI sent back, 2026-10-06): a **string** `updatedToolOutput` for `Bash` and for `Read` was ignored — the "model" received `ORIGINAL-STDOUT` and the original file — while a same-shaped object (`{...response, stdout}`, `{...response, file: {...file, content}}`) was honoured, and a string for an in-process MCP tool was honoured. The CLI's own source in that binary says why: it `safeParse`s the replacement against the tool's `outputSchema` and on failure logs *"PostToolUse hook returned updatedToolOutput that does not match <tool>'s output shape; using original output"*. So **before this change neither the cap nor the redaction of the hook reached the model for any built-in tool, `Bash` included**; the stored transcript was redacted regardless at write (TD-012). Also measured with the same stub: a `PreToolUse` `allow` ran `echo hi > out.txt`, `cd / && ls` and `rm -rf /tmp/…` with **no** `canUseTool` call, an `ask` reached `canUseTool`, and a `deny`'s reason is the text the model reads.

**Confirmed: dependency additions are judged afterwards.** `npm install <pkg>`, `pnpm add`, `pip install <pkg>`, `composer require` now run under `auto`; the dependency gate (`pipeline/dependency-gate.ts`, WP-38) fires on the Developer stage's completion and reads the merge request's manifest diff (allow / question / return). It does not see a package installed without a manifest change or by a role that pushes no diff, and a registry is reachable only when an operator declared it and the run may install from a lockfile (`runMayInstallFromLockfile`).

**The credential helper does not restrict the path.** `RunCredentialBroker.answer` refuses any host but the project's git host, by exact comparison, and only while the run is live — that is the control that holds whatever the spelling, because under `auto` an interpreter can spell any refused git command past a command-line reading. It does **not** compare the repository path (git sends none unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set): a static run token that reaches other repositories on the same host reaches them from such a spelling. Filed as **481**.

**Consequences, stated.** Under `auto` an `ask` entry a layer writes no longer stops a command (a narrowed `allow` decides only what is audited as an `ask`); a command a project wants stopped belongs in `block`. `verification.mode: ci`'s blocks hold through every wrapper, but a runner no list names (`vendor/bin/phpunit`) now runs under `auto` — the `## Verification` prompt is what keeps the model from it. `DECLINED_BLOCK_VARIANTS` (`rm -fr /`, `git branch --delete --force`) now run in the sandbox under `auto`; their stated verdicts say so.

**Tests.** `packages/domain/src/policies/unattended-commands.test.ts` (191: the `auto` allows with their recorded reasons, the `deny` refusals, block/uncertain/hazard in both modes, 82 carve-out spellings in both modes, a property of 1 000 runs over 7 core refusals × 25 wrappers — `env`, `sh -c`, `bash -c`, `eval`, lists, pipes, `( )`, `$( )`, backticks, `<( )`, `git -C`, `git -c`, `--no-pager`, quoted and escaped `git`, `/usr/bin/git`, `xargs` — and a property of 3 000 arbitrary lines that nothing blocked or unparseable is ever allowed and that `deny` never allows an ask; canary: `gitBoundaryViolation` stubbed to `null` failed 80); `packages/infrastructure/src/runner/hooks.test.ts` › "never answers `ask`, whatever the command and the mode", › "cuts a Bash output in its own shape — stdout and stderr together under the cap, every other key kept", › "still redacts a Read, in the Read’s own shape — the redaction does not depend on the cap", and the five cases of its `it.each` that never cap `Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Glob` or `Grep`; `fake-claude-runner.test.ts` › "refuses a scenario that pushes past the git boundary, whatever the lists say"; `repository-grades.test.ts`, `effective-config.test.ts`, `planner.test.ts` › "plans `auto` by default, and `deny` when any layer says so"; `apps/server/src/agent.test.ts` (the new denial text); the `denied-tool` golden. **Fake-Claude e2e, extended**: `test/e2e/pipeline/project-commands.e2e.test.ts` now drives both modes through the production hook — under `auto` the narrowed-away `npm run build` runs and writes its marker, its `hook` row says *unattended: ask allowed in the sandbox*, nothing reaches `canUseTool` and `GET …/config` publishes `unattended: auto`; under `deny` it never runs and the refusal names it (2/2 passed).

### 481. **The run credential helper answers for the project's git host but not for the project's repository: a static run token reaches every repository on that host its owner can, from any spelling the command-line git boundary does not read** **RESOLVED** at `860be46a`, first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **major — the real control behind backlog 480's carve-out**; found while deciding it, 2026-10-06). `RunCredentialBroker.answer(runId, host)` (`packages/infrastructure/src/workspace/broker.ts`) compares the host exactly and nothing else; the helper (`runlet/credential-helper.ts`) sends `protocol` and `host` only, and git sends no `path` unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set. Under `unattended: auto` an interpreter (`python3 -c '…subprocess…'`) or a script the run wrote can run `git push https://<git host>/<other group>/<other repo> …`, and git will ask the helper for that host. A minted project access token and a deploy key are scoped to the project by the provider; a dedicated user's token and the operator's own repository-only token (BD-025's 2026-10-03/04 amendments) are not. **Done when** the workspace's git configuration sets `credential.useHttpPath=true` (the launcher writes it beside the helper), the helper sends the path in `cred.get`, the broker refuses a path other than the project's repository (exact, normalised for a trailing `.git`), and a Docker check shows a push to another path on the same host failing for want of a credential.

**Built** (technical/05 § *Credentials and identity* and TD-025, both amended 2026-10-06). **The path reaches the broker**: `DockerWorkspaceProvider` (and the fake) answers `credential.useHttpPath=true` **beside** `credential.helper` in `cliEnvironment.gitConfig`, so the CLI's environment and the run container's carry it in the numbered `GIT_CONFIG_*` list (`COUNT=3` for an HTTPS run, still 2 for a deploy-key run); `agentic-runlet credential` forwards git's `path` verbatim in `cred.get` (required and nullable; at most 1 024 characters and no control character, otherwise `null`); the shim relays it; `RUNLET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is **2**, so a run image and a runner from either side of the change refuse each other at `hello`. **The rule** (`repositoryPathMatches` and `isRepositoryPath` in `packages/infrastructure/src/workspace/broker.ts`): the runner's broker holds `RunWorkspaceProject.projectPath` — `repositoryPathOf(projects.repo_url)` — and answers only a `path` that is exactly `P` or exactly `P.git`: case-sensitive, nothing decoded, no slash trimmed, no query. No path, another repository, a case variant, `P.GIT`, `P/` and every normalisation git did not do itself get the ordinary `null` and a `warn` with `run_id` and `reason` (`no_path`, `another_repository`, `another_host`, `no_repository_held`, `deploy_key`), never the path text, which the workspace chose. `hold` refuses (`invalid_spec`) a `P` outside GitLab's own path rule; it now runs inside the provisioner's `try`, so that refusal revokes a minted token like any failed start. A broker holding no path answers nothing — the launcher's copy, which serves only its helpers. **What needed nothing**: the mirror fetch and export push (`credentialFor` and their own environment helper, against the mirror's `remote.origin.url`, which the run cannot change), and a deploy-key run (no HTTPS helper; its reach is the key's enablement at the provider, decision 13b item 8).

**Measured, not assumed** (2026-10-06, no real credential anywhere). (1) git 2.47.3 in `platform-runtime:dev`, a logging helper against a local HTTPS server that answers 401: with the list's `useHttpPath` the helper received `path=` for `ls-remote` and `push` alike; git percent-decodes it, resolves `.`/`..` and trims slashes before the helper sees it (`acme/%2e%2e/other/repo.git` and `acme/api.git/../../other/repo.git` arrive as `other/repo.git`, `acme%2Fapi.git` as `acme/api.git`), keeps a query (`acme/api.git?x=1`) and sends a URL's user name as a separate field; a repository's `credential.useHttpPath=false` **and** its `credential.https://<host>.useHttpPath=false` both lost to the command-line list (git applies every matching `credential.*` entry in reading order); `git -c credential.useHttpPath=false` won and git sent no path. (2) `node scripts/credential-path-check.mjs` (new; the image's git, and the helper, shim, spawn adapter and broker from source, a fake static token held for `acme/api`): `ls-remote` and `push` of `acme/api.git` each carried the token once; five asks for `other/repo.git` — `push`, `ls-remote`, a push from a `node -e` child process, one under `-c credential.useHttpPath=false`, one with the repository's configuration switched off — never carried it; the broker logged `another_repository` four times and `no_path` once, and no log line held the token: `PASS: credential-path-check (4/4 checks)`. (3) The host's own git repeats (1) through the Docker provider's real answer and `cliEnvironment`, with the list minus the entry as the control: `packages/infrastructure/src/workspace/cli-environment.test.ts` › "asks with the path for ls-remote and push, over a repository that turned it off".

**Tests.** `packages/infrastructure/src/workspace/broker.test.ts` › "the repository path a cred.get is answered for" (two accepted spellings; twenty refusals, each named for the looser rule that would admit it — a case-folding matcher fails exactly the case and upper-case-suffix rows; no path; no path held; one repository per run; the refusal log carries neither the path nor the token; ten malformed held paths). `packages/infrastructure/src/launcher/provisioner.test.ts` › "answers the project’s repository on the git host and refuses another repository on it" (over a real shim). The helper (verbatim forwarding, `null` for absent, empty, over-long and control-character paths), the shim (relayed path; a frame without `path`, an empty one, a newline and 1 025 characters are protocol errors; protocol 1 refused at `hello`), the spawn adapter (the path reaches the responder), the options composition (`COUNT=3`; a spec cannot remove the entry), the provider contract suite and the launcher's own copy (answers no workspace). `scripts/launcher-control-plane-check.mjs` now expects `COUNT=3` and a refused fill for `other/repo.git` — **not run**: it needs images rebuilt from this tree, and the running stack's tags were left alone.

**A residual this does not close, stated.** The helper's answer is the token itself, as it must be for the project's own push. Code that asks the helper for the project's path — an interpreter speaking git's credential protocol to `agentic-runlet credential`, which the command boundary refuses by name but cannot see inside a script — holds the value and can use it against any repository the token reaches on the git host. For a dedicated user's or the operator's static token the bound on a *determined* run is therefore still the token's own scope; what this closes is every request **git** makes (a wrapper, a script, an agent's mistake). Keeping the value out of the container is TD-021's phase 2. **Discovered work:** whether that residual earns its own row — a git-host-only proxy that injects the credential for the project's path — is the orchestrator's to number.

### 482. **RESOLVED** at `e214edb1`, WP-153, session 12 — **The command scanner reads a here-document's body as commands, so a line in it can refuse the whole command** (TODO, **minor — pre-existing, more visible under `auto`**; found while building backlog 480, 2026-10-06). `parseCommand` splits on newlines without knowing `<<EOF`, so `cat > a.php <<'EOF'` followed by a body with an apostrophe (`// don't`) is an unbalanced quote — rule 5's uncertainty, which an unattended run refuses in both modes — and a body line that reads like a refused git command is judged as one. `computesCommandName` skips here-document bodies; the scanner does not. Agents usually write files with the Write tool, so the cost is a refused turn with a reason that names the construct. **Done when** the scanner treats a here-document body as data (bounded by its delimiter, `<<-` stripping tabs, a quoted delimiter disabling expansion and an unquoted one still running `$(…)`), with bypass cases.
> **M9 (architect, session 12): → WP-153.**


### 484. **The unattended git boundary did not see through `timeout`: `timeout 180 git push --no-verify …`, a refspec push and a push to a foreign URL were allowed** **RESOLVED** at `cdfc3e40`, first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **security — major; found by reading AUT-6820's third developer run, which pushed as `timeout 180 git push -u origin agentic/AUT-6820`, then `--no-verify`, then `origin HEAD:refs/heads/agentic/AUT-6820`, each recorded "unattended: ask allowed in the sandbox (no list matches it)"**. `commandArgvCandidates` peels only `ARGV0_WRAPPERS`, which had `env`, `nice`, `nohup`, `xargs` and the shells but no `timeout`. Fifteen exec wrappers were added (`timeout`, `stdbuf`, `setsid`, `flock`, `chrt`, `taskset`, `unbuffer`, `watch`, `strace`, `ltrace`, `nsenter`, `unshare`, `runuser`, `su`, `doas` — not `sudo`, which the block list bans by name); the block list reads the same list, so it only tightens. The property test's wrapper table gained six spellings and three named cases, which fail without the change. **Still an enumeration** (backlog 481's credential-helper path check is the control that does not depend on spelling))

### 483. **A task escalated to `needs_human` could not be sent back to an earlier stage: `return-to-stage` and `rework` answered `409 illegal_transition: needs_human -> returned`, and the only way to `implementation` was `resume` then a return raced against the stage re-escalating** **RESOLVED** at `2284d056` (docs `67c434dd`), first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **major — the person handling an escalation is exactly the one who knows which earlier stage should re-run**). AUT-6820 escalated at `ci_gate` because its developer stage opened no merge request; `TASK_TRANSITIONS.needs_human` is `['active', 'paused', 'cancelled']`, so a person could resume the task only *at the stage it stopped at*.

**What was built.** *The transition design — no new edge.* `returnEscalatedTask` in the Task aggregate (`packages/domain/src/aggregates/task.ts`) takes the two edges the table already has, `needs_human → active` (`task.resumed`, as every way out of a stop emits) and `active → returned` (`task.stage.returned`), in **one** decision; `applyDecision` applies a `return` through it when a human command passes `returnFromEscalation` (`transitions.ts`), and `returnToStageCommand`/`reworkStageCommand` pass it for a `needs_human` task (`escalationReturn` in `commands.ts`). The table stays as technical/02 draws it on purpose: `needs_human → returned` as an edge would let any caller of `returnToStage` — a provider signal interpreted for a parked task included — un-park it, and `task.resumed` is load-bearing (the dependency gate's deferred ending is performed on it, a take-over ends on it). The aggregate **refuses** rather than escalates: any other state, a spent loop (`InvariantViolationError`; the command refuses first with `iteration_limit_reached`, so no HTTP request re-escalates), and a task that entered `merged_gate`. The rework's close duty takes its cause from the `task.stage.returned` event by type, because out of an escalation the first event is the `task.resumed`. The parked attempt's `task_stages` row is closed `returned` with outcome `escalated` — it ended in the escalation, so the Checks panel reads *"escalated, then sent back by a person"* instead of *"red, sent back"* — and the person's note is its `return_reason`, which is how the target stage is given it (redacted, TD-012).
*The rule both returns now share, from `active` too.* The order asserted a target *"must be an earlier stage the task has reached"*, and nothing checked it: a return named any string, and an unknown stage left the task `active` at a stage nothing would run. `assertReturnTarget` refuses a stage the compiled template does not run or has disabled (`409 stage_not_in_template`, the hand-back's error) and one the task has not entered or that sits after its current stage (`StageNotReachedError`, `409 stage_not_reached`). **Assumption:** the current stage itself is admitted, as it was — a return to it or a rework of it is a new attempt carrying the person's words, which `retry-stage` does not carry. `compile-sites.test.ts` counts the new `compilePipeline` site (28).
*retry-stage and resume from `needs_human`* already worked (`humanEnter` → `enterStage`, `needs_human → active`, `task.resumed`) and are unchanged; a case holds it.
*The SPA* never hid the stage commands for `needs_human` (`StageCommands` renders for every state with an entered stage); it now says, on a `needs_human` task, that sending it back, reworking it or retrying the stopped stage is the way out.
*Docs:* technical/02 (dated note under the Task state machine), product/04 (the escalation definition), technical/08 (the two refusal codes), the user guide's *Return to stage* and *Rework* rows, the state table's docblock, and the saga's two blocker-brief comments that said a return was refused (the briefs still name only the retry, which is what asks afresh).

**Tests.** Domain: `task.test.ts` (`returnEscalatedTask` admitted with the two events chained on the stream; refused from eight other states, for a merged task, and for a spent loop; `returnToStage` still refused from `needs_human`), and a `ReturnEscalated` command in the model-based property test, run from every state the sequences reach. Application: `human-commands.test.ts` parks a task at `ci_gate` through the real red-CI loop and returns it (events `task.resumed`, `task.stage.returned`, `task.stage.entered`, all by the user; a human round; the reason redacted; the gate row `returned`/`escalated`; the next Developer run's `return_feedback` carries the note and not the planted credential; BD-008 parks it again), reworks it (agent loops reset, new branch, close duty's cause is the return), refuses an unknown, an unreached and a Ready target and a spent loop with nothing appended, still retries the stopped stage; plus the new guard from `active` and the still-refused return from a pause; `deadlines.test.ts`'s refusal became an acceptance. Server: `routes/commands.test.ts` drives both routes for a `needs_human` task through the real router (one `human_actions` row each) and maps `stage_not_reached`. UI: `stage-commands.test.tsx` (the hint, and both requests with an `Idempotency-Key`) and a Checks-panel case. E2E (fake Claude): `pipeline.e2e.test.ts` returns the task the red pipeline parked, through the real route, and asserts the run's prompt, the user-actor events and one audit row.

**Discovered work** (for the refiner). A task escalated **after** its merge (in `retro`) has no human way forward but cancel, and one wrong one: `resume`/`retry-stage` at `retrospective` take `needs_human → retro`, which is not an edge (409), while `hand-back` to an agent stage takes `needs_human → active` and would put a merged task back to work — the side door `returnEscalatedTask` closes for returns, still open for the hand-back.

### 485. **A red pipeline with three failing jobs returned the task with one job's log: AUT-6820's Developer was given phpstan's and had to fix `db-schema-consistency` and `codesniffer` blind** **RESOLVED** at `571872fe`, first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **major — the project is `verification.mode: ci` and the run image has no PHP, so the CI log is the only evidence the run gets**). `failingJobWithLog` (`packages/application/src/pipeline/ci-log.ts`) picked the first failing, not-allowed-to-fail job that named a log and `readFailingJobLog` read that one; the other two were named in the gate's sentence and nothing more. The `return_feedback` block's marker said `original_chars="20657"` — phpstan's log alone.

**What was built.** `ci-log.ts`: `failingJobs` names every failing, not-allowed-to-fail job in the pipeline's order; `selectLogJobs` keeps at most `MAX_CI_LOG_JOBS` = 5 (those naming a log first, both lists back in pipeline order) and names the rest; `readFailingJobLogs` reads them **sequentially** through `gitReads.jobLog` (the executor: audited, rate-limited, refused inside a transaction — the gate's artifact transaction is closed before the reads, as before) and redacts each **whole** before anything is cut. **The budget rule**: the 6 000 characters WP-81 gave one log (`CI_LOG_BUDGET_CHARS`) are **split, not multiplied**, by `splitLogBudget` — max-min fair, shortest first, each log an even share of what is left, so a short log stays whole and gives its unused share to the others, and no log gets less than `floor(6000 / n)` (1 200 at the cap, `CI_LOG_MIN_SHARE_CHARS`) unless it is shorter; an unreadable log takes no share. `boundLog(text, share)` keeps **the end first**: the tail takes the share up to 4 500 and only a larger share keeps a head, up to 1 500 — so a lone failing job keeps exactly WP-81's head and tail (the existing cases did not move). `gates.ts` `composeFailureDetail`: the platform's sentences, then per job in pipeline order `Log of the failing job <name>, redacted:\n<excerpt>` or `No log of the failing job <name> is included: <why>.`, then `N more failing jobs past the first 5, whose logs were not read: …`; `detailOriginalChars` is the detail's length plus every included log's cut, so `truncated`/`original_chars` stay true for the whole block (the jobs past the cap are said in words, not counted as a cut). `CiReading.logJob` became `logJobs`; the event path (`ci-settle.ts`) passes the event's `failed_job_logs` through `failingJobs`, and a payload from an older build states per job that no log was named. Docs: technical/04 (dated amendment under the WP-81 paragraph), technical/02, product/04 S4, BD-024's consequence, the user guide.

Sample, three jobs (fake text):

```
pipeline p-7 failed: phpstan, db-schema-consistency, codesniffer
Log of the failing job phpstan, redacted:
…last ~3 000 characters… Line 12: Call to an undefined method Totals::round()
 [ERROR] Found 1 error
Log of the failing job db-schema-consistency, redacted:
[ERROR] The database schema is not in sync with the current mapping file.
No log of the failing job codesniffer is included: the provider refused the log (not_found).
```

**Tests.** `ci-log.test.ts`: `boundLog` end-first at a small share, head only past the tail, WP-81's split at the whole budget; `splitLogBudget` even split, a short log's share given away, the 1 200 minimum at the cap, and a fast-check property (never past the budget, never more than a log has, none below `min(length, floor(budget / n))`, less than one character per log left unspent while a log was cut); `failingJobs`/`selectLogJobs` order and cap. `gates.test.ts` › "every failing job’s log (backlog 485)": three jobs → three labelled tails of exactly 2 000 each, read in order, a token straddling a share's start leaving no byte, `detailOriginalChars` equal to the detail plus every cut; a short log's share given to the other two; a job with no log reference and a refused read said by name, the one readable log given the whole budget (head and tail); seven failing jobs → five reads and `2 more failing jobs past the first 5, whose logs were not read: f, g.` with no cut reported. Two existing cases' expected wording moved to the per-job line. `planner.test.ts`: the three-job reason rendered as one `return_feedback` block, its marker carrying the gate's `original_chars`, no log text outside it. Fake-Claude e2e (`pipeline.e2e.test.ts`, *when the merge request's pipeline is red*): a new case seeds AUT-6820's three jobs (`codesniffer` with no log) through a new harness option `ciFailedJobs` (`test/e2e/support/pipeline.ts`; the fake provider already held several jobs per pipeline, so its divergence register is unchanged) and asserts the second Developer prompt's block.

**Residual.** The labels are platform text inside the untrusted block, so a job's log can print a line that reads like one; the nonce'd marker is the boundary, as for every other line in a data block. Five reads per settlement instead of one: a pipeline that fails often on a poll-only binding spends up to five of the binding's `get_job_log` budget per settlement.

*Follow-up (backlog 481's session, 2026-10-06):* with `sudo` peeled, `sudo rm -rf /var` is refused by the block-list entry `rm -rf /*` rather than `sudo *`, and the `denied-tool` golden transcript still named the old entry, so `pnpm run -s verify` was red on `main` after `cdfc3e40`. The golden now names the entry that matches (`672bd8c1`); both entries block, only the reason text changed.

### 490. **A CI gate whose provider stopped answering threw its job until pg-boss failed it, and the task was escalated as a stage that had *"never started"*** **RESOLVED** at `02c9a073`, first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **major — robustness; a network blip parks every task waiting at a gate**. AUT-6820 waited at `ci_gate` on a poll-only GitLab binding (WP-136) when the host's network to gitlab.com dropped. The gate's `stage.execute` threw — first a bare `TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout`, then `IntegrationError {code: "unavailable", cause: TimeoutError}` — so the queue's two retries were spent in about ten minutes and the job ended `failed`; the stranded-stage recovery (WP-108) re-enqueued it once, that job failed the same way, and the task went to `needs_human` with *"the "ci_gate" stage (attempt 6) was entered … and never started: no job was queued for it and no run was created"*. The stage had started many times; the provider had been unreachable. **Done when** a transient provider failure during a gate's evaluation is a bounded re-ask with a brief naming the provider error, not a thrown job, and the recovery's brief says a job **failed** when it did.)

**What was built.** `packages/application/src/pipeline/gate-outage.ts` (pure): `transientProviderFailure` answers `unavailable` or `rate_limited` for an `IntegrationError` whose own `retryable` says so (the executor's two retry codes), `timeout` for a bare `TimeoutError` (what `AbortSignal.timeout` rejects with — including while a body is read, after the adapter's `catch`, which is AUT-6820's first error), `network` for undici's `TypeError: fetch failed` and the closed `NETWORK_ERROR_CODES` list (`ECONNRESET`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `UND_ERR_*`, …), following the cause chain five links; an `IntegrationError` with any other code decides by its code, whatever transport error it carries (`unauthorised`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `invalid_request`, `invalid_response`, `unsupported_capability` keep today's ending: the job throws). Class and code only — never the message. `gates.ts`: every provider read of the CI and rebase gates runs inside one closure whose `catch` turns a transient failure into `{kind: 'unreachable', code, provider, host, ciTimeoutMinutes}` (a new `GateEvaluation` = `GateResult | GateProviderOutage`; `judgeCiSettlement` and `ci-settle.ts` keep `GateResult`) and rethrows anything else unchanged. `jobs.ts`: `waitForProvider` re-asks after **30 s doubling to a 5 min ceiling** (30, 60, 120, 240, 300, 300 …) and does **not** move `gate_checks` (a failed read is not a check, so an outage cannot spend `MAX_GATE_CHECKS`). The bound: the CI gate on a **poll-only** binding keeps WP-136's clock — `ci_timeout_minutes` from the attempt's `task_stages.entered_at`, the last re-ask clamped to the deadline, a closed row doing nothing; every other gate gets `GATE_OUTAGE_LIMIT_MINUTES` = **60** (the default CI timeout) from the first failure in a row. That instant and the count ride the payload (`provider_failing_since`, `provider_failures`), cleared by any answer, a `pending` included; a backstop count (`ceil(limit / 30 s) + 1`) bounds the chain if a clock is wrong, and an instant that does not parse is past the deadline (rule 16). **The `stage.execute` payload is now parsed by a strict zod schema** (`stageExecuteDataSchema`; `enqueueStage` is its one writer) — there was none, only a cast and an `effortSchema.parse`. At the bound the task is escalated `undecided`; the brief: *"gitlab.com did not answer for 60 minutes: unavailable. The "ci_gate" gate asked 16 times without an answer, waiting 30 seconds and then twice as long each time up to 5 minutes, until the platform's 60-minute limit for a provider outage at a gate. Nothing about the merge request was decided: this is the provider being unreachable, not a result. Check that gitlab.com is reachable from the platform's host (and its status page), then hand the task back at ci_gate."* (on a poll-only CI gate the bound reads *"the CI timeout of N minutes from the gate's entry (`pipeline.limits.ci_timeout_minutes = N`)"*); the reason: *"the "ci_gate" gate could not be decided: gitlab.com did not answer for 60 minutes: unavailable (16 failed reads); it stopped at … (PROGRESS backlog 490)"*. The host is the binding's `IntegrationRef.host`, the provider id when it names none.

*The recovery's brief.* `StrandedStage.failedJob` (application) and a second lateral read in `postgres-stranded-stage-store.ts`: the newest `stage.execute` job of **this entry** (`data.stage`/`data.attempt` compared, never selected; completed at or after `entered_at`) in pg-boss's `failed` state, with `retry_count + 1` and the serialised error's `name`/`code` and its cause's, each bounded to 80 characters. The output shape was measured, not assumed: serialize-error 13.0.1 (pg-boss 12.30.0's) answers AUT-6820's error as `{code: "unavailable", provider, action, retryable, name: "IntegrationError", message, cause: {name: "TimeoutError", message, code: 23}}`. `errorIdentifier` admits only `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$`, so a message — which may quote a provider (BD-022) — never reaches the brief. The ending, when the entry has no ended run but a failed job: reason *"… its stage.execute job failed: the queue spent its retries (3 tries), the last one at … throwing IntegrationError (unavailable), caused by TimeoutError (23); the platform re-enqueued the stage once at … and it is still stuck (PROGRESS backlogs 320, 490)"*; brief *"ACME-1 is at "ci_gate", and the job that runs this stage kept failing: the queue spent its retries (3 tries) and the last one threw IntegrationError (unavailable), caused by TimeoutError (23); one re-enqueue by the platform did not get the stage past it either. The stage did start — it is the job that failed, not a job that was lost. That error means a provider did not answer: check that it is reachable from the platform's host. The failed job and its message are in the organisation's failed-jobs list. Fix the cause, then hand the task back at "ci_gate" — or cancel it if it is no longer wanted."* (the reachability sentence only for a transient class or code). The re-enqueue before it is unchanged. The pass's log line carries `failed_job_error` (class and code).

*The fake.* `FailureScript.failWhile(action, decide)` (`packages/integrations/src/support/fake-support.ts`): an outage the test ends by its own condition, consulted after the queued failures — divergence 30 of the git fake's register.

**Tests.** `gate-outage.test.ts` (the classifier's codes, its refusals over a transport cause, message text never read, the cause depth, odd throwables; the delay sequence and two fast-check properties — the delay in [30 s, 5 min] and non-decreasing, and the chain never re-asking past its deadline nor past the backstop; the clamp, rule 16, the brief's and reason's words). `gates.test.ts` › "a gate whose provider does not answer (backlog 490)" (each read of both gates answers `unreachable` with its code; the CI timeout only for the CI gate on a poll-only binding; four non-transient codes over a `TimeoutError` cause and a programming error rethrown by identity). `saga.test.ts` › "a gate whose provider does not answer (backlog 490)" (30 s → 5 min over seven failed reads with `gate_checks` still 1 and no escalation, then Ready when the provider answers; a `pending` clears the clock; parks at exactly 60 minutes with the exact brief and reason; a poll-only CI gate parks at its 15-minute timeout from the entry with the last step clamped, delays `[60 s, 30 s, 60 s, 120 s, 30 s]`; a `forbidden` still throws; the strict payload refuses an unparseable instant and an unknown key). `stranded-stage.test.ts` › "says the stage’s job failed, by class and code, when its last job failed rather than was lost (backlog 490)" and › "quotes a failed job’s class and code only when they are identifiers, never text (BD-022)". `stranded-stage-store.integration.test.ts` › "reads the entry’s failed job by class and code, and no other entry’s (backlog 490)" (a planted fake token in the message absent from the row; another attempt's and a pre-entry failed job not read). `fake-support.test.ts` › "keeps an outage until its own condition says the provider is back (backlog 490)". Fake-Claude e2e `test/e2e/pipeline/gate-outage.e2e.test.ts`: the fake git provider down for twelve pipeline reads made inside `stage.execute` (an `AsyncLocalStorage` through the harness's `jobs` seam, because the `mr_pipeline` duty reads the same status at the same moment) — four evaluations of three executor attempts, more than a thrown job's nine — reaches Ready with no `task.escalated`, no failed `stage.execute` job and four failed `get_pipeline_status` audit rows of three attempts each; **canary**: with the transient branch disabled it never leaves `ci_gate` (measured, 90 s to the settle deadline).

**Residual, stated.** An `IntegrationError` inside `ciConfigOnDefaultBranch` (the CI-location read, WP-139) is still caught there and answered `pending` with the error named — a transient one spends a gate check, as before; and an `IntegrationError` reading a failing job's log is still an *unreadable log* in a red pipeline's detail (`ci-log.ts`). Neither throws; a bare `TimeoutError` from either now reaches the outage path instead of failing the job. An agent stage's provider reads are untouched (they never threw the job: rule 20 at each read).

**Verification.** `pnpm run -s verify` PASS. Fake-Claude e2e: `test/e2e/pipeline` (all 38 files, the new one included) plus `onboarding/discovery-recovery` and `onboarding/history-bootstrap` (the other two that drive the stranded-stage row): 40 files, 109 tests, PASS. Integration: `test/integration/recovery` (10 files, 67 tests) PASS.

The model shortened the summary on every retry and never added a field. **Done when** this is measured and one of: the ImplementationNotes schema makes its lists optional with `[]` defaults and `mr` filled from the platform's record when absent (the record wins anyway, WP-138), so a summary-only answer validates; or the platform's prompt carries a minimal valid example of the artifact; or, after the second identical rejection, the runner steers the run with the missing field names in platform text. ### 495. **Rejecting a plan created no stage attempt: the task moved to architecture attempt 2 with no `task_stages` row, so its run had no stage and the maintainer's reason never reached the architect** **RESOLVED** at `c0a5e3a3`, first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **major — the product owner inserted the row into the database by hand**: *"zamítnutí plánu nezaloží pokus stage (to jsme v DB dopsali ručně)"*. Product owner's feedback)

**Cause.** `packages/application/src/pipeline/saga.ts`'s `pipeline.approval` handler answered a rejected plan with the domain's `resumeStage` and a task `save` — never `recordStageEntered`, which only `transitions.ts`'s `enter` called. The aggregate moved `waiting_approval → active` at architecture attempt N+1 and emitted `task.resumed` + `task.stage.entered`, but the attempt had no row: `stage.execute` treated the absent row as open (`revalidateOpen`) and ran the architect, whose `runs` row was inserted with `task_stage_id` null (so the run projection refuses it a stage, the 409 of backlog 493), whose completion closed nothing, and whose prompt carried no `return_feedback` — `lastReturnReason` reads a row whose `returned_to` is the stage, and nothing wrote one. **The answered-question resumption in the same file had the identical gap** (a question at refinement, or the dependency gate's question at implementation). The censuses in `task-save-sites.test.ts` count closes per escalation and per entry *row write*, so an entry with no row write was invisible to them.

**What a rejection now does, event by event** (`resumeAtStage` in `transitions.ts`, the one way out of a human wait back into its stage): the route appends `task.approval.decided` (`rejected`, the reason redacted) → the saga closes the parked attempt's row `returned` to its **own** stage, outcome **`plan.rejected`** (a new `taskStageOutcomeWordSchema` word with its sentence on the task page), `return_reason` = the reason → `task.resumed` and `task.stage.entered` (architecture, attempt N+1) → the new attempt's row is opened `running`, `caused_by_event_id` = the decision → `architecture_revisions` + 1 → `stage.execute` enqueued after commit, whose architect run gets the reason as its `return_feedback` block. With the loop spent (default 2) `resumeStage` escalates instead: `task.escalated`, the rejected attempt still carries the reason, the parked row is closed through `closeParkedStageRow`, nothing runs. An answered question goes through the same function without the returned row.

**Other approval kinds.** `budget` rejected escalates (`budget.rejected`, `closeParkedStageRow`) — no attempt is entered, correct; `expired` escalates likewise; `approved` re-asks the interpreter, whose `enter` writes the row. `knowledge` and `rework` are declared in `approvalKindSchema` and created by no writer in this build.

**Decided.** The rejected attempt's row is overwritten from the executor's `completed` to `returned`, which is what `apply`'s `return` case already does to every agent verdict's row; the self-return is the shape `lastReturnReason` was written to read (a human return at the stage the task is at). Docs: BD-006 amendment (it was silent on what a rejection does), product/04 S2, technical/02's Approval section.

**Tests.** `saga.test.ts`: the rejection's three events, the two rows (attempt 1 `returned`/`plan.rejected` with the reason, attempt 2 opened and closed by its run) and the second architect prompt's `return_feedback` block; the bound (three rejections → `needs_human`, counter at 2, three `returned` rows); the answered question's attempt-2 row. A new census (`every stage entry opens its attempt's row`): every `enterStage(`/`resumeStage(` in a production module is matched by a `.recordStageEntered(`, and `resumeStage(` counts in the escalation census. `command-api.e2e.test.ts`: a reject through the real route against PostgreSQL — the rows, the events after the decision, both architect runs linked to a stage, the reason in attempt 2's stored `user_prompt`, the counter; and the question case now waits for refinement attempt 2's run joined to its row. **Before the fix** the three saga cases and the e2e reject case failed (*expected [ 1 ] to deeply equal [ 1, 2 ]*).

**Verification.** `pnpm run -s verify` PASS; `verify:ui` PASS; fake-Claude e2e: `command-api`, `budget-approval`, `epic-split`, `dependency-gate`, `dependency-gate-recovery`, `slack-socket`, `manual-start`, `read-api` — 8 files, 19 tests, PASS.

### 494. **A retry pressed while the stage's run was in flight was silently skipped: answered 200, no second run, and the old run's result won** **RESOLVED** at `17e6c05b`, first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **major — the person's command did nothing and said nothing**, product owner: *"retry během běžícího pokusu se tiše přeskočí"*). **Root cause**: `retryStageCommand` (`packages/application/src/pipeline/commands.ts:912` before the fix) only moved the attempt counter, and its docblock claimed that *superseded* the live run — but the executor's re-validation is asked of a **job**, and the old run was already past it. Its recording transaction (`stage-executor.ts` `record`, `:1546`–`:1719`) checked the task's state and never its **attempt**, so `completeStage` completed the stage on the task's new attempt; the new attempt's job, waiting behind the old one on the `stately` `stage.execute` queue (pg-boss 12: one `created` and one `active` per key, the fetch tolerating the unique violation until the active job ends), then found the task at the next stage and skipped. Measured first in the harness: `human-commands.test.ts` › "stops the run in flight and runs the new attempt — the old run never completes the stage" answered `[1]` where `[1, 2]` was expected. **Behaviour chosen: (a), stop the run** — what the docs promised. The retry locks the stage's live run (`lockLiveRunOf(…, {forUpdate, stage})`, so an ask beside it is never touched) and stops it through the run cancel's two branches **without the cancel's pause** (TD-028 decision 11: a `cancel` row for a live lease holder, its id derived from the `Idempotency-Key`; the record ended in place otherwise). The executor records a run whose attempt the task left and completes nothing (`isCurrentStageAttempt` on the task aggregate); the lease sweep ends such a run without escalating the task on the new attempt; a stage wake-up for a superseded attempt **forwards** itself to the current one, so a second retry whose enqueue was `coalesced` onto the first still runs (canary: the forward disabled → `[1]` for `[1, 3]`). The answer is `retryStageResponseSchema` — `attempt` and `stopped_run {run_id, command_id}` — audited so a replay answers the same, and *Retry stage* now shows it as a status line. `POST /api/runs/:id/retry` is unchanged: it refuses a live run (`run_not_live`). Amended: technical/08 and technical/02 (2026-10-06), the user guide's command table. ### 486. **The developer's merge request was marked ready as soon as the Developer stage completed, before CI and the reviews had run: the product owner wants it a draft until it is green and verified** **RESOLVED** at `ceac6213`, first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **product-owner decision — reverses WP-138 ruling (g)**: *"Not marking the MR ready until it is green and verified."* Ruling (g) undrafted at the Developer's completion because Autix's CI skipped drafts; Autix's rule is being changed separately so `agentic/*` drafts run full CI).

**What was built.** `packages/application/src/pipeline/merge-request-ready.ts` is now three duties, each a priority-120 handler that decides and a `pipeline.outbound` job that calls (WP-15d), all through `IntegrationActionExecutor` (shadow → `would_have`):
- **`mr_pipeline`** (on `task.stage.completed` of the `ImplementationNotes` stage) keeps backlog 459's nudge — a merge-request pipeline when the live head has none or one held at `manual` and the default branch has (or may have) a CI file, keyed per head — and **marks nothing ready**. It reads the merge request first for its live head and asks nothing for one that is merged or closed.
- **`mr_ready`** (on `task.stage.entered` for `ready_for_merge`, every way in: the rebase gate's pass, a resume from a pause at Ready, the `ready_head_check` entry) reads the merge request and removes `Draft:` when it has it, keyed per entry; a task no longer at `ready_for_merge` when the job fires is left alone.
- **`mr_draft`** (on `task.stage.entered` for an **agent** stage of a task whose `stageAttempts.ready_for_merge ≥ 1`) puts an open, ready merge request back to draft, only while the task is `active` — so a late job never re-drafts a merge request that is Ready again. **Decided:** a **gate** re-entry from Ready (a default-branch move re-checks `rebase_gate`, a person's push re-enters `ci_gate`) does not re-draft: nothing of the platform's changes the merge request there, and toggling draft on every default-branch move is noise on the provider. A person who marked it ready by hand while an agent reworks it is overruled the same way.
- **Exhaustion** (`ports/job-exhaustion.ts`): `mr_pipeline` and `mr_ready` bound-and-escalate (with escalation text in `outbound.ts`), `mr_draft` notification-shaped; the census reads thirty-two duties (it said twenty-nine with thirty declared). New executor action `mark_merge_request_draft` (`codeMergeRequestWrites.markDraft`).
- **The CI gate's pending detail** (`gates.ts`, `pendingPipelineDetail`, the one change to that file): a pipeline whose status is `manual` reads *"the merge request is a draft and pipeline N is held at manual job "X" — the project's CI rules may skip or hold jobs for drafts, and the platform keeps its merge request a draft until Ready; see the readiness panel's CI-rules warning"*, or, for a merge request that is not a draft, *"… is held at manual job "X": nothing runs until somebody starts it on the provider"*. A `running` pipeline with a manual job further on still reads *running*.
- **WP-143's readiness check** (`packages/domain/src/readiness/ci-rules.ts`) assumed *"`mr_ready` undrafts before the CI gate reads a pipeline"*: its merge-request context now carries the title `Draft: X-1: change`, the context is worded *a draft merge-request pipeline*, and the warning's fix adds *including a draft's*. On Autix's shape the merge-request half is now decided by the `Draft:` rule (`codeception` rules[1]).
- **Prompts:** the developer prompt (version 4, eval case `dev-mr-stays-draft`), the `gitlab-mr` skill (4) and the `mr-description` skill (3) no longer say the platform marks the merge request ready at the stage's completion; they say it stays a draft until Ready and is never marked ready by the run.
- **Docs:** the plan's WP-138 ruling (g) (dated amendment), product/04 S7, technical/06's port line, technical/02's exhaustion table, the user guide (*The merge request stays a draft until Ready*), `docs/first-local-test.md` (the CI-rules step now asks for `agentic/` drafts to run the test jobs; § 7), `docs/TODO.md`'s measurement row.

### 496. **`report_progress` was offered to nearly every role and refused at every call: `TranscriptEvent` had no kind for a line the agent reports, and the task page gave no sense of what a running stage was doing** **RESOLVED** at `3780fa1e`, first local test (2026-10-06) — (TODO, **major — agents on Autix called it and read an error back ("report_progress padá"), and the operator's question during a run, "is anything happening?" (backlog 455), had no answer but a static badge**. **Done when** an accepted call writes one bounded, redacted transcript row through the run's own sink, a call in a loop floods nothing, the model is answered in a plain sentence, the run page renders the row, the task page shows the running stage's latest line live, and the developer and architect prompts say when to call it. Product owner's feedback)

**What was built.**
- **A transcript kind** `progress` (`packages/contracts/src/transcript.ts`, migration **0084** appends it to `transcript_kind`): `{summary, percent_complete, truncated}` with the usual envelope. The tool trims the summary and cuts it to `PROGRESS_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS` (500); the stored ceiling is four times that, because the cut happens before the runner's redaction door and a redaction may lengthen the text — an entry past even that becomes the runner's `transcript_normalisation_failed` row, never an unbounded one.
- **How the tool reaches the sink**: the runner (`claude-runner.ts`) puts a **progress door** on `PlatformToolContext.progress`, built over its single transcript door, so the row takes the run's next `seq`, its TD-012 redactor and its sink, and is announced on `run:<id>` like every other entry. The door holds the **per-run rate bound** (`createProgressGate`): at most one line per 30 s and 100 per run, on the runner's clock; a refused call writes nothing. `reportProgressTool` (`packages/application/src/pipeline/progress-tool.ts`) bounds the words and answers the model in one plain sentence — *"Progress recorded."*, *"Progress recorded, shortened to its first 500 characters."*, *"Not recorded: … Carry on …"* — never as an error. `apps/server/src/platform-tools.ts` composes it, and `report_progress` is in `IMPLEMENTED_PLATFORM_TOOLS`, so the planner registers it again (backlog 476's `availablePlatformTools`) and *This run* lists it.
- **The runner's transcript door is serialised.** Hooks and tool handlers write while the message loop does, and the SSE bridge reads rows back from a watermark, so a row stored after a higher `seq` would never reach a live stream. The door now hands the sink one entry at a time in `seq` order (canary: without the chain, `keeps a slow progress write ahead of the rows written after it` fails).
- **The read**: `RunRecord.latest_progress` — `{seq, at, summary, percent_complete}` or `null` — on `GET /api/runs/:id`, the task page's runs and the Agents screen (`latestProgressFor`, one `distinct on (run_id)` query per list).
- **The SPA**: the run page's transcript renders a *progress* card (percentage badge, a cut marked *shortened by the platform*, searchable); the task page shows a **live stage** panel above the header while a stage run has not ended — a pulsing indicator, stage and role, elapsed time, the latest line and *Watch the run* — subscribing to `run:<id>` while mounted, so a newer `progress` frame replaces the line. Everything the model wrote is `UntrustedText`.
- **Prompts**: developer **6** (step 4 *Say where you are*: one line after each pushed slice, at least every few minutes of a long step; *Not recorded* is not an error), architect **5** (one line when the reading ends and the plan begins). Eval cases `dev-progress-not-recorded-is-not-a-gap`, `arch-progress-line-is-not-the-plan`. `role-prompts.contract.test.ts` drops `report_progress` from its unbuilt list and now holds every role prompt to naming only platform tools its role is given.
- **Docs**: technical/04 (the amendment under *Streaming and steering*), technical/03 (`run_messages.kind`), technical/08 (`latest_progress`), technical/09 (transcript kinds, the task-detail row), the user guide § 4.

**Decisions and assumptions.**
- **No domain event.** Nothing in the pipeline decides on progress, and the transcript is already streamed; a `run.progress` event would be a second copy with no consumer on an append-only, replayed table.
- **Cut, not refused**, past 500 characters: a refusal costs a turn (backlog 492's lesson), and the model is told the line was shortened.
- **The row is `neutral` for the stall detector**: the tool call that asked for it is already transcribed and re-armed it.
- **`ask` stays without it**: an ask is one turn and the person is reading the answer as it streams.
- **The live panel is the newest non-ended *stage* run**; an ask run has its own thread.
- **`latest_progress` refuses an unreadable row by name** (`UnprojectableRowError`), as `/messages` does, rather than publishing "no progress".

**What of backlog 455 is done**: (1) — a running stage shows a live indicator, its elapsed time and, beyond what 455 asked, its latest progress line. Still open: (2) the timeline newest first, (3) timeline entries linking to their runs, (4) the running stage's whole transcript streaming on the task page.

**Tests.** `packages/application/src/pipeline/progress-tool.test.ts` (bound incl. a property test, the gate's interval and cap, the sentences, no door → refusal); `packages/infrastructure/src/runner/claude-runner.test.ts` › "report_progress (backlog 496)" — the tool called through the real `platform` MCP server mid-run: a redacted row with the run's `seq`, a burst refused, the second line after 30 s, and the serialisation canary; `platform-mcp.test.ts` (the port's sentence, `percent_complete` 101 refused); `postgres-transcript-sink.test.ts` (kind and search text); `platform-tools.test.ts` (composed, bounded, refusal sentence moved to `notify_human`); `transcript.test.ts` (round trip and bounds); `test/integration/server/read-api.integration.test.ts` › "publishes the newest progress line a run reported, and null for one that reported none" (rows through the production sink, migration 0084, `findRun` and the task projection); web `live-stage.test.tsx` (which run is live, newer-`seq` wins, the panel through `createApp`, a live frame replacing the line, hostile text as text, no panel when nothing is live), `blocks.test.ts`, `view.test.tsx`.

**Verification.** `pnpm run -s verify` PASS (536 files, 11 527 tests, coverage ratchet PASS; the first run fell 0.11 points under `apps/server`'s branch threshold and the row mapper got its own unit test); `pnpm test:ui` 56 files, 566 tests; `verify:web-e2e` PASS (51; the first run caught the panel's `aria-label="Live stage"` matching `getByLabel('Stage')` — it reads *Running now*); integration `read-api` and `db/*` (14 files, 123); e2e `run-api`, `agent-run` and `take-over` (10). The whole `verify:e2e` tier was not run.

**Discovered work.**
- No partial index on `run_messages (run_id, seq) where kind = 'progress'`: migration 0084 cannot name the label in the transaction that adds it. `latestProgressFor` walks a run's rows for a run that reported nothing; a second migration can add the index if the task page's read shows up.
- The fake CLI (`fake-spawn.ts`) cannot issue an MCP tool call, so no e2e drives `report_progress` through a whole `apps/server`; the runner unit test calls the registered handler on the real MCP server instead.

Per-stage models are set only in `.agentic/config.yml` (`stages.<id>.model`, `packages/contracts/src/config.ts:227`, also a free string), edited outside the SPA (*"a YAML editor in the browser is not built"*, `docs/user-guide.md:710`). product/03:9, product/10:26 and technical/02:18 promise *"default models"* in org settings; nothing in the SPA serves that today. That is a separate gap, not this entry.
- **The server accepts any id.** `retryRunRequestSchema.model` is `nonEmptyStringSchema.max(128).optional()` (`packages/contracts/src/api.ts:2299`). Its docblock (`:2291-2297`) gives the reason on purpose: *"The platform publishes no list of model ids … because a project may pin a model this build has never heard of — so the override cannot be an enum"*. `retryRunCommand` (`packages/application/src/pipeline/commands.ts:1604`) puts it on the wake-up unchecked, and it reaches the CLI as `Options.model` (`packages/infrastructure/src/runner/options.ts:185`).
- **A typo surfaces at run time, not at the write.** *Hypothesis, needs measurement*: the retry answers 200, a new stage attempt starts, and the CLI or API refuses the unknown model, so that run fails. Nobody has measured what `run.failed` reason, brief and cost row that leaves, or whether the task escalates. The ledger half is known: a model with no `price_list` row gets *no* ledger row and a log line (`packages/application/src/cost/ledger.ts:276-284`). A misspelt id the CLI did accept would therefore run unpriced.

**Where the platform already keeps its ids (the candidate option source, rule 7: not a copy in the SPA).**
- `price_list` (seeded by `packages/infrastructure/src/db/migrations/0009_price_list_seed.sql`: `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5`) is data the operator maintains. It is also the ledger's own definition of a model the platform can charge, so offering exactly its current rows also keeps a person away from an unpriced run. **No route reads it today** (no `price` in `apps/server/src/routes/`).
- The shipped defaults are `STAGE_AGENT_DEFAULTS` / `FALLBACK_STAGE_AGENT_DEFAULTS` (`packages/domain/src/pipeline/templates.ts:55`, `:109`) and `DEFAULT_ASK_MODEL` (`packages/domain/src/ask/ask.ts:37`). Each one is in the seed today, but nothing checks that.

**What it costs to leave.** One failed run and a confused person per typo. The person who asked does not know the ids, so today the box is usable only by copying the placeholder.

**Done when**
1. *Retry run* offers a `<select>` whose options come from the server: the current `price_list` model ids through a read route (new, or a field on an existing DTO), held by `apps/server/src/routes/client-census.test.ts` in both directions. The SPA has no hard-coded list.
2. The run's own model (`record.model`) is preselected. Submitting without changing it sends **no** `model`, so the *"empty means as before"* rule in the comment at `run-detail.tsx:261-263` still holds (the new attempt is re-planned from configuration).
3. A model that is configured but not in the list (an older or custom id, the case the `api.ts` docblock protects) is shown as its own option, labelled as not priced, and kept. It is never replaced silently with the first entry. An *other…* free entry stays, because the API still accepts any id. The field stays a string; it does **not** become an enum.
4. A unit test asserts that every shipped default model id (item 2 of the source list above) has a seed row, so a default cannot drift out of the list.
5. The `api.ts` docblock sentence *"The platform publishes no list of model ids"* and the user guide's retry sentence (`docs/user-guide.md:545`) are amended in the same change (rule 83).
6. *Optional, needs measurement first*: the typo path above is measured and its outcome written here. If it is opaque, the retry route refuses an id that has no `price_list` row unless the person ticks *other…* explicitly.

**Depends on** nothing. **Row**: none of WP-150…WP-157 fits. WP-155 is the onboarding wizard, which asks for no model, and WP-154 touches `live-stage.tsx`/`transcript/view.tsx`, not `run-detail.tsx`. It needs a small SPA + read-route row of its own, or it rides with the next SPA row. Because of `apps/web/src/app/queries.ts` it is serial with WP-154 and WP-155.

### 499. **A push from a linked worktree ran the pre-push unit tier there, and the tests that build scratch git repositories wrote into the real one: `core.bare=true`, `refs/heads/main` moved to fixture commits, tags `v0.1.0`/`v0.5.0` and a branch `side` created, and the main checkout's index replaced** (TODO, **major — it silently corrupts a developer's repository and can create release-shaped tags that `scripts/version.mjs` reads. The cause is unmeasured.** Orchestrator's incident record, session 12, 2026-10-06 13:02–13:05. Refiner, session 12; **no work package owns it**: none of WP-150…WP-157 touches `scripts/` or the test harness)

**What happened (the orchestrator's record, quoted).**
- *"Made a linked worktree (`git worktree add --detach <scratch>/wt-backlog origin/main`), `pnpm install --offline` there, committed backlog 498, `git push origin HEAD:main` -> lefthook pre-push ran unit tier IN THE LINKED WORKTREE."* The hook is `lefthook.yml:31-36` (`pnpm run -s conflict:check`, then `pnpm run -s test`).
- *"54 unit tests failed (scripts/census-files.test.ts, scripts/changelog.test.ts, ... — tests that build temp git repos); e.g. census … received 1973 paths instead of 6 -> their git calls hit the real repo."* The full list of the 54 was not kept.
- Damage to the shared repository: *"core.bare=true in .git/config; refs/heads/main moved to test commits 24411ccb "feat: one" -> 4b3fe7de "f" -> 348091d1 "f" (author f@example.invalid); refs/heads/side and tags v0.1.0/v0.5.0 created; main index replaced by fixture tree (.gitignore '/ignored.ts', notes.md, staged.ts, tracked.ts, src/deep.ts, apps/server/src/routes/patch.ts). Nothing pushed (hook refused before push)."*
- Repair: *"git config core.bare false; git update-ref refs/heads/main 9cc93a45 348091d1; git reset -q (mixed); git branch -D side; git tag -d v0.1.0 v0.5.0; worktree prune. Implementer's working tree untouched."* WP-150's implementer re-ran the integration files it had run in that window (its notes say so).

**Which tests wrote what (read at `9cc93a45`, not run, rule 66).** The artefacts match two files, and only one of them is in the record's list:
- `scripts/census-files.test.ts`: the index fixture and the `f` commits. Its scratch repository writes `.gitignore` = `/ignored.ts`, `tracked.ts`, `staged.ts`, `src/deep.ts`, `notes.md` (`:41-48`) and commits as `user.email=f@example.invalid`, message `f` (`:49`). Its production-import case adds `apps/server/src/routes/…` (`:176-183`).
- `scripts/version.test.ts`: `feat: one` and the tags and branch. It builds histories such as `['feat: one', 'tag:v0.1.0']` (`:210`), and its other-branch case runs `checkout -b side` and `tag v0.5.0` (`:214-218`).
- `scripts/changelog.test.ts` was in the failing list. Nothing in the record's damage is uniquely its own.
- Nothing in the test sources sets `core.bare` (grep: only `deploy-key-check.mjs`, the Docker workspace e2e support and `provider.ts`, none of them unit tier). How it became `true` is part of the unmeasured cause.

**How those tests build a git child's environment (read, not run).** None removes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` or `GIT_COMMON_DIR`. A `cwd` does not help, because git honours `GIT_DIR` before it searches from the working directory.
- **No `env` at all, so the whole parent environment is inherited**: `scripts/census-files.test.ts:179`, `scripts/changelog.test.ts:126-140` and `:484-499`, `scripts/version.test.ts:161-179`.
- **`...process.env` plus `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` (and an author)**: `scripts/census-files.test.ts:35-38`, `scripts/check-conflict.test.ts:49-56`, `scripts/check-ignored.test.ts:48-55`, `scripts/check-nul.test.ts:40-47`, `scripts/gitleaks.test.ts:46-53`, `scripts/nested-checkouts.test.ts:81-88`, `scripts/check-data-model.test.ts:214-221`. The scripts under test (`check-*.mjs`) are spawned with the same environment, and they run `git` themselves (`scripts/census-files.mjs:49`).
- `packages/infrastructure/src/workspace/tracked.test.ts:220` runs a shell script with `...process.env`.
- **Scrubbed**: only `scripts/changelog.test.ts:513-516`, which runs `changelog.mjs` with `env: { PATH }`. Production already has the shape this needs: `gitEnvironment` builds a git child's environment from an allow-list (`packages/infrastructure/src/knowledge/git-vault.ts:231-256`).
- Outside the unit tier, the same exposure exists for any caller with `GIT_*` set: the integration and e2e files that spawn `git` (`test/integration/knowledge/git-vault-index.integration.test.ts`, `test/integration/server/default-branch-reads.integration.test.ts`, `test/integration/config/prompt-reread.integration.test.ts`, six under `test/e2e/onboarding/` and `test/e2e/pipeline/`).

**The cause is unmeasured. Hypothesis:** git exports repository-locating variables into a hook's environment, and the tests' `git` children inherited them instead of discovering their scratch repository. What does not fit a simple version of this: a `GIT_DIR` naming the linked worktree's own git directory (`.git/worktrees/wt-backlog`) would explain the shared refs, tags and config. It would not explain the **main checkout's** index (`.git/index`) being replaced. So either the value pointed at the common directory, or `GIT_INDEX_FILE` was set, or something else redirected the writes. Nobody recorded the hook's environment, and the worktree was pruned in the repair, so this cannot be read back. **Needs measurement** (item 1 below).
Whether a tier run **directly** in a linked worktree (an ordinary shell, no hook) is exposed is also unmeasured. An ordinary shell exports no `GIT_*`, so probably not. But `git worktree list` shows 17 agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` today, and technical/14:17 sends parallel implementers into isolated worktrees, so this is not a rare configuration.

**What it costs to leave.**
- The repository is corrupted silently, and the failure looks like a test failure. Here 54 tests failed and the hook refused the push. A run where the redirected writes did not break any assertion would push with nothing visible.
- Local tags `v0.1.0`/`v0.5.0` change what `scripts/version.mjs:129` (`latestReleaseTag(releaseTags(root))`) and `pnpm changelog` compute on that machine. A `git push --tags` or `--follow-tags` would publish them, and CI's `version` job reads tags from the remote.
- A moved `refs/heads/main` makes the next push from the main checkout offer fixture commits. The remote refuses that as non-fast-forward unless the push is forced.
- A concurrent implementer's tiers run on corrupted git state for as long as it lasts. That happened to WP-150's integration files.

**Done when**
1. **Measure first, never in this repository.** Use a throwaway clone with a local bare remote and a linked worktree whose `pre-push` hook writes `env | grep '^GIT_'` to a file. Push once with plain git hooks and once under lefthook. Record each `GIT_*` name and value here. Then run one fixture suite (`scripts/census-files.test.ts`) from that hook and record which of the throwaway repository's config, refs and index change. That run is the canary for item 4.
2. **One helper** builds every test's git child environment for a scratch repository. It drops **every** inherited name with the `GIT_` prefix: a prefix rule, not a list of known names, because git reads many (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_NAMESPACE`, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_CONFIG_*` …). It then adds back the fixture's own values (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` = `/dev/null`, author and committer, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`). Every site listed above uses it, including the scripts the tests spawn. A second guard is wanted beside the scrub: after `git init`, the helper checks that `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` is inside the scratch root and throws otherwise, so a test that would act on another repository fails before its first write.
3. **A census** refuses a `git` spawn in any test file (unit, integration and e2e tiers) whose options do not take the helper's environment. It reads files through `scripts/census-files.mjs`, tracked and untracked, as the other censuses do. Its docblock lists what it cannot see (a `git` inside a shell string, as `tracked.test.ts:220` uses through `trackedListingScript`; a command name held in a variable). Canary: revert one site and the census fails.
4. **A reproduction** that fails on today's tree. A process-tier case, or a script the orchestrator runs, points `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` at a throwaway repository, runs the fixture suites, and asserts that repository's config, refs and index are byte-identical afterwards. Ideally it goes through a real linked worktree's hook, per item 1.
5. The proposed standing rule below is retired in the same change.

**Proposed standing rule, for the orchestrator to adopt (as rule 95; not added to the rules section by the refiner):** *"**Never run a test tier, and never push, from a linked worktree of this repository until backlog 499 is fixed.** On 2026-10-06 a push from a linked worktree ran the pre-push unit tier there, and the tests that build scratch git repositories wrote into the real one: `core.bare=true`, `main` moved to fixture commits, tags `v0.1.0`/`v0.5.0` and a branch `side` created, and the main checkout's index replaced. A docs commit waits for the main tree (rule 90). A parallel implementer in a worktree (technical/14 step 3) hands its branch to the main tree for every tier run and every push. After any push or tier run that fails strangely, check `git config core.bare`, `git rev-parse main`, `git tag -l 'v*'` and `git branch` before doing anything else."*

**Depends on** nothing. Until it is fixed, technical/14:17's worktree parallelism is limited by the rule above. That limit is the orchestrator's to state in its brief, not a protocol amendment made here.
