#### WP-116 — review round 1 (APPROVE with nits), fixed by the orchestrator

- **(minor)** The lookalike table in `scripts/e2e-harness-volumes.test.ts` had no **container** that carries a creator pid but no marker (the volume and network kinds had one), so a canary dropping the marker filter in `test/e2e/support/harness-volumes.ts` killed the volume and network cases and not the container one — `agentic-e2e-repo-zzzzzz` has no labels at all, so the pid test rejected it first. The file alone 7/7.
- **(nit, recorded)** `spawnCreator`'s child exits by itself after 120 s, so a `docker run` slower than that (an image pull) would reopen the parallel-sweep race; a worker killed with SIGKILL leaves the child for at most 120 s, and the lookalike containers sleep 600 s with nothing sweeping them after a killed run (backlog 394's class).
- **(nit, recorded)** The daemon double accepts `container rm` without `-f` for a running container, which the real daemon refuses — kinder (rule 1), but the exact removal string `container rm -f -v …` is pinned, so a canary dropping `-f` still dies.
- Round 1 confirmed every new wait binds the last row the platform writes with its before-state asserted, and that criterion (2)'s `mr.updated` half was already met by `test/e2e/pipeline/review-threads-refresh.e2e.test.ts` › "re-counts the threads once per signal, open and then resolved", clause by clause.

### Architect ruling (M8 additions, session 11) — three rows, and the merge request comes first

Written 2026-10-03 at `d07ae04`, about 18 h before the product owner's first local test on Autix
(**gitlab.com Free** + Jira Cloud, `local` mode on a Mac, a **poll-only** GitLab binding,
`docs/first-local-test.md`). Read off the code; nothing was run. Three things stand between that test
and a first merge request, and the plan's M8 table carries one row for each, **in this order**:

1. **WP-138 — the Developer opens and updates its merge request.** Found by the orchestrator:
   `open_mr` and `update_mr_description` refuse by name (`apps/server/src/platform-tools.ts:140-141`)
   while the developer prompt and `ImplementationNotes` require a merge request, so the first feature
   ticket fails at Implementation (backlog 51's trigger, now owned). The ruling, in the row: the
   executor for both tools (shadow → `would_have`); the tool call is already the *call* half of WP-15d's
   split because it runs in `stage.execute`'s no-transaction phase; source branch = `tasks.branch`,
   target = `projects.default_branch` (Autix's `develop`), never the model's; one merge request per task
   and branch (executor key plus adopting an existing open one only when it is ours); title and
   description bounded, redacted, footer appended; `tasks.mr_ref` written by a narrow compare-and-set
   method and no longer from the model's artifact. Two further rulings it carries because Autix's CI
   exposes them: **a head with no pipeline is not "no CI"** when the default branch has a
   `.gitlab-ci.yml` (today `ci_gate` passes it, `gates.ts:490-493` — on Autix, whose MR pipelines are
   skipped for a `Draft:` title, that is a pass with no evidence), and **ready before CI** (an outbound
   duty undrafts at the Developer stage's completion and creates a merge-request pipeline when the head
   has none). Branch names stay `agentic/*` (**Q114** filed with that recommendation); the runbook tells
   the operator to admit `agentic/` in Autix's `^(feature|bugfix)/` rule.
2. **WP-137 — a static run credential**, the founder's answer to **Q98 (b)** (moved to *Answered by the
   founder (session 11, 2026-10-03)* in `docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`). Recorded as dated amendments:
   BD-025 (§3's exception, opt-in and named), TD-028 (**decision 13**, and an in-place note on decision
   6), TD-021 (same path, stated loss). Declared on the GitLab integration as `run_credential: static`
   plus a separate secret field `run_token` (a dedicated user's personal access token, Developer on that
   one project, `read_repository` + `write_repository`, expiry ≤ 90 days and declared); it reaches a run
   exactly as a minted token does (create request → launcher broker map → runner's `cred.get`), joins the
   run's redactors, is never used for platform API calls, is never given to a shadow task, and its use is
   recorded as `runs.credential_source`. **Lost, stated**: no per-run revocation, a lifetime of weeks, a
   push-capable token in read-only stages, and a token the agent pushes into the repository still works;
   the platform's one added control is an exact-value search of the merge request's added lines.
   Without this row no stage can fetch Autix's private repository — which is why it is second only to
   the row that makes a merge request exist.
3. **WP-136 — the CI gate on a poll-only binding waits up to a CI timeout** (the product owner's
   decision). Time-bounded from `task_stages.entered_at`, re-read on every fire (TD-004), 30 s for five
   checks then 60 s, a backstop count, only for `ci_gate` on a binding that receives no webhooks;
   `pipeline.limits.ci_timeout_minutes`, 10–1440, default **60** because GitLab's own default job
   timeout is 60 minutes (research/10's 2026-10-03 addendum). The brief names the timeout and the key.
   Until it lands, the runbook's hand-back at `ci_gate` is the workaround.

**The stack answer.** Autix is PHP + Composer and its GitLab CI covers it, so the run image is **not**
changed: agents edit and push, and the pipeline is the evidence. Two consequences the product owner
should expect and the runbook should say: discovery cannot run the PHP suite in the run image, so the
readiness criteria that need a local run (R1, R2) read as not detected; and the Developer's
`commands_run` will show no local test run — which is exactly why WP-138's *no pipeline is not no CI*
ruling matters.

**Verification added.** `docs/TODO.md` gains two rows (the draft/undraft pipeline behaviour, owner
WP-138; the gitlab.com Free static-credential run, the product owner's), and research/10 an addendum
with the personal-access-token tiers, GitLab's job timeout and the merge-request pipeline endpoint (one
line `[unverified]`).

### Architect ruling (M8 round 3, session 11) — seven rows, and the measurement that costs nothing comes first

Written 2026-10-04 at `7960d3f`, M8's eight rows DONE, about 10 h before the product owner's first test on
Autix (gitlab.com Free, poll-only, Jira Cloud, `local` mode). Read off the tree and the decisions; nothing
was run. The founder answered four things that day (recorded in `docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` § "Answered by
the founder (session 11, 2026-10-04)"), and the plan's M8 table gains one row per piece of work, **in
order of value to the test**:

1. **WP-140 — the real-model pre-flight (Q115).** The founder allows one bounded run with their
   subscription token *"if it will not cost anything"*: no per-token charge, but it counts toward the
   plan's limits, so it is **one** tiny turn with no tools and no retry. It supersedes M8's *no model
   credential* sentence for this row only. It is a flag-gated leg of the launcher check on its own
   disposable fixture, so it cannot write to GitLab or Jira by construction; the token is read from the
   environment only and asserted absent from every output. It closes backlog 137's post-login half — the
   hosts a logged-in CLI contacts — with the open sub-question of whether tinyproxy's log shows allowed
   `CONNECT`s at all (measure first). If the orchestrator's shell has no token, the leg ships and running
   it is the product owner's one command.
2. **WP-141 — the operator's own repository-only token (TD-028 decision 13a).** The probe's
   "Developer at most" refusal becomes, for `run_token_owner: operator`, a **scope proof** (`GET /user`
   with the run token must be refused) plus a **protection check** with the API token (default branch,
   push "No one", no force push, re-read before each such run). The argument for allowing a Maintainer's
   token: protection, membership and settings are API operations, which a repository-only token cannot
   perform; what remains is git, which the protection bounds. The loss is reach — every repository the
   user can access — stated beside the setting.
3. **WP-142 — one default branch (441, with 442's index and intake-lock halves).** The stored
   `projects.default_branch` is the only answer; the provider's default is read by the wizard's prefill
   and a mismatch **notice**, never a refusal, because the product owner's `develop` → `main` move passes
   through a moment where the two differ. A change resets the poll's default-head baseline so it records
   no spurious move.
4. **WP-143 — the CI-rules readiness warning (Q114).** A warning, not a fifteenth criterion; a pure
   evaluator of `workflow:rules`, `rules:` and `only`/`except` in a push and a merge-request context for
   `agentic/X-1`; anything it cannot read (`include:`, `extends`, `!reference`, `changes:`, `exists:`,
   unknown variables, external CI paths) yields a note, never a warning, so a false alarm needs a rule the
   evaluator fully understood.
5. **WP-144 — a stop hands the run back (432).** SIGTERM aborts the session, ends the run with the new
   reason `shutdown`, releases its reservation, destroys the workspace and re-enqueues the same stage
   entry in the run's ending transaction; twice per stage entry, then the brief. A crash is unchanged
   (the lease sweep escalates), stated.
6. **WP-145 — Jira edits after a move (437).** Update signals match by the issue id first; a matched
   key change updates the task's key narrowly; the poll re-reads by id. Branch and MR keep the old key.
7. **WP-146 — the SSH deploy key (TD-028 decision 13b).** The key **never enters a run container**: the
   shim serves an ssh-agent socket on `/ctl` whose sign requests the runner answers, so the container
   holds a signing oracle for the run's lifetime and nothing after it. SSH reaches gitlab.com as
   `CONNECT altssh.gitlab.com:443` through the existing sidecar; no port 22, because tinyproxy's
   `ConnectPort` is global — so a self-managed host is refused by name. `known_hosts` comes from the
   documented keys (research/10's 2026-10-04 addendum; altssh's keys measured first). The platform's
   vault mirror keeps HTTPS with the binding token; the launcher's mirror helper holds the key on tmpfs,
   the same class as its `GIT_PASS` today. **It may land after the test starts** — WP-141 (or WP-137)
   serves the test until then, and the runbook should say which to pick today.

**Decisions amended** (dated 2026-10-04): TD-028 (decisions 13a and 13b), BD-025 (the operator chooses
which static form, including their own), TD-021 (the agent socket, the egress host, the mirror helper).
**Verification added**: four `docs/TODO.md` rows (post-login hosts; the `GET /user` refusal shape;
altssh's host keys and a deploy-key push through `CONNECT`; JQL by id after a move) and research/10's

- **Criterion (1), measured before the fix** (rule 76, on a copy of the case — `test/e2e/server/zz-wp119-measure.e2e.test.ts`, deleted — with a state dump on timeout; the production edits were Edit-tool canaries behind an environment switch, reverted with the Edit tool, md5 `f74a694a…` and `a2eaa107…` restored). One run each, load 3–6:
  - **Unchanged**: green in 9.9 s. The dump already shows the race: the run ended `cancelled` with `usd_reported = 0.40` — the scripted session's **full** cost — so the stop landed after the session's own `result`, inside the runner's transcript flush.
  - **Heartbeat delayed past the wait** (`renewEveryMs` 200 s, notify intact): green, the same dump. The heartbeat is never on this path: `RUN_LEASE_RENEW_MS` is 100 s, already past the 90 s wait.
  - **`pg_notify` wake-up dropped**: **reproduces 391 exactly** — timeout after 90 s (96 s wall), *"the task is state=paused stage=refinement"*; the run `completed`/`success` at 0.40, the cancel refused `run_ended`.
  - **Wake-up delayed 3 s** (a third reading, the load-shaped one): **reproduces it the same way.**
  - **Cause**: the case released the held run (`held.open()`) before the stop was applied, so the stop raced the scripted session's whole lifetime; any notification latency longer than that session — load, a reconnecting `LISTEN` — lets the run end `completed`, a status the wait's `cancelled` can never reach, and the only other path (the heartbeat) is slower than the wait. Not a product defect: a cancel that loses to the session's own ending is closed `run_ended`, as designed.
  - **Fix (the wait, never a timeout)**: the case now waits for the cancel's `run_commands` row to read `applied` **before** releasing the hold, so the stop is parked on the provisioning handle and the session is stopped at its start. On the copy, with the fix: green unchanged, and green with the wake-up delayed 3 s. With the wake-up dropped it would wait for the 100 s heartbeat and fail by the new wait's name, which is the bound the product documents.

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed).
- **The organisation and project caps do not add the admitting run's reserve.** `createBudgetGuard` refuses only an exhausted window (`spent + pending + held >= limit`), while the shadow, maintenance, bootstrap and task caps compare `… + reserve > cap`. So an org or project budget admits a run that may take it past its limit by up to that run's per-run cap — the over-admission rule 89 names, on the admitting run rather than on the runs before it. Read off the tree; BD-010's *"prevents new runs"* wording may intend it. Needs a ruling (it changes two caps' comparison).
- **A `cost_unreported` run is written as a measured `usd_reported = 0`** (`claude-runner.ts`'s floor, then `rowCostOf`), so it is neither held nor counted until the ledger prices it from its tokens — and a model with no price row is never priced. Read, not run; rule 16's neighbour, outside this row's set (both cost columns are not null).
- **The board card prints `cost_actual_usd` with no exclusion line** (`apps/web/src/features/board.tsx:104`). 403's *Done* names the task page and the notification only; the card is the third place the measured total is shown.
- **`test/integration/bootstrap/postgres-history-bootstrap-store.integration.test.ts` cleans up outside `finally`**, so a failure in "values a batch’s runs the ledger has not recorded, and stops once it has" leaves its batch row and the next case fails on `history_bootstrap_batches_one_live` — a cascade that names the wrong test (seen once, under a canary).

**Residuals.**
- A run swept or cancelled before its process spawned is held at its cap until its window rolls over (or, for the task cap, until a human raises the cap): the row cannot prove the spawn never happened (criterion (6)).
- The task cap's hold never rolls over, by the ruling: a task whose run ended unmeasured and whose process died stays held until a human raises its cap.
- How often a real run ends unmeasured is still not measured (WP-33's credential).

#### WP-131 — pre-review round (406, 407, 410)

The orchestrator folded three of the refiner's entries into this row.

- **406 — the org and project caps now make the other caps' comparison (orchestrator's ruling).** `createBudgetGuard` refuses when `spent + pending + held + the admitted run's reservation > limit` (`capIsSpent`, so a run that exactly fills the window is admitted). It **also** still refuses any run once the window is used up (`spent + pending + held >= limit`), so a caller that may spend nothing (`reserveUsd` 0) is still refused at an exhausted window. `BlockingBudget.reserveUsd` is new, and `blockingBudgetDetail` no longer says *"is exhausted"* about a window that is not: *"the project budget for this month cannot take this run: 10 spent of 20 USD since …, and this run may spend 10.01 more"*. The guard's WP-131 cases lose their extra 5 USD charge and use the row's figures. - **410 — no column proves the CLI was never spawned, so the hold stays** (the ruling's own fallback). What the row records, and when:
  - `lease_owner`/`lease_expires_at` are claimed in the transaction that inserts the row.
  - `started_at` is the domain clock at that insert.
  - `run.started` is appended in the same transaction.
  - `session_id` is written only at the ending.
  So all four predate provisioning, and an in-place cancel or a sweep of a pre-spawn run leaves them looking exactly like a run that spawned. Nothing is written *at* the spawn. The shim spawns inside the run's container, and the launcher records no spawn in the database.
  The nearest marker is the transcript's `system`/`init` row. It is written by the runner from the CLI's own stream, and a sink failure fails the run (`postgres-transcript-sink.ts` decision 2), so its **presence** proves the CLI spawned and spoke. Its **absence** does not prove the converse, for three reasons:
  - a CLI that spawned and died, or was cut off, before its first line leaves no row;
  - the `init` insert races the CLI's first model request (the CLI does not wait for the platform to persist its line), so a runner process that dies in that window leaves no row for a session that may already be spending;
  - an `init` entry that fails validation is stored as `transcript_normalisation_failed`.
  Excluding on its absence would count 0 for runs that may have spent: the fail-open direction rule 20 and the ruling refuse. The case each way is therefore not written. 410's own remedy stands: a marker committed **before** the launcher's `create` (its absence then proves no spawn), which needs the provisioning path to write the database or the launcher to report back. That is a launcher/provisioner change (TD-028), not this row's. Recorded in technical/03's WP-131 implementation note.

#### WP-120

**What a project command or a template can still walk past** — backlogs 343 and 338. Implementer, session 11.

**Decisions and assumptions.**

- **343: the spellings were read off the sources, not run.** go and pytest are not installed on this machine, and the brief allowed running them only if they were. The sources are go1.25.0, pytest 9.0.2 and pytest-cov 7.1.0, at their tags. Python's own `argparse` (3.14.6) **was** run with pytest's `-o` and `--debug` declarations copied. The spellings and the URLs are recorded under backlog 343 and in the comment above the new entries.
- **Ten new `HAZARDOUS_ARGUMENTS` entries, floored always.**
  - **Seven go entries**, one per flag in `GO_PATH_WRITING_TEST_FLAGS`. Each is token-scoped by its exact name: `^--?(?:test\.)?<name>(?:=|$)` on a `go*` binary. It is not a `go* -memprofile*` glob, because that would also floor `-memprofilerate`, `-blockprofilerate` and `-mutexprofilefraction`, which are different flags; go does not match prefixes.
  - **`-o`/`--override-ini` is floored for every key, not only `cache_dir`.** This is the same reasoning as pnpm's `--config.<key>`. The override sets any ini key, `log_file` writes a path, and `addopts` is read from the overridden configuration (`findpaths.py` merges before `getini("addopts")`). So `-o addopts=--basetemp=tests` re-adds any floored flag, and no whole-line or token match sees it. Over-block: `pytest -o xfail_strict=true` asks.
  - **The short-option cluster is scanned** (`-qo k=v`, `-vqok=v`). The scan stops at a value-taking short option (`k m c p W r`), because argparse gives such an option the rest of its token. So `-knot_slow` and `-p no:cacheprovider` stay `allow`.
  - **`pytest* --debug*`** floors even a bare `--debug`. argparse's `nargs="?"` takes the next word, so `--debug tests/conftest.py` truncates that file. A bare `--debug` writes `pytestdebug.log`, and that over-block is stated.
  - **`--cov-report` is floored only with a `:DEST`**, either `--cov-report=xml:p` or `--cov-report xml:p`, for the seven kinds pytest-cov allows a destination. `term-missing` and a bare `xml` write a configured default path, which is repository content. Over-block: `--cov-report=xml:coverage.xml` asks. The space form is matched by "the flag is present and some positional starts with `<kind>:`", because `splitFlags` keeps no order. That can over-match a test id that looks like `xml:…`, which is the safe direction.
- **338: the invariant, not only the ruling's one shape.** `unconfirmedCiExcuseIssue` refuses an enabled `ci_gate` that has no enabled `rebase_gate` declared **after** it. That covers three shapes:
  - disabled, which is the ruling's case;
  - missing;
  - declared before `ci_gate`.

  Each is the same unconfirmed fall-through, and the message names both stages and says which shape it is. **Assumption:** this widens (a) only to shapes no build produces today. If the reviewer wants the literal ruling only, the change is the `rebase > ci` test plus one branch of the message. A template with no enabled `ci_gate` passes, because nothing then writes an excuse. The check runs in `assertValidTemplate`, and so at every `compilePipeline`. The dial disables only `business_review` and is applied after the check, which is irrelevant here. The docblock and technical/02 state that a future `stages.<s>.enabled` reader must apply the flag **before** `assertValidTemplate`.
- **BD-025** already says the floor is "an enumeration of known spellings, not a boundary", but about command strings. Proposed text for the orchestrator to append after "…a spelling nobody enumerated reaches `allow`." in BD-025's WP-54 paragraph: *"The same is true of the floors on flags that write a path the model chose (`--basetemp`, `--junitxml`, `go test -o` and the profile outputs, `cargo --target-dir`, pytest's `-o`, `--debug` and `--cov-report=<kind>:<dest>`; WP-104 and WP-120): they are an enumeration, the known unfloored ones are named at `PROJECT_COMMAND_ALLOW`, and a file of arguments (`pytest @<file>`) is the repository-content route."*

**1. Arguments and configuration read from a file.**
- **`@<file>`, floored.** `fromfile_prefix_chars="@"` is set at `src/_pytest/config/argparsing.py:463` (`PytestArgumentParser.__init__`). Run through `argparse`, `@args.txt` holding `--basetemp=tests` set `basetemp`, alone and after `-q`. After `-k` it was expanded too, and became `-k`'s value. After `--` it was expanded into a positional. So the floor matches any dequoted token starting with `@`, flag or positional, on a `pytest*` binary.
- **`-c`/`--config-file`, floored.** It is declared at `src/_pytest/main.py:251-258` (`dest="inifilename"`), and `config/findpaths.py` `determine_setup` loads the file as the configuration, `addopts` included. These spellings set it: `-c x`, `-cx`, `-c=x`, `--config-file x`, `--config-file=x`, `-qc x` and `-qcx`. `--config x` does not. The short-cluster scan is now one function, `pytestClusterValueOption`, which returns the first value-taking letter (`k m c p o W r`). `-o` floors on `o` and `-c` on `c`.
- **`--rootdir`, floored, but as a path writer, not a reader.** `determine_setup` locates the ini file from the **arguments** whether or not `--rootdir` is given. `--rootdir` only replaces the rootdir, and `cacheprovider.py:107` resolves `cache_dir` against it. So `--rootdir=tests` writes `.pytest_cache` (README, `.gitignore`, `CACHEDIR.TAG`, `v/…`) under `tests/`.
- **`--confcutdir`, not floored.** It is `directory_arg`, and it only limits which `conftest.py` files load. It reads no configuration and writes nothing.
- **The residual, stated at the docblock and technical/04.** `locate_config` searches each argument and its parents for `pytest.toml`, `.pytest.toml`, `pytest.ini`, `.pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `tox.ini` and `setup.cfg`. So `pytest sub/` reads a `sub/pytest.ini` the agent wrote, `addopts` included. No floor can tell that line from `pytest tests/`. It is the repository-content route, BD-025's accepted residual.

**2. The rest of the list.**
- **pytest `--log-file`.** Declared at `logging.py:293`. It is opened with `--log-file-mode`, default `w`, so `--log-file=tests/conftest.py` truncates a protected file. Matched by exact name, so `--log-file-level`/`-mode`/`-format` stay `allow`.

- **go `-pkgdir`, `-debug-trace`, `-debug-actiongraph`, `-debug-runtime-trace`** (`GO_PATH_WRITING_BUILD_FLAGS`):

  - write there: `work/init.go` `os.Create`/`trace.Start`, `work/exec.go`, and `go help build`'s `-pkgdir`;

- **Correction to 343's widening note.** `--cache-clear` does not delete the whole cache directory: `clear_cache` removes `<cache_dir>/d` and `<cache_dir>/v` only. With `-o cache_dir=tests` it deletes `tests/d` and `tests/v`. The `-o` entry's hazard text now says so.

**3. The widened 338 check is kept.** It is stated at `assertValidTemplate`'s docblock and in technical/02 as wider than the ruling and fail-closed.

**4. `.pytest_cache` with no ini file: it cannot land in `tests/` on its own.** I read the source, not a run. `determine_setup` with no ini and no `setup.py` sets rootdir to `get_common_ancestor(invocation_dir, [invocation_dir, ancestor])`, which is the checkout root for any arguments under it. `cd` is not an allowed verb, so a run's pytest is invoked from the checkout. The cache lands under `tests/` only in three cases:
- a `--rootdir` pointing there (floored now);
- `-o cache_dir`/`-c` (floored);
- an ini file located in `tests/` by the arguments.

That last case is either the repository's own configuration or a file the guard judged when it was written. Even then the cache writes only **new** files (`_ensure_cache_dir_and_supporting_files` returns early if the directory exists). It writes its own `*` `.gitignore`, so nothing it writes is committed, and WP-81's tamper check is unaffected. So `-p cacheprovider` is not floored: re-enabling the cache changes nothing above.

Decisions and assumptions (each is also stated at the code):

- **(1) One migration, `0073_reading_redaction_mark.sql`.** `project_repository_config.prompts_redaction` is added `not null default 'patterns'`, which marks every existing row, and the default is then **dropped**: a writer that forgets the column fails rather than marking a reading it did not redact. A check holds it to `patterns`/`exact`. `prompts_withheld jsonb` is `{reason, integrations: [{integration, reason}]}` or `null`, with a shape check and a second check (`withheld_has_no_prompts`) so a withheld record and stored prompt text never sit together. `runs.prompts_withheld` has the same shape check. Applied migrations are untouched.
- **The mark is read in one place.** Every reader of a stored reading (the store, the pipeline's settings port, `GET …/config`, the Librarian's read) goes through `snapshotOfRow` (`packages/infrastructure/src/config/postgres-repository-config-store.ts`). A row whose mark is not `exact` is answered with **no** prompts and with `promptsWithheld`: the re-read's recorded failure if there is one, else `PATTERN_READING_WITHHELD_REASON`. A missing or unknown mark reads as `patterns` (rule 20); only a hand-built caller row can lack the column. **Assumption:** a `patterns` row serves no prompt text even **before** the re-read has tried it, not only after a failed re-read. TD-012's M7 amendment says *"a stale copy that may hold a credential is withheld, never served"*, and the ruling's narrower sentence (*"that cannot be re-read"*) is the case the reason is recorded for. Until the pass reaches a project, its stages run without their prompt files.
- **`RepositoryConfigStore.record` writes `exact` on every insert and update.** Its one caller, `refreshRepositoryConfig`, has run both steps over everything the snapshot holds. The port's docblock says so.
- **The re-read** (`packages/application/src/config/prompt-reread.ts`): `rereadPatternReadings` reads up to `PATTERN_REREAD_BATCH` (8) `patterns` projects, oldest reading first, through the same refresher an index run uses (no commit pinned: the default branch's head). An outcome other than `recorded` (`unavailable`, `stale`, or a throw) is recorded through `PatternReadingStore.withholdPatternReading`. That drops the row's prompts, stores the reason (pattern-redacted, one line, cause bounded at 400 characters) and **keeps the mark**, so the next index run or refresh still replaces the row. It never throws for one project. `startPatternReadingReread` loops passes with a 1 s pause, excluding **every project it has touched** (re-read or failed) for the process lifetime, so it ends at the first pass that is not full, even if a writer left a row `patterns`. It is composed in `composeKnowledgeIndexing` after the index runtime starts, so it runs in every process that runs the index (`ROLE=all`, `worker`, `indexer`) and in the background. `ComposedKnowledgeIndexing.patternReread` is a labelled seam the integration case awaits, and `stop` ends the loop first. **Assumption:** the pass runs at every process start, not once per installation. The mark is set only by migration 0073, so after the first successful start there is nothing left to do but failures, and retrying those once per start is the intent.

For every binding and every live communication account it adds the decrypted `secret_ids` and every declared secret field found as a non-empty string in the configuration (`integrations.config` with `bindings.config` over it). Names are `<provider>:<integrationId>:<field>`. A config-held copy equal to the sealed value is kept once. One that differs gets `…:<field>.config`, because a placeholder name is an identity (`exactSecretRedactor`). A project bound to the org account is one entry. **Assumption, stated at the code:** an organisation account whose credentials will not decrypt is `unreadable` like a binding, so it withholds **every** project's prompt texts until repaired. That is the fail-closed direction WP-107 chose, now at organisation scope. Config fields are read even for an integration whose sealed credentials failed.

The record's strings go through both redaction steps before they are stored. `ProjectSettings.repositoryPromptsWithheld` carries it to the stage executor, which freezes it, through the run's own redactor, on `NewRun.promptsWithheld` → `runs.prompts_withheld`. `NewRun.promptsWithheld` is **required** (every insert site and fixture updated, write-only like the prompt columns, dropped by the memory store). #### WP-122

**Start a ticket by hand, download the task record, and an outage that reads as a missing role** — backlog 379, 381, 385 and 388. Implementer, session 11, on `31179e5`. No migration; `pnpm schemas` unchanged (`schemas/` generates no API DTO).

Decisions and assumptions (each is also stated at the code):

- **379 — the command is the application ring's** (`packages/application/src/pipeline/manual-start.ts`, `startTicketManually`). Outside any transaction it resolves the project's bindings (`integrationsForProject`, `noRunScopedSecrets()`) and reads the ticket through `ticketReads(...).ticket` — the task-management binding and the process's one `IntegrationActionExecutor`. Then `appendOnProjectWithRetry` runs **one transaction**: it re-asks `findByTicket`, appends the same `ticket.matched` intake consumes (`rule: 'manual'`, actor `{kind: 'user'}`, the provider's **own** `ticket.ref`, never the typed key or the read's placeholder URL) and calls the caller's `record`, which writes the `human_actions` row `task.start`. A lost project-stream race repeats only the transaction, never the read. `rule` is a free string in `ticketMatchedEvent`, so no contracts change and nothing to replay.
- **The payload is redacted by the binding's redactor before it is built** — the poller's rule (`ticket-poll.ts`), because events are append-only. Only the fields a webhook match carries are stored (ref, priority, issue type, epic key, links); the ticket's text is intake's own read (`tasks.ticket_snapshot`).
- **The Idempotency-Key is claimed before the read** (`claimIdempotentAttempt`, WP-67's claim-before-effect), so a replay reads nothing and records nothing and a concurrent repeat is `409 idempotency_key_in_flight`. The claim is **completed inside the match's transaction** by `recordHumanActionInTransaction` (`apps/server/src/queries/onboarding-queries.ts`, raw SQL on the transaction's client: the audit insert plus `completeCommandAttempt`'s upsert). `claimIdempotentAttemptInTransaction` could not serve: its `on conflict do nothing` answers `false` for the claim this route already took. A replay answers `202 {performed: false}` from the audit row's `event_id` and `ticket`, and refuses (`409 idempotency_key_reused`) rather than inventing when they cannot be read — the shadow batch's rule.
- **Refusals, each typed and recording nothing.** `no_task_management` → `409 no_task_management_binding`; `task_exists` → `409 ticket_has_task` (asked before the read **and** inside the append; two concurrent different-key starts that both pass are absorbed by intake's own `findByTicket`, the ruling's backstop); `ticket_not_found` → `404 ticket_not_found` (an `IntegrationError` `not_found` from the provider); **`ticket_unreadable` → `502`** for any other provider failure — a mutation fails closed (rule 20), with only the error's code in the answer and the provider's words in the log. **Assumption: a fourth refusal, `not_picked_up` → `409 project_does_not_pick_up_tickets`**, for a project whose autonomy dial does not pick up new tickets (Observe). Intake's check drops such a match **without a word** (`saga.ts`), so the ruling's "nothing else is bypassed" would otherwise answer `202` for a ticket nothing will ever start (rule 18). The predicate is now one function, `picksUpNewTickets` (`pipeline/settings.ts`), asked by intake and by the start, so the two cannot disagree (rule 9). Four lost project-stream races answer the existing `409 project_stream_contended`.
- **Classification, WIP, protected branch, refused configuration: unchanged and not re-implemented.** The start records a match and returns; intake decides. So above the WIP limit the task is `queued`, an unprotected default branch escalates at intake, a refused configuration parks at the first step (WP-106), and WP-131's admission and caps are untouched. *Blocked-ticket links*: intake reads no link today; the start carries the ticket's links in the payload exactly as a webhook match does, so whatever reads them later reads both.
- **The body is `{ticket_key}` only.** `createTaskRequestSchema` carried `template` and `mode` from before anything served it; both are removed (a template override would bypass classification, and a shadow task has its own command). The key is `ticketKeyInputSchema`: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 (`MAX_TICKET_KEY_CHARS`) — refused, never escaped (rules 13/37), because it reaches a provider's URL path.
- **Composition.** `createTaskStartCommands` (`apps/server/src/task-start.ts`) on every process that serves the API and composed the integration stack, over `createProjectIntegrationsPort` (the shadow batch's loader). It needs **no** job client: the event is dispatched like any other, so `ROLE=api` serves it whole. A process with none answers `503 task_start_unavailable`. The route is `apps/server/src/routes/task-start.ts`, `task.create` at `preValidation`.
- **Who is offered what is the server's answer, not the session's role** — the effective role is the higher of the org role and a project membership (`effectiveRole`), which the SPA cannot compute. So `GET /api/projects/:id/tasks` carries `can_start_task` (`task.create`) and `GET /api/tasks/:id` carries `can_export` (`task.export`), both required booleans beside WP-131's `can_raise_budget`; the export drops `can_export` with `can_raise_budget` (a document handed on must not carry the exporter's permissions). Both are contracts changes, so `verify:ui` and `verify:web-e2e` apply (rule 80); the web-e2e fixtures gained both fields.
- **The board** (`apps/web/src/features/board.tsx`): `StartTicketForm` above the columns when `can_start_task`; the key is held to the contract's schema before it is sent, a server refusal is shown as the server said it, and a success says *Started X — its task appears on the board once intake has created it*. **The empty-state hint names only what exists** (`emptyBoardHint`): the four pick-up rule kinds a binding has (`ticketMatchRuleSchema` — label, status, epic, query; the old hint's *"a component"* is no rule kind), and the form only to a caller it is shown to.
- **381 — Download JSON** on the task page through `DownloadLink` (`taskExportPath`), when `can_export`.
- **385 — the five sites** pass their role sentence through `readErrorDetail`: the user list, the organisation budgets (`settings.tsx`), the settings audit (`operating-mode.tsx`), the identity mappings (`identities.tsx`) and the task's *Who did what* (`task-detail.tsx`), which keeps *Not shown* for a 403 only (`isForbiddenError`, new in `api/read-error.ts`) and shows an `ErrorNotice` with the server's message otherwise.
- **388 — one selector**: `bindableIntegrations` / `useBindableIntegrations(type?)` in `apps/web/src/app/queries.ts`; the three pickers read it, and `integrations.tsx` keeps the unfiltered read.
- **The manual start's audit row has `task_id` null** (no task exists when it commits); its `params` name the project, the event, the ticket and the key. So the task page's *Who did what* does not show the start; the event's actor does, and the export carries it.

#### WP-122 — pre-review round (the binding's scope)

The orchestrator ruled that the scoping bypass this row's first version introduced (its own discovered item) is closed here: a binding's declared scope is not the pick-up rule.

- **A provider-declared check.** `TaskManagementPort.ticketScope(ticketKey) → TicketScopeVerdict` (`unscoped` | `in_scope` | `out_of_scope` with the binding's list), pure, required on the port. Jira answers from `project_keys` with the webhook's own `projectKeyOf` (now exported from `webhook.ts`), so the manual start and a delivery judge a key one way; an empty list is `unscoped`, as `config.ts` defines it. The fake answers from `FakeTaskManagementOptions.projectKeys` and, through its registration, from `bindings.config.project_keys` (the fake registration's config schema gained it); the harness stub answers `unscoped`. A provider with no scope concept answers `unscoped` and is never refused.
- **Which key is judged: the read value.** The check runs **after** the read and before any write, on `ticket.ref.key` — the key Jira answered, in its canonical upper-case form — so a typed `acme-7` is judged as Jira normalises it and exactly as the webhook judges a delivered key. `Ticket` carries no project field, so the canonical key's prefix is the read value available. The cost, stated at the code: one audited read of a ticket that is then refused; nothing is stored.
- **The refusal**: `ManualStartRefusedError('outside_binding_scope')` → `409 ticket_outside_binding_scope`, naming the binding's list (operator configuration) and the key the person typed, never the ticket's content.
- **The audit residual** is stated at the route's docblock and description, in technical/08 and in the user guide: the `task.start` row's `task_id` is **null** because no task exists when it commits — intake creates it later in its own `intake_check` job and transaction — so `GET /api/tasks/:id/audit` (*Who did what*) does not list the start; the match's `actor` names the person and the export carries it.

#### WP-122 — review round 1 (REQUEST CHANGES), addressed

1. **[major] The read outside every transaction is now enforced, not claimed.** `assertOutsideTransaction` (asked by `integrationsForProject` and `ticketReads`) sees only transactions opened through `markTransactions`, and the route hands in the plain `eventing.unitOfWork`, so moving the read inside a transaction left every case green (the reviewer's canary). `startTicketManually` now wraps its unit of work in `markTransactions` itself, so every composition gets it, as `createPipelineRuntime` does for the job path. The module note and the `@throws` say so. Cases in `packages/application/src/pipeline/manual-start.test.ts`: › "marks the transactions it opens, so a provider call inside one would be refused" (inside `record`, `transactionIsOpen()` is true) and › "refuses to read the ticket from inside a transaction" (`withOpenTransaction` around the start rejects with `TransactionOpenError` and records nothing). Canaries, both made with the Edit tool and reverted the same way, md5 identical: (a) the mark removed → the first case fails; (b) the reviewer's own, the read wrapped in `unitOfWork.transaction(...)` → 12 of 15 cases fail with `TransactionOpenError`.
2. **[minor] A moved Jira issue is a second key — stated, not closed.** Jira answers `GET issue/OLD-1` for a moved issue under its new key `NEW-5`. Scope is judged on `NEW-5`, but both one-task checks and intake's `unique (project_id, ticket_key, mode)` compare key strings, so a task created as `OLD-1` does not stop a second under `NEW-5`. The webhook door shares the gap, so it predates this row. The residual is stated in `manual-start.ts`'s module note and in technical/08's task-start row; the orchestrator files it.

#### WP-123

**A poll-only GitLab binding re-checks Ready and hears a reviewer; the real Sentry `resolve` runs end to end; the poll sweep's variable is renamed** — backlog 373, 378 and 372. Implementer, session 11, on `87673da`. Migration **0074**.

Decisions and assumptions (each is also stated at the code):

- **"Poll-only" is the port's answer, not a GitLab key read by the pipeline** (BD-017). `MergeRequestPollPlan` gained `receives_webhooks` (strict, required): GitLab answers `true` when either `webhook_secret_token` or `webhook_signing_token` is a non-empty secret — with neither, `verifyGitLabDelivery` refuses every delivery, so "no secret" is exactly "no delivery". The fake answers its `receivesWebhooks` option, and its registration the binding config key `receives_webhooks` (default `false`, GitLab's no-secret answer). The poller makes both new reads only when it is `false`, so no event can arrive by two doors (the ruling).
- **(a) The default branch.** Each poll of a poll-only binding reads `gitReads.defaultBranch` (audited, outside every transaction) and compares the sha with `bindings.mr_poll_default_head` (migration 0074). First read: write the head, record nothing (a poll that never saw the branch cannot say it moved). A different head: `default_branch.moved` through `recordNormalisedDelivery`, key `<provider>:poll:<project>:<path>@default:<old>..<new>` (redacted, like every `delivery_id`), **then** the head is written — a poll that dies between the two re-records the same key and the `inbox` row collapses it. **Why both heads in the key**: a key of the new head alone loses A → B → C → B's second B. **Stated residual, pinned by a test**: an exact repeat of an earlier pair (A → B → A → B) collides and is not recorded again — it needs the default branch force-pushed back to an exact earlier commit twice, which the protected default branch the platform requires forbids. The read happens on every poll, not only with a task at Ready: the knowledge index consumes the event too (one port read; on GitLab two requests, project then branch — the setup guide says so).
- **(b) The review notes.** `MergeRequestPollStore.readyMergeRequests` lists the project's tasks at `ready_for_merge` with an `mr_ref`, joined to their **current** Ready `task_stages` row (the attempt `stage_attempts` names, the stranded-stage read's join) for `entered_at` in the database's own microseconds, oldest entry first. At most `MR_POLL_REVIEW_TASKS_LIMIT` = **20** per poll (asked as 21, so a `warn` and `capped: true` say the cap was reached; the same twenty every poll until one leaves Ready — stated, not rotated). Each gets one `gitReads.discussions` (the window handler's own read). Each discussion is redacted before anything is built from it; a note is recorded as `mr.review.comment` when it is not `system`, not `isPlatformNote` (the saga's predicate) and its `created_at` is at or after `entered_at − REVIEW_NOTE_SKEW_MS`, under `<provider>:poll:<project>:<path>!<iid>#note:<id>` (an `inbox.find` first skips a recorded note without a transaction). The payload is the webhook's: `task_id: null`, the task's own `mr_ref`, the discussion's `id` as `thread_id` and its `resolved`, the note's author (as the adapter maps it; a poll consults no identity mapping).
- **The two-clock comparison, made in the safe direction.** The ruling asks for "notes created after the task entered Ready" — provider `created_at` against the platform's `entered_at`, which WP-110 learned not to compare. `REVIEW_NOTE_SKEW_MS` = `TICKET_POLL_OVERLAP_MS` (5 min) is subtracted, so a provider clock behind ours cannot lose a note; the cost, stated: a person's note written up to five minutes **before** Ready arms the review window a webhook would not have — and that window acts on the merge request's open threads whenever it fires, so it changes *when* an open thread returns the task, never *whether*.
- **Both reads fail open** (rule 20): a provider error is a `warn` and `failed` in the report; the stored head and the per-note keys lose nothing by a skipped poll. A failure to **record** is not caught — the poll fails and re-arms like any other. They run after the listing and the cursor, so a failed listing skips them for that poll.
- **`mr.approved` stays webhook-only** (ruling): it feeds the human-time projector's review minutes and nothing else. Also stated: a polled note is dated by the poll that recorded it (the envelope's `occurred_at`, up to one interval late), which is what the projector reads.
- **372.** `ServerConfig.pollSweepIntervalMs` from `APP_POLL_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`, else the old `APP_TICKET_POLL_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS` (blank is unset for both). `loadServerConfig` stays pure; `deprecatedEnvironment(env)` lists a set old name with its replacement and whether it is ignored, and `startRuntime` logs one `warn` per entry. `DEPRECATED_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES` is exported so the compose census (`test/e2e/compose/compose-config.e2e.test.ts`, "every name the server reads is delivered") excludes the old name **by the server's own list** — shipping it in `.env.example` would teach it.
- **378.** A new file rather than a fourth case in WP-111's, because its harness differs (the production Sentry registration over a stub `SentryFetch`, the integration created through the route). The stub serves Sentry's documented "Retrieve an Issue" example from `test/fixtures/http/sentry/issues.json`, re-pointed at the issue. The 429 case throttles all three executor attempts (`Retry-After: 0`), so the job fails after issue 7 is resolved, and then nudges the retry's `start_after` rather than waiting `PIPELINE_OUTBOUND_RETRY`'s 30 s.
- **The fake.** `addHumanDiscussion` gained `createdAt` and `system`; divergence **22** states that the fake verifies a delivery whatever its plan's `receives_webhooks` says (GitLab refuses all of them with no secret), and that its notes are on the fake's clock unless stated.

#### WP-124

**Work the queue fails, drops or delays, with nothing to recover it** — backlog 366, 368 and 392, built per TD-004's M7 amendment. Implementer, session 11, on `7ea1490`. Migration **0075** (`0075_lost_work_recovery.sql`); technical/02 (a job section and the proposal machine), technical/03, technical/08, the operator and user guides amended in the same change. The measurements are pasted under 366 and 392 (and a pointer under 314).

Decisions and assumptions (each is also stated at the code):

- **The JOB_EXHAUSTION column is `shape`** — `recovery_row` | `bound_and_escalate` | `notification_shaped`, and **`per_duty`** for `pipeline.outbound` only, whose twenty-nine duties are declared one by one in `OUTBOUND_DUTY_EXHAUSTION`, typed as a `Record` over `OutboundJobData['duty']` so a duty added without a row does not build. Next-tick queues (the polls, the reconciler, hygiene, the maintenance schedules) are declared `notification_shaped`: their next tick re-derives the effect, which is the amendment's own wording for that shape. `stage.execute` is `bound_and_escalate` (the archetype). The failed-jobs wire (`failedJobSchema.exhaustion.shape`) and the screen's last sentence follow the shape.
- **Bound and escalate needs the try number**, so `JobContext` gained `retries: {count, limit}` (pg-boss's `retry_count`/`retry_limit` through `includeMetadata: true`; the fake's own count), with `isLastTry`; held for both adapters by a contract case. `escalatingOnLastTry` (`pipeline/job-escalation.ts`) wraps the outbound dispatch and the review window: on the **last** try's throw it escalates the task with a platform-text brief (never the error's message) and then **rethrows**, so the job still ends `failed` and listed. An earlier try's throw, and a notification-shaped duty's, pass through untouched.
- **The bound-and-escalate duties are the ruling's four plus two the measurement added**: `dependency_gate` (a policy gate that otherwise lets a push through unchecked) and `ready_head_check` (a person's resume or hand-back that otherwise leaves the task where it was, silently). The other twenty-three are recovery rows already or notification-shaped; the table with each reason is under 366.
- **Q113, filed and implemented as its recommendation (a):** most of those tasks are `done` when the job runs (review-only, lint, a last-child breakdown, every discovery task), and `done` has no edge to `needs_human`. `escalateTaskWithBrief` escalates a task that can; adds the brief to one already in `needs_human` (`amendEscalation`); and for a finished task enqueues one `notify` duty of class `escalation` keyed by the job's own cause event, with the same brief. Residual: a project with no chat binding hears nothing more than the log and the failed-jobs list.
- **`apply_failed` is a seventh proposal status** (migration 0075: `alter type … add value`, `apply_recovery_attempted_at`, `apply_failure_reason` with a pair check), against `decide.ts`'s argument for six, because the fact is carried by no column; the docblock and technical/02 say so. It is not awaiting apply, so neither the apply pass nor the nightly hygiene sweep retries it; `decide` admits it (the store clears the mark and the reason in the same statement) and approving it enqueues an apply. The card says *apply failed* with the reason and offers **Approve again**.
- **The `knowledge_apply` row's predicate** is the proposal store's own `AWAITING_APPLY` clause (exported, one spelling, rule 41) plus no `knowledge.apply` job keyed `project:<id>` that is `created`, `retry` or `active` in pg-boss's table — the `stranded_stage` row's way. Mark and ending are both conditional on that predicate in their `where` (rule 9). A project with **no git binding** reaches the same ending on purpose: its approved proposals would never land, and the reason names both causes.
- **The `discovery_record` row** keys a new table `discovery_record_recoveries` on the artifact (the `knowledge_curations` shape). "Recorded" is a `readiness_evaluations` row of the project with source `discovery`/`rediscovery` evaluated at or after the artifact (a `recheck` carries the old evaluation forward and does not count), and only the project's **newest** draft is ever recovered, so a stale draft never overwrites a newer evaluation. Its ending escalates the discovery task through the same helper (a notification for a `done` task, keyed by the `artifact.created` event the read returns) **and** is published on `GET …/rediscovery` as `last_discovery.findings_unrecorded`, shown beside the Re-evaluate button.
- **368**: the reconciler appends through `appendOnProjectWithRetry` with the event built per attempt from the attempt's sequence; a match that loses all four attempts is skipped and counted (`contended`), never thrown; the handler runs the reconciliation and the stranded-work table in two `try`s and rethrows the first failure after both ran (the `finally` still re-arms). `intake-reconcile.ts` left `EXPECTED_SITES`.
- **392**: the ruling's first branch was measured first and **did not help** (identical drain at N = 20 and 50 with `burstWhenReadyExceeds: 1` on every worker — the cache is populated but refreshed on two 60-s cadences), so its other branch is built: `pipeline.outbound` registers at `PIPELINE_OUTBOUND_POLLING_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 0.5` (pg-boss's floor); every other queue keeps `APP_JOBS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS`. No burst trigger is set, and the adapter's docblock says why. **Assumption:** the ruling's "`pipeline.intake`" is the `intake_check` duty of `pipeline.outbound` (no such queue exists), so the one change covers it. The idle cost (an outbound fetch twice a second per process) was **not measured on a large job table**.
- **technical/02 had no job table** for criterion (5) to follow, so one was written: § "Jobs, and what a job that spent its retries does".

Tests:
- `packages/application/src/pipeline/intake-reconcile.test.ts` › "re-emits every match once through three lost races, and the stranded pass still runs in that tick"; › "skips a match that loses every attempt, counts it, and still re-emits the next project’s and runs the stranded pass"; › "runs the stranded pass even when the intake half throws, and then fails the job (the canary for the separate try)".
- `packages/application/src/pipeline/job-escalation.test.ts` (new, 14): › "escalates the task with a brief naming %s, then still fails the job" over every duty declared `bound_and_escalate` (six); › "leaves a throw before the last try to the retry policy, and escalates nothing (the other side)"; › "lists a notification-shaped duty only: its last try escalates nothing (rule 20)"; › "escalates the task with a brief naming the merge request, then still fails the job" (`mr.comment.debounce`); the endings › "adds the brief to a task already waiting for a person, without moving it", › "tells a finished task’s people through an escalation notification, since it cannot escalate (Q113)", › "answers absent for a task that is gone", › "rethrows the job’s own failure when escalating fails too"; › "has escalation text for exactly the duties declared bound_and_escalate".

That timing matches the WP-124 failure.
- **Fix:** `quiesced` in `test/e2e/pipeline/mr-poll.e2e.test.ts` takes the baseline only after two things.
  - First, no `event_dispatch` row is pending and no `pipeline.outbound` job is `created`, `retry` or `active`: the last thing the Ready entry's duties do is leave the queue.

- **Sweep of the file's other waits.** None needed a change.

  - No other case counts provider calls.

#### WP-125

**Knowledge proposals lost to a settings refusal, or colliding on one path** — backlog 356, 369 and 355. Implementer, session 11, on `4f293ea`. Migration **0076** (`0076_knowledge_deferral_and_settings_refusal.sql`); technical/02, /03, /07, /08 and the user guide amended in the same change.

**Criterion 1, measured first.** The store did **not** record which merge request carries which path: `markApplied` wrote `status` and `applied_commit_sha` only (`packages/infrastructure/src/knowledge/postgres-proposal-store.ts` at `4f293ea`), and nothing else on `kb_proposals` or any other table names a knowledge merge request (grep for `knowledge_mr`/`agentic/knowledge` over `packages`, `apps`: only the idempotency key and the branch name builder). So 0076 adds `kb_proposals.applied_merge_request jsonb` (the ref `openMergeRequest` answered, parsed with `mergeRequestRefSchema` on read) and `apply_deferred_reason text` (with `kb_proposals_deferral_is_unapplied`), plus `knowledge_curations.settings_refused_at` and its partial index.

Decisions and assumptions (each is also stated at the code):

- **356 — a refusal records itself and clears the attempt.** `KnowledgeProposalStore.markCurationRefused` upserts `settings_refused_at` and sets `recovery_attempted_at = null` in one statement (never over a curated or abandoned row); the Librarian and the research page call it through `recordCurationRefusal`. The stranded pass then finds the row unattempted at every interval and re-offers it until the document parses. `endCuration` now also requires `recovery_attempted_at is not null`, so an ending racing a refusal writes nothing (rule 9). A re-offer is a settings read and no model call; the old reason in technical/03 (*a model call a minute*) was wrong and is corrected there.
- **The waiting count** is `countCurationsWaitingOnSettings` (`apps/server/src/queries/project-queries.ts`): refused, uncurated, unabandoned rows of the project's tasks. The `409 invalid_stored_config` adds one platform sentence (`waitingCurationsSentence`, nothing when zero); the settings screen already renders the 409's message as text, so no contract change was needed for it. **Assumption:** the count is computed on every `GET …/config` (one indexed read) rather than only on a refusal, to keep `effectiveConfigResponseOf` pure.
- **369 — deferral, as ruled.** Before a `create`, `planBatch` (`packages/application/src/knowledge/apply.ts`) reads the path's carriers (`applyCarriers`: applied rows with a recorded merge request, at most `MAX_CARRIERS_PER_PATH` = 3 per path) and asks the provider through `gitReads.mergeRequest`. `opened`/`locked` defers (reason names `!iid` and the path); `merged`/`closed`/`not_found` blocks nothing and the **index** decides, as before. **Assumption:** a merged merge request is left to the index rather than forced to `update`, because the next pass is asked for by the index run that read the merge (`wakeAwaitingKnowledgeApply`, composed in `afterIndex` in `apps/server/src/knowledge.ts`), so the index holds the page by then; forcing `update` would turn a page deleted after the merge into a refused commit. A deferred proposal stays approved, holds no place in the batch, and is outside the WP-124 `knowledge_apply` recovery predicate (waiting on a person's merge is not stranded); the nightly hygiene sweep still re-enqueues its project. `markApplied` and `decide` clear the reason. It is published as `apply_deferred_reason` on the proposal record and drawn on the card (*waits for a merge*).
- **A provider read failure**: retryable (`rate_limited`, `unavailable`) throws, so pg-boss retries the pass; any other refusal (`forbidden`, `invalid_response`, …) defers **that** proposal with `applyUnreadableReason` instead of failing the batch — never a `create` on a guess.
- **355.** `describedConfigClauses` renders an `unrecognized_keys` issue as `<path or (root)> (<zod message>)`, still redacted then bounded; the issue type gained an optional `code`.
- **420 (read, not fixed).** The deferral makes it **no worse and slightly better**: a deferred page never enters the commit, so it cannot be the page that fails a batch while it waits, and a non-retryable read failure holds back one page rather than failing the batch. The batch is still one commit, so a page the provider refuses still fails its siblings.

Tests:
- `test/contract/knowledge-apply-deferral.contract.test.ts` (new, fake git) › "gives one merge request, defers the second with a reason naming it, and updates the page once it merges"; › "holds back only the waiting page: another page in the same pass is still committed"; › "creates the page when the earlier merge request was closed without merging (the other side)".
- `packages/application/src/knowledge/apply.test.ts` › "defers the newer one while the merge request is open, and names it"; › "creates the page when the merge request was %s" (closed, not_found); › "fails closed on a retryable provider failure: no commit, and the pass throws for pg-boss to retry"; › "holds back only that page when the provider refuses the read for good, never creating it on a guess"; › "does not ask the provider about a page the index already holds"; › "wakes the apply after an index run only when an approved proposal waits".
- `test/integration/knowledge/curation-settings-refusal.integration.test.ts` (new, PostgreSQL 18, the real project read over `projects.config`) › "is re-offered at the next interval, not ended, and lands once the document parses"; › "still ends a curation whose re-offered wake-up was lost again (the bound the refusal does not touch)".
- `packages/application/src/knowledge/librarian.test.ts` › "records the refusal instead of proceeding when the project’s stored settings do not parse" (now asserts the refusal mark, for the research page too) and › "lands the curation once the document parses, after a refusal (WP-125, backlog 356)".
- `apps/server/src/routes/projects.test.ts` › "names how many knowledge curations wait on a refused document, and says nothing of them when none does (WP-125)"; `apps/web/src/features/project-settings.test.tsx` › "shows how many knowledge curations wait on a refused stored configuration (WP-125)".
- `packages/application/src/pipeline/settings.test.ts` › "names an unknown key at the root, with (root) rather than an empty path"; › "names an unknown key inside an object, under the object’s path"; › "still renders a refused value by its value (the other side)"; › "redacts the key before it bounds the clause, so a credential across the bound is not half-published".
- `test/contract/support/knowledge-proposals-suite.ts` (memory and PostgreSQL) › "records a curation refusal without curating, and the curation that follows still claims"; › "records the merge request an apply opened, and answers it per path, bounded"; › "defers only a proposal still awaiting apply, and an apply or a decision clears the deferral".
- `test/integration/recovery/lost-work-recovery-stores.integration.test.ts` › "never marks or ends a proposal deferred behind an open knowledge merge request (WP-125)".
- UI: `apps/web/src/features/project-panels.test.tsx` › "says, as text, that an approved proposal waits for the open knowledge merge request that creates its page (WP-125)" and › "draws no deferral on a proposal that waits for nothing (the other side)".

- *Criterion (1), `APP_PORT=0`.* Compose **2.38.2** (the release binary, CI's version) and **v5.5.1** (this machine) both accept `0` in `'${APP_PORT:-8080}:8080'`: `config` renders `published: "0"`, `up` publishes an ephemeral port on `0.0.0.0` and `[::]`, and `docker compose port app 8080` answers `0.0.0.0:55912`. Against Docker Desktop 29.8.1; CI's daemon is 28.0.4, which was not run (ephemeral `0` host ports are daemon behaviour much older than either). So 348 closes: no probe, no retry.
- *The default network's upgrade path* (a two-service project making exactly `compose.yml`'s change, both versions): v5.5.1's plain `up -d` **and** `run --rm migrate` stop the containers, remove the old network and fail to start them (`could not find a network matching network mode <old>`); `--force-recreate` recovers. 2.38.2 recreates them on `<project>_default` and leaves the old network behind. `docker compose down` with the **old** file first, then the new file's `run`/`up`, is clean on both. Written into `docs/operator-guide.md` § 5.
- *The web e2e hang* (`ci` `36952588895` attempt 1, job `110668545991`, read through the jobs API — `gh run view --job` returned the rerun's log): `51 passed (45.0s)` at 01:48:36, **no** `PASS: verify:web-e2e`, cancelled 02:20:01, and the runner's orphan sweep then killed `pnpm → sh → MainThread` twice — `scripts/verify.mjs`'s chain and `playwright test` itself. Playwright 1.63 tears its `webServer` down **before** `onEnd`, and its CLI exits through `gracefullyProcessExitDoNotHang` (bounded at 30 s) once `runAllTestsWithConfig` returns, so what was left is the reporters' `onEnd`/`onExit` (HTML on CI) and the flush. **Not reproduced**: locally the target exits every time (summary → `PASS` 39 ms passing, 27 ms for a failing test whose trace the HTML report copied, `CI=true`); two healthy CI runs read 77 ms and 95 ms. #### WP-126 — review round 1 (REQUEST CHANGES), addressed

- **(major) The watchdog would end an interactive process.** Playwright 1.63 builds the config's reporters for every test-server run (`lib/runner/index.js:6848`, read), so `--ui`, watch mode and the VS Code extension would have been `process.exit(1)`'d 90 s after a run. `playwright.config.ts` now lists it **on CI only** (CI runs only the plain path). `scripts/playwright-exit-watchdog.test.ts` › "lists the watchdog on CI, after `list` and before `html`" and › "does not list it off CI, where `--ui`, watch mode and the editor reuse the process" import the real config under each `CI`. Canary: the watchdog put back into the non-CI branch → the second fails by name.
- **(major) The job census read one key shape.** `workflowJobs` in `scripts/release.test.ts` reads every two-space line inside `jobs:` as a key (bare, quoted, any case, with a comment) and **reports** a two-space line it cannot parse, or a flow-style `jobs:`, instead of folding it into the previous job; `ci.yml` is asserted to have eleven. Not `yaml`: it is `packages/infrastructure`'s dependency, not the root's. › "finds a planted unbounded job in every key spelling, and exempts a reusable-workflow call" (adds `later: # c`, `Deploy:`, `_x:`, `"quoted job":`, `'single':`, `- not a key`) and › "reads every job key a workflow can spell, and stops at the next top-level key". Canary: the old `[a-z][\w-]*:$` shape restored → both fail.
- **(minor) A reusable-workflow call** (`uses:` at job level) is exempt, stated at the line: GitHub refuses `timeout-minutes` there and the called workflow's jobs are in the census. Canary: exemption disabled → the planted case fails with `"reusable: none"`.
- **(minor) Start-up and global volumes.** The isolation check starts with `Promise.allSettled` and rethrows the first refusal only after both `up`s have ended. **Measured** with a copy whose second project's `up` names a service that does not exist: `allSettled` → FAIL by name, nothing left; the `Promise.all` copy → FAIL by name and project `a`'s `app` container and two volumes **left behind**, the race this closes. `composeEnvironment(project)` (support module) gives `APP_PORT=0` plus `<project>-ctl`/`<project>-repo-cache`, used by the web and isolation checks (the stock check already set both in its `.env`), and `image.yml`'s teardown passes the same names. › "lets the daemon choose the port and names both global volumes after the project".
- **(nit)** Operator guide § 5: the already-pulled path is `down`, `docker network rm agentic`, `run --rm migrate`, `up -d` — measured clean on Compose v5.5.1 and 2.38.2 — and why `run --rm migrate` first fails on v5.5.1 and how to recover.
- **(nit)** `parsePublishedPort` trims each line: › "reads a CRLF answer, line by line"; canary: the trim removed → it fails.
- **`.gitignore`**: `/test-results/` and `/playwright-report/` anchored. Playwright resolves both against the config's directory, the repository root (the HTML reporter's `resolveReporterOutputPath`), and both appear only at the root after a run.
- Docker: `compose-isolation-check` and `web-compose-check` **PASS** at a load of 6.0. The `Promise.all` canary left two volumes, `agentic-isolation-check-wp126all-a_exports` and `agentic-isolation-check-wp126all-a_knowledge` (its container was removed); the volume hook stops the implementer removing them — **for the user** to remove. Volume count 146 before (other projects grew from 140), 148 after: those two.

#### WP-127

**A run that cannot start, or cannot reach the model, says nothing about why** — backlog 351, 344, 346, 339 and 341. Implementer, session 11, on `f434cfc`.

**Measured first** (criterion 1; a daemon, no model credential; the numbers are pasted into 339, 346 and 341 above).
- *(a) 339* — the bare `docker stop` gave **3.1 s**, not ten (a control container: 3.15 s bare, 10.16 s with `-t 10`). Under `-t 10` the launcher exited **137** with `launcher signal: SIGTERM` and nothing after; under a 90 s grace its close resolved after **12.1 s**, exit 0, the create answered. Neither hypothesis — the close neither rejects nor leaves early; the create outlasts the grace.
- *(b) 346* — sidecar stopped before the CLI started: ten `api_retry` (`error_status: null`), delays doubling from 0.61 s to a cap near 32–37 s, give-up (`<synthetic>` "Request timed out" + `error_during_execution`) **177 s** after the first request, no stderr.
- *(c) 341* — a pre-WP-103 orphan (worktree at `68906a56^`): two containers, one network, two volumes and the control directory, none with `com.agentic.instance`; the guide's commands leave only `ws-<run>`.

Decisions and assumptions (each also at the code):
- **351** — `WorkspaceError` gains `reason` (closed vocabulary `WORKSPACE_ERROR_REASONS`, 19 codes, set only where the platform wrote the refusal) and `commit` (kept only if it parses as `shaSchema`); both cross the control plane in the error envelope (optional fields, so a launcher one build behind still parses), and the client derives `launcher_unreachable`/`_unauthorized`/`_request_refused`/`_internal_error` when the launcher sent none. `RunStartError` carries a `diagnosis` derived from a `WorkspaceError` cause, and `describeStartFailure` re-reads every field through its schema before writing `RunStartError: invalid_spec, checkout_commit_missing, commit <sha>` into `run.failed.error`, the escalation's reason and its blocker brief. The message and `detail` stay in the logs.
- **344** — the ruling's seam: `createRunletSpawn` returns a `RunletSpawn` with `setStderrSink`; `createClaudeRunner` sets it with `createStderrLog` over the run's redactor (`runner/stderr-log.ts`). Before the first stream message stderr is **held raw** (64 KiB, newest kept) and redacted as one string at the end — so a credential split across two frames is still redacted — and written as one `warn` line, its redacted tail cut to 8 KiB; after it, each frame at `debug`. Nothing reaches the transcript, the outcome or the task. The `onStderr` option stays for scripts, replaced by the sink.
- **346** — an `api_retry` is not progress; the CLI's `<synthetic>` assistant message is **neutral** (neither progress nor a retry). **Beyond the ruling's letter, because of (b)**: the CLI gives up at ~3 min, before the shipped 5-minute stall, so the stall alone would never name the route on the defaults; a non-success `result` reached with only retries since the last progress also carries the platform sentence (`retriedWithoutModel('gave_up', …)`) instead of the CLI's words. When the retries reported HTTP statuses the sentence names them (integers checked to 100–599) and says the provider failed or refused, not that there is no route.
- **339** — outcome (b): the docblock in `apps/launcher/src/index.ts` states the measured cause; no drain below ten seconds was built because the create does not fit in one. The check now stops with `-t 10`.
- **341** — `docs/operator-guide.md` § 5, *Upgrading past the build that removes orphaned run containers (WP-103)*, placed after WP-126's paragraph.

- (1) the measurements above; `scripts/launcher-control-plane-check.mjs` records *backlog 339: a launcher stopped during a create drains it or is killed at the grace, never leaves early (WP-127)*, *backlog 346: the sidecar was stopped before the CLI started, and the CLI retried the model API*, and *backlog 346: the retries did not hold the run open; it ended stalled, naming the route (WP-127)* (or, with both flags past the give-up, *…the CLI gave up and the run’s error names the route*).

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed):
- `ask/executor.ts`'s start failure writes the class name only, as the stage executor did before WP-127; `describeStartFailure` is the one-line fix.
- `compose.yml` gives the launcher compose's default ten-second `stop_grace_period`; a longer one (the measured drain was 12.1 s) would let SIGTERM answer an in-flight create instead of leaving it to the orphan pass.
- A bare `docker stop` on Docker Desktop 29.8.1 grants 3.1 s, not the documented ten; any other script or doc that stops a container expecting ten seconds has the same gap.

#### WP-128

**The test tiers pass for the wrong reason or leave debris on a shared daemon** — backlog 398, 394, 395, 352 and 390. Implementer, session 11, on `18f16d2`.

**Machine discipline, recorded.** Two runs were started over the gate, each with the reading taken in the same command rather than before it: a unit run of two files at a one-minute load of **30.4**, and the second `verify` at **23.9** (its own previous `verify:e2e` had just ended; it passed). The stand-in's own three objects were removed by the measured cleanup itself. No `com.agentic.run` container, network or volume was on the daemon before or after.

- An object with `com.agentic.run` and no instance label (made before WP-103) is never removed by a cleanup or a sweep, which fails towards keeping.
- The liveness test is still this pid namespace's: on a daemon shared with another host, a live fixture's servers, attached containers and run objects are now removed as well (stated at the module).
- An unlabelled `ws-<uuid>` volume belonging to another consumer is still removed by a cleanup's name sweep; production never makes one unlabelled (`provider.ts` creates it labelled).

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; nothing measured unless said):

One exited export container was observed after a `verify:e2e`.
- `startDockerFixture`'s probe containers (`agentic-e2e-probe-<suffix>`) carry no marker and sit on a run's network; a probe left by a killed file would keep its `run-<id>` network from the instance join's `rm`.
- A measurement that needs a disposable compose instance cannot remove that instance's volumes under the session's volume hook; the brief's teardown recipe assumes it can.

**A stack that stops, crashes or refuses during a first test leaves no lost create, no unnamed failure
and no debris.** Folds backlogs 425, 424, 426, 428, 405 and 427 (each marked RESOLVED, commit pending).

**(1) 425 — the launcher's stop grace, measured first (rule 27, rule 64).** All on Docker Desktop,
Engine 29.8.1 / Compose 5.5.1, `linux/arm64`, load read before each step.
- *Why a stop was ~3 s.* A two-service compose project with no volumes (a `sh` that traps TERM and
  then sleeps 20 s): the service with `stop_grace_period: 30s` was created with `Config.StopTimeout`
  30 and `docker compose stop` took 21 s, exit 0 (drained); the service with **no**
  `stop_grace_period` (`StopTimeout` `<nil>`) was killed after **3 s**, exit 137. A bare `docker stop`
  of a plain container: no `--stop-timeout` → 3.2 s, exit 137; `--stop-timeout 30` → 20.9 s, exit 0.
  So on this daemon a container with no grace of its own gets about three seconds — through compose
  too — not the documented ten (WP-103's "about three seconds", WP-127's 3.1 s). Cause inside Docker
  Desktop not established; the docs say 10 s.
- *The create under a stop.* `scripts/launcher-control-plane-check.mjs` now starts the launcher with
  `--stop-timeout` = `compose.yml`'s `stop_grace_period` (read off the file; `--launcher-stop-grace-s`
  overrides it) and stops it with a bare `docker stop`, which is compose's path. At 90 s (load ~5): the
  stop came 1.6 s into the create and the close resolved **11 675 ms** after SIGTERM, create answered,
  exit 0. With nothing in flight: **199 ms**. At the shipped 60 s (load 6–7): **12 597 ms**, answered,
  exit 0; idle **169 ms**. WP-127's 12.1 s was at load 14, so the duration is barely load-sensitive.
- *The setting.* `compose.yml` › `launcher` › `stop_grace_period: 60s`, about five times the longest
  reading, stated beside it with the readings; the cost is nil unless something is in flight (idle
  stop 0.2 s). Residual stated there: a first mirror clone of a large repository can outlast it.
- *Assertions.* `backlog 339 and 425: a launcher stopped during a create drains it inside its 60 s
  grace and answers it (WP-132)` (drained only — WP-127's record also accepted "killed at the grace"),
