#### WP-133

**The real CLI in `local` mode, measured without a credential, before the product owner's first run.**
Folds backlog 137's `local`-mode half and WP-132's discovered work (the stop graces of `app`, `runner`
and `db`). Implementer, session 11, on `677b6be`. Every reading used an obviously fake
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; no model credential was used. Docker Desktop 29.8.1, Compose 5.5.1,
`linux/arm64`; images rebuilt from the tree (`node scripts/build-images.mjs platform launcher`).

**The finding that matters most: a `local`-mode instance ran no agent at all.** The first run of the
new `local` leg (image of the tree before the fix) failed (b): the `runner` logged *"the pipeline is
composed without an agent runner"* with `missing: ["CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (…)"]` while the probe in
the same container showed the token in its environment and in `agentRunEnvironment`'s output.
`apps/server/src/pipeline.ts` called `composeAgentRunner` without `modelOauthToken`, and the field was
optional on `AgentRunnerOptions`, so it typechecked. Fixed (the value passed), and the field is now
**required** so leaving it out is a type error (`agent.test.ts` gained `modelOauthToken: null` at its
`api`-mode call sites). The product owner's `compose.local.yml` instance would have queued every stage.

**(1) The host list (backlog 137, pasted there).** `scripts/launcher-control-plane-check.mjs` runs the
real `claude` 2.1.267 a second time in `local` mode — `launcher-control-plane-runner.mjs`'s `real-cli`
phase with `CHECK_REAL_CLI_MODE=local`: the run's environment from the server's `agentRunEnvironment`,
`providerMode: 'local'`, and the egress list from `SERVER_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.modelEgressHosts`. Result,
twice (load 4–8): every host the CLI asked for is on the run's list; none was refused (allowed hosts
are below the sidecar's log level, so not listed), and the API answered 401 twice
(`api_retry` with `error_status` 401), *"Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 Invalid bearer token"*,
run over in 2.3 s. `api.anthropic.com` is allowed because it is the model API; the 401 proves it was
reached. Records: *the run carries the server’s local-mode
environment — CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN by name, and nothing else*, *the run’s egress list is the stock
model hosts and the git host*, *the CLI reached the model host and was refused the fake subscription
token* (asserted on the transcript's `"error_status":401`), *the sidecar refused no host*, and *the
token’s value is in no record and no log line* (runner record, sidecar log, launcher log). **PASS
54/54** (49 + 5). Calibration in the same run: the `api` leg, which allows no model host, gives
`refusedHosts: ["api.anthropic.com"]` through the same parser.

**(2) The `local` leg of `scripts/compose-stock-check.mjs`** (`--leg stock|local|all`, default `all`,
which `image.yml` runs; its teardown gains the `-lm` project). A second project from `compose.yml` +
`compose.local.yml` with the launcher pair, a fake token and `LOG_LEVEL=info`: (a) `app` and `runner`
**healthy** by the image's `HEALTHCHECK` and the launcher logging *"the launcher control plane is
listening"*; (b) the runner logs *"this process runs agent stages"* and never *"composed without an
agent runner"*, the `app` still composes none, and the runner's own client and token answer the
launcher's `health`; (c) a probe run in the runner (`node --import ./scripts/ts-source-resolver.mjs`,
the image's own `loadServerConfig` and `agentRunEnvironment`) prints names and booleans only:
`env_names: ["CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN"]`, the same `secret_env_names`, `value_is_the_container_token:
true`, `api_key_blank: true`; and the value is in no line of `docker compose logs` (179 lines) and no row
of a `pg_dump --data-only` (45 KB). Before the fix: (b) **FAIL**, everything else ok. After: **PASS**,
both legs (21 stock checks unchanged + 9 local). Teardown is the script's own `down -v` through
`execFile`, which the volume hook does not see (read, and WP-126 recorded the same); the leg creates no
run, so no `repo-cache` volume.

**(3) Operator guide § 8** now states what was measured (runs agents since the fix; the token by name;
nothing refused up to authentication, with the log's limit; how a wrong token fails, named; the
plan-limit failure marked inferred), that a subscription token is billed to
the plan — Anthropic's page quoted, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#generate-a-long-lived-token
— and what is not measured (the cost the CLI reports for a subscription run; hosts after a successful
authentication). Also that the CLI prefers an API key when both are set (same page, *Authentication
precedence*).

**The fold: stop graces.** Measured first:
- *Idle stops*, through compose with each grace in place (`local` leg, load ~6): `runner`, `app`, `db`
  each **0.2 s, exit 0** (twice).
- *PostgreSQL under load*: a `postgres` of the pinned digest with PGDATA in the container layer
  (`--rm` / `rm -v`, no named volume), 3 M rows then a 1 M-row update leaving **16 269 of 16 384**
  shared buffers dirty, then a plain `docker stop`: **0.63 s** and **0.76 s**, exit 0, *"database system
  is shut down"* (stop signal SIGINT, fast shutdown).
- *The runner with a run in flight*: a scratch e2e (two `apps/server` processes on one database, the
  run held at its workspace in `runner`, then `runner.stop()`, deleted after) — the stop was **still
  waiting after 60 s**, the run `running`, its `stage.execute` job `active`. So the runner's shutdown
  waits for the stage (the pipeline worker's `offWork` with `wait`), and in a container the deadline
  `close-with-grace` applies, `APP_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` (30 s), is what ends it (exit 1; read in
  `main.ts` and the library, not measured in a container). The run then waits for the lease sweep
  (WP-47, not re-measured). **This scratch run was started without a separate load reading: the load
  was 12.5 at its start** — a breach of the gate, stated; the reading is a "did not finish in 60 s",
  which load does not make shorter.
- Settings, each stated beside it in `compose.yml`: `app` and `runner` **45 s** (the 30 s deadline plus
  a margin; raise both with `APP_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS`, which `.env.example` now says), `db` **30 s**
  (about forty times 0.76 s, for a slower disk). Honest note at the line: on the measured disk three
  seconds would have sufficed for `db`.
- Operator guide § 5 (upgrade): what happens to a run in flight on `stop runner` and the three graces.

- (1) the five `backlog 137 (local)` records above.
- (2) the nine `local mode:` checks above; `test/e2e/pipeline/local-mode.e2e.test.ts` › "a runner in local mode (compose.local.yml’s arrangement)" › "composes an agent runner and spawns the CLI with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN by name (WP-133)"
  (the shipped topology in-process: the `runner` in `local` mode takes the first stage, the spec's

- The fold: `scripts/compose-check-support.test.ts` › "the stop graces compose.yml declares (WP-133)" › "reads a service’s grace, answers null for none, and refuses a spelling it cannot read", "gives app and runner more than the server’s own shutdown deadline, with a margin", "gives db and the launcher several times the longest stop they were measured at", "leaves no long-lived service on the daemon’s three seconds unless it is named with a reason";

**Decisions and assumptions** (each also at the code):
- The `local` real-CLI leg allows the stock model host, so the fake token **does** reach
  `api.anthropic.com` and is refused there — the brief's "before it fails authentication". An allowed
  `CONNECT` is below the sidecar's `Notice` level, so the model host is shown reached by the 401, and
  "every host" means every host asked of the proxy (a direct connection would die on the `internal`
  network unlogged — stated in 137).
- Stock check's `local` leg runs at `LOG_LEVEL=info` (the stock leg stays at `warn`): (b)'s positive
  line is `info`, and "in no log" is stronger over the verbose log.
- `stopGracePeriodSeconds` reads only `<n>s`, refusing other spellings by name rather than misreading
  them. `docker-socket-proxy` and `db-backup` are exempted in the census with a reason each.
- `db-backup`'s exemption is unmeasured (a dump cut short at three seconds) — discovered work.

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed):
- **Nothing stops a run on SIGTERM.** A runner stopped mid-run (an upgrade, `docker compose up -d`
  after an `.env` change) waits its 30 s deadline, exits 1, and the run is left to the lease sweep and
  the task to `needs_human`. Interrupting live runs on shutdown (with the WP-101 cancel path, charging
  what was measured) would turn a lost run into a cancelled one.
- operator-guide § Restore stops `app launcher` but not `runner`, which also writes the database.
- `db-backup` has no `stop_grace_period`; whether a dump in flight survives a three-second stop is
  unmeasured.
- What the CLI reports as a run's cost under a subscription token is unmeasured; the ledger and the
  budgets take it as reported (BD-011), so in `local` mode a budget may be denominated in a figure that
  is not money billed.

**What the first Jira ticket meets — 416, 418, 375, 408 folded.** No Docker by hand, no credential.

**Measured first (418).** The key is stored as `tasks.ticket_key` and one task per ticket was
`unique (project_id, ticket_key, mode)` plus `findByTicket` on the same tuple (0004). Every Jira
document the adapter reads already carries the issue's `id` beside `key` — `GET issue/{key}` (manual
start, intake's snapshot), `GET search/jql` (poll) and the webhook envelope's `issue` — and every
fixture under `test/fixtures/http/jira-cloud/` shows it (`"id": "10001"`); `jiraIssueSchema` parsed it
as `id?: string` and dropped it. That a move keeps the id is read, not measured: Atlassian's KB
(`moved-issues-no-longer-redirect-…`, retrieved 2026-10-03) redirects every former key and joins it to
`moved_issue_key.issue_id = jiraissue.id`; added to `SOURCES.md`. The id is available on all three
doors, so no key-resolution fallback was needed.

**Decisions.**
- **416 — option (b), the projection.** Option (a) is an `update` of `human_actions`, which
  `platform_apply_grants` (0001) gives the application role `insert` on and revokes `update` from —
  measured: the integration case's `update` is refused `permission denied`. One SQL subquery
  (`packages/infrastructure/src/ask/task-audit.ts`) is spliced into both audit readers — the ask store's
  `auditForTask` (*Who did what* and the export) and `get_task_context`'s Drizzle `listTaskAudit`: the
  `task.start` row with `task_id is null` whose `params.event_id` is the `task.created` event's
  `cause_event_id` — or, for a match the intake reconciler re-emitted, that match's own cause — and
  whose `params.project_id` is the task's project (on `human_actions_project_idx`).
- **418 — `TicketRef.id`** (`ticketIdSchema`: 1–64 of `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, `nullish`), carried by the
  Jira adapter on every ref it builds (`issueRef`, only for 1–20 decimal digits, else omitted).
  Migration **0077**: `tasks.ticket_id` (insert-only, outside the `save` partition), a shape check, and
  a partial unique index `(project_id, ticket_provider, ticket_id, mode) where ticket_id is not null` as
  the backstop. `findByTicket` takes an optional `ticketId` and answers key **or** id (oldest first);
  intake (both reads), the manual start's in-transaction check and the intake reconciler ask with it.
  **Residual, stated in technical/08 and the guide:** a task created before 0077 recorded no id (no
  backfill — the id is the provider's) and is still judged by its key. The fake carries no id (one task
  per key; its divergence register says so).
- **375 — the adapter, plus a signal.** WP-110's review round already dropped the keys a `400` names.
  What was left: Cloud's wording is unmeasured and the error text is cut at 300 characters, so a
  refusal naming no key still blinded the read. Now: Jira's other wording (*"The value 'X' does not
  exist for the field 'key'"*) is read too, a refusal naming none is **bisected** to the single
  refused key, all within `MAX_KEY_SEARCHES` = 32 (replaces `MISSING_KEY_RETRIES`); every key refused
  on its own with none named is the query's fault and Jira's error is thrown (fail open, as before).
  The port's `matchTickets` gained an optional `onUnreadableKeys` callback (platform keys only); the
  poll's live read logs a `warn` naming them every poll. No escalation — that stays a decision.
- **408 — `apps/web/src/features/cost-text.ts`** holds the words both the task page and the card read;
  the card's tooltip no longer says *"Provider-reported"* and an `excl. N unmeasured` count sits beside
  the total when there is one.

**Discovered work** (for the refiner):
- `test/e2e/topology/two-processes.e2e.test.ts` › "commits, in the worker, a knowledge approval the API
  answered" reads `pgboss.job.state` right after the commit is visible; the commit happens inside the

  Failed once under load in WP-134's first `verify:e2e`.
- `TaskRepository.recordTicketSignal` (and the webhook/poll `ticket.updated` path behind it) is keyed by
  `ticket_key`: after a move, edits arrive under `NEW-5` and never stamp the task created as `OLD-1`, so
  its snapshot is not re-read. Same for any other key-keyed lookup of a task by ticket.
- The poll's live read asks `key in ("OLD-1")` for a moved ticket's task; whether Jira's JQL resolves a
  former key is unmeasured. If it does not, the key is now reported as unreadable every poll (named,
  not silent), and that task's edits are lost to the poll.

  *"Provider-reported cost"*, false in `local` mode (backlog 408's neighbours).

**Decisions and assumptions.**
- The runbook recommends `COMPOSE_FILE=compose.yml:compose.local.yml` in `.env` so no later plain
  `docker compose` command can recreate `app`/`runner` in `api` mode — measured with `config` only.
- It recommends **poll-only** for both providers on a laptop, and therefore states the CI-gate cost
  below rather than hiding it.
- Autix's stack is not assumed; the runbook states what the run image carries (Node and npm only) and
  that CI is the evidence for a project in another language.
- The `docker stats` reading of the stack's memory failed (the container list was empty by the time it
  ran, so it listed other projects' containers); discarded — the runbook says the stack's own memory
  is not measured.

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed):
- **A poll-only GitLab binding parks every task whose CI runs longer than about two minutes**
  (read off the code, not measured). `ci_gate` is evaluated on entry and re-checked every
  `GATE_RECHECK_MS` (30 s) up to `MAX_GATE_CHECKS` (5), then escalates *undecided*; the pipeline event
  that normally settles it is webhook-only, and WP-123's poll-only reads add no pipeline read. The
  GitLab guide's *"The CI gate does not need the pipeline event (it asks GitLab for the head's pipeline
  itself)"* is therefore true only for CI shorter than ~2 min. Graded **major for the first test** if
  Autix's CI is longer: the first task stops at the CI gate. The runbook states it and the hand-back.
- **`docker compose up --build` cannot build from an empty machine** (measured above); operator guide
  fixed, but `compose.yml`'s and `compose.local.yml`'s headers still teach `up --build`, and nothing in
  compose builds `platform-base`, `platform-runtime` or `platform-egress` (a `base` service with
  `profiles`, or `additional_contexts`, would close it). No check covers the empty-machine path: the
  stock check needs prebuilt images.
- **No password change**: no screen in `apps/web/src`; operator guide § 2 still says *"change it after
  first sign-in"*. Better Auth may serve an endpoint; not tried.
- **Operator guide stale since WP-50**: § 3's *"Both of those are among the variables `compose.yml`
  does not pass through, so they need the override from §2"* and § 10's *"`compose.yml` passes the
  `app` service a fixed list of variables"* contradict § 2's `env_file` paragraph.
- **The GHCR packages are not anonymously pullable** (401/403 without a login), while operator guide
  § 2 and § 5 teach `docker pull ghcr.io/gtfo-ai/…` as if they were.
- **The run image has no PHP, Composer, Python or pnpm**, and `LOCKFILE_INSTALL_ALLOW` names only
  `npm ci`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pip install -r`, so a non-Node project's tests cannot
  run inside a run (discovery's R1/R2/R6 included).
- WP-133's discovered-work bullet *"the ledger and the budgets take it as reported"* is contradicted by
  the code (above); whether the CLI's `modelUsage` ids match the seeded `price_list` rows under a
  subscription is unmeasured.

#### WP-138

**The Developer opens and updates its merge request** — `open_mr` and `update_mr_description` are real, through `IntegrationActionExecutor`, and the merge request a task has is the platform's record. Rulings (a)–(h) of § "Architect ruling (M8 additions, session 11)". No migration.

- **(a)/(b)/(d) the tools** — `packages/application/src/pipeline/merge-request-tool.ts` (`createMergeRequestTools`), composed by `apps/server/src/platform-tools.ts` (`createMergeRequestToolReader` reads task, project default branch and requester in a short transaction; `IMPLEMENTED_PLATFORM_TOOLS` is now four). Source branch = `tasks.branch ?? taskBranchName(key)`, refused outside `agentic/`; target = `projects.default_branch`. The input schema (`openMrInputSchema`) takes `title`, `description`, optional `draft` (default true); `source_branch`/`target_branch` are still accepted and **ignored** (a model trained on the old shape sends them). Title one line ≤ 255, description ≤ 32 KiB with the cut announced, both redacted with the run's redactor (new optional `PlatformToolContext.redactor`, always supplied by `platform-mcp.ts`; the tool **refuses** a call without it) composed with the binding's; footer *"Opened by the agentic platform for <key>. Requested by <name>."* appended after redaction. A provider `invalid_request` (e.g. the branch is not pushed) is re-thrown naming both branches. Shadow: `would_have`, no provider call, no `mr_ref`.
- **(c) one merge request** — executor key `open_mr:<task>:<branch>`; a `conflict` is answered by `findOpenMergeRequest` + `authenticatedUser` and adopted only when its target is the default branch and its author is the binding's account, else `MergeRequestNotAdoptedError` (`codeMergeRequestWrites.open`, `integrations.ts`). `update_mr_description` addresses only `tasks.mr_ref`, keyed by a digest of the composed text.

**Decisions and assumptions.**
- **The branch before the task has one** is `taskBranchName(key)` — the run's push allow-list already permits it; the workspace still checks out the default branch on a first run, so the prompt names the rule and the tool's refusal names the branch (discovered work below).
- **`saveMergeRequestHead` keeps its version bump** though `save` no longer names `mr_ref`: a handler decision over a pre-push snapshot is still refused and re-made.
- **The duty reads the CI file before the head** (a project with no CI file never asks for a pipeline nor reads its head) — also what keeps the unit walks' scripted pipeline sequences unconsumed.
- **The e2e harness** calls `open_mr` through the production port for every Developer run, hands its seeded merge request to the first task that reaches one (moved to that task's branch), mirrors the seeded CI onto a merge request the tool opened fresh, and — for the `real-over-fake-cli` mode, whose scripted CLI calls no MCP tool — writes the record the tool would through the production store. The unit harness records the reported MR as the tool would (`ScriptedRun.opensMergeRequest`). **Shadow** records nothing in both, except where a case states why it needs the old world (`shadowMergeRequests` / `ScriptedRun.shadowMergeRequest`, WP-34's report tests) — kinder than production, stated at the option.
- **A shadow task's behaviour is changed, stated**: before WP-138 a shadow Developer's `open_mr` was refused and the saga recorded whatever `mr` the artifact claimed (a model-chosen iid — possibly a person's merge request); now nothing is recorded, so a shadow task's CI gate answers `unsupported` and escalates, and the shadow report has no agent diff (discovered work).

#### WP-137

**A static run credential where the provider cannot mint** — TD-028 decision 13 (BD-025's and TD-021's amendments of 2026-10-03, the founder's answer to Q98 (b)) built. Migration **0078** (`runs.credential_source`, `runs.credential_integration_id`).

- **Criterion (1), measured first** (read off the tree, `grep` over `apps/server/src/queries/onboarding-queries.ts` for `update(integrations)`/`insert(integrations)`/`insert(bindings)`): `integrations.config` and its credentials are written by exactly **four** statements — the create (`createIntegration`), the `PATCH` (`updateIntegrationConfig`), the re-seal (`resealIntegrationSecrets`) and the retire (which only deletes) — and `bindings` by one (`replaceProjectBindings`). `mint_credentials` was validated by the GitLab config schema alone (a boolean), and read by `capabilities().credentialMinting`. The refusals land at the create, the `PATCH`, the re-seal and the bindings `PUT`; the run's start re-checks what the load can answer.
- **Declaration** — `packages/integrations/src/static-run-credential.ts`: a registration declares which keys carry it (`ProviderRegistration.staticRunCredential`, checked against `configSchema`/`secretFields` at registration, git only, token ≠ API field), and the provider-neutral readers (`staticRunCredentialConfigIssues`, `staticRunCredentialWriteIssues`, `staticRunCredentialOf`, `expiryInstantOf`). GitLab: `run_credential: minted | static` (default `minted`), secret `run_token`, `run_token_username`, `run_token_expires_at` (`z.iso.date()`); `GITLAB_STATIC_RUN_CREDENTIAL`, and `gitlabAdapterInput` builds the adapter **without** `run_token` (config and secrets). The cross-field rules are not a zod refinement because the catalogue's `omit` refuses a refined object (measured: *".omit() cannot be used on object schemas containing refinements"*); `configIssuesOf` appends them.
- **Load → use** — the loader reads `GitBinding.staticRunCredential` (value, username, expiry instant, `sameAsApiToken` from the two decrypted values, config `refusal`); `runCredentialWrites.mint` answers a third kind `static` before asking about minting, `unavailable` for a shadow task (decision 13 item 4), and throws `StaticRunCredentialRefusedError` for no token, a short one, the API token, a config fault, no clock or a passed expiry; the refusal with neither source names the binding, **both** settings (`CredentialMintingHints.static`, GitLab's in its registration) and the API token never sent. `apps/server/src/workspaces.ts` registers the value with the run's secrets, returns it on the minted path (`source: 'static'`, no-op revoke), turns a refusal into `WorkspaceError('invalid_spec')` before the create, and records `credential_source` (`recordCredentialSource`, narrow, before the create). The wire (`runCredentialSchema.source`, optional, absent = `minted`), the broker and the provisioner accept a **static** push credential on a read-only spec and nothing else.
- **Probe** — `GitProviderPort.projectMemberAccess(project, username)` (port, fake divergence 24, GitLab `GET /users?username=` + `GET /projects/:id/members/all/:user_id`, `project-members.json` with `source` blocks, SOURCES.md WP-137 section, shared contract case); `createIntegrationProber` adds a `run_credential` check through the executor (`check_run_credential_member`, a read with the API token) on the one bound project (`boundProjectPathReader`), refuses a role that cannot push (`pushes`, Developer and above) and one that `administers` (Maintainer and above), fails (never passes) when unbound or uncomposed, and always says it cannot confirm the token's owner; the route returns every check and stores the failing one's detail.
- **Leak search** — `addedLinesContain` (domain) and `parkOnStaticRunTokenLeak` in `dependency-gate.ts`: an added line carrying the exact token escalates the task (`escalateTaskWithBrief`) with *"Rotate the run token now"*, never printing it, before anything else of the gate runs.

(8) is the product owner's.

**Decisions and assumptions.**
- **The expiry instant is 00:00 UTC on the declared date** — GitLab's own reading of a personal access token's `expires_at` (review round 1 corrected an earlier "a day early" wording). "At most 90 days ahead" is measured from the write's instant to that midnight.
- **A broken static declaration refuses every run with a checkout, read-only included** (`invalid_spec`), rather than letting a read-only run fetch anonymously: the operator declared a source, and falling back silently would be rule 18's permissive default. A **shadow** task, by contrast, gets `unavailable`, exactly as decision 13 item 4 says, so a shadow read-only run fetches anonymously and a shadow writing run is refused.
- **`run_token_username` is required with `static`** (decision 13 says GitLab "takes" it): the probe needs it, and git sends it beside the token.
- **The probe's check fails when no single project is bound** (unbound, or — impossible past the write — more than one), and when the composition gave no reader; it never reports a check it did not make as passed. The integration's `health` then stores the failing check's detail.
- **`run_credential`, `run_token_username` and `run_token_expires_at` are GitLab's `accountOnlyFields`** (decision 13 item 1 puts the declaration on the integration): a binding overlay could otherwise switch one project of a minted account to `static`, past the one-binding rule, which reads the account's document. `apps/server/src/queries/onboarding-queries.test.ts` › "refuses run_credential on a GitLab binding, so no project switches its account to static". GitLab declared no account-only field before, so a binding may still set `mint_credentials` — pre-existing, left (discovered work).
- **The probe also refuses a role that cannot push** (below Developer), beside decision 13's *above Developer*: a Reporter's token would fetch and then fail every writing stage at its push, and the check exists to say whether the declared user is the one decision 13 describes. Recorded here as an extension, not a re-reading of the decision.
- **The probe looks the project up first** (`GET /projects/:id`), so an unknown project is `not_found` whatever the username.
- **Binding uniqueness is serialised by a transaction-scoped advisory lock per integration** (`hashtextextended('static-run-credential:<id>')`), taken by the bindings `PUT` and by a `PATCH` into `static` after their row locks; the bindings `PUT` holds integration rows only `for share`, so two projects' writes would otherwise both pass.
- **`createIntegration` reads every referenced variable before it seals any**, so the equality check runs before a single ciphertext exists (it read and sealed in one loop before).
- **`credential_source` is written from the runner's provision on the pool** (the run row is committed before provisioning), narrow, two columns; `none` with an integration id is a refused static credential.
- **The wire's `source` is optional, absent = `minted`**, so an absent field falls under the strict rule; the launcher check exercises the minted path unchanged.
- **The provisioner's refusal sentence** reads *"no git credential can be given to it"* (was *"…can be minted for it"*), because the reason after it now names both settings.

**Sentences falsified** (grep over `docs/`, `packages/`, `apps/`, `test/`, `scripts/`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` for `mint_credentials`, `Premium or Ultimate`, `cannot mint`, `minting setting is off`, `read credential or none`, the runbook's GitLab section):

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed).
- **The leak search reads only the Developer stage's diff** (the dependency gate's trigger): a token pushed by a later stage (conflict resolution, a CI fix) into the same merge request is searched only when the Developer stage completes again. Also bounded by the gate's per-file patch bound and file bound, and blind to an encoded or split token.
- **A GitLab binding overlay may set `mint_credentials`** (GitLab declares it no account-only field), so one project of an account that does not mint can turn minting on for itself; decision 13's one-source rule reads the account's document.
- **No screen shows `runs.credential_source`**: it is on the row, not on `GET /api/runs/:id` or the run page.
- **No warning before a static token's declared expiry**: the first signal is a refused run on the day.
- **The probe's `run_credential` check reads the bound project's path from `projects.repo_url`**, not from the integration's `project` key; a binding whose `repo_url` names another namespace than the token's project is checked against the URL's.

**Residuals.**
- Nothing was measured on gitlab.com (criterion (8), `docs/TODO.md`): the declared username over git HTTPS, the members endpoint's 404 for a non-member (inferred), and the dedicated user's push to a protected default branch being refused.
- Whether the run token belongs to the declared user cannot be checked without using it, which decision 13 item 3 forbids; the probe says so.
- A static token is not revoked when a run ends: a run that exfiltrates it within its egress (the git host) holds a working token until the declared expiry — decision 13 item 5, stated on four pages.

- **(a) where** — `gates.ts`: the evaluator's `ci_gate` branch answers a `pending` with `ciWait` (`CiWait`: the timeout read at this evaluation, the binding's provider id, the head pipeline it saw or `null`) **only** when `bindings.git.port.pollPlan()?.receives_webhooks === false` (`withCiWait`). A webhook binding, a binding with **no** poll plan (polling off), and every other gate answer `pending` exactly as before and keep `MAX_GATE_CHECKS`. The settings are read only on a pending CI read on such a binding.
- **(b)/(c) the clock and the cadence** — `packages/application/src/pipeline/ci-wait.ts` (pure: `decideCiWait`, `ciWaitBackstopChecks`, the brief and the reason) and `jobs.ts` `waitForPollOnlyCi`: every fire reads the attempt's own `task_stages` row through the new `TaskRepository.stageAttemptEntry` (both stores; `entered_at` is the database's `clock_timestamp()`, the memory store's `now`), and decides: elapsed ≥ `ci_timeout_minutes` → park; checks ≥ `ceil(timeout / 60 s) + 5` → park (backstop); else re-enqueue after 30 s for checks 1–4 and 60 s after. A **closed** row (a hand-back opened a new attempt; an escalation closed it) → the fire does nothing. **No row** → the five-check bound, logged (rule 16: no invented clock).
- **(d) config** — `pipeline.limits.ci_timeout_minutes` (`packages/contracts/src/config.ts`, `MIN/MAX/DEFAULT_CI_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` 10/1440/60), in `PLATFORM_DEFAULT_CONFIG` so the pipeline screen shows it with its source, graded `operational` (`repository-grades.ts`), `schemas/agentic-config.schema.json` regenerated, technical/12's limits block and grade table. `ciTimeoutMinutesOf` re-checks the number and falls back to 60 (rule 16).
- **(e) the brief** — the ruling's sentence, e.g. *"The CI pipeline pipeline-9 for this merge request was still running after 60 minutes — the CI timeout (`pipeline.limits.ci_timeout_minutes = 60`). This project's fake-git binding is poll-only, so the platform asked fake-git every minute rather than waiting for a webhook. Look at the pipeline; when it has finished, hand the task back at ci_gate. If pipelines here routinely take longer, raise ci_timeout_minutes."*; *"No CI pipeline has started for the head commit of this merge request after <n> minutes …"* when there is none; a backstop park says so. Outcome `undecided` as before.

**Criteria → tests** (canaries by Edit-tool mutation, md5 restored, rule 88):
- (1) *measure first* — read off `packages/integrations/src/providers/gitlab/mapping.test.ts` (no gitlab.com credential): GitLab's `created`, `waiting_for_resource`, `preparing`, `waiting_for_callback`, `scheduled` map to `pending`, `canceling` to `running`, `manual` to `manual`; `gates.ts` treats everything outside `success` and `failed`/`canceled`/`skipped` as pending. **Decisions and assumptions.**
- **A binding with no poll plan keeps five checks.** The ruling's condition is the plan's `receives_webhooks: false`; GitLab answers `null` when `poll_enabled` is off, and the platform then cannot tell from the port whether a webhook reaches it. Such a binding hears nothing at all, which the five-check park already surfaces.
- **A resume is not a new entry.** A pause closes no `task_stages` row, so a task resumed at `ci_gate` keeps its clock; resumed past its timeout, it gets one read and parks if the pipeline is still pending. A hand-back at `ci_gate` is the fresh clock (the ruling).
- **The brief names the provider id** (`gitlab`) where the ruling's text says "GitLab", because the pipeline does not know which provider it talks to (BD-017); on Autix it reads "This project's gitlab binding is poll-only, so the platform asked gitlab every minute …".
- **The reason** (the row's and `task.escalated`'s) is the timeout sentence plus *"; the last read: <detail>"*, so a pending that came from the tamper check's empty diff is still named.
- **The configuration-refusal census** declares the new settings read (`config-refusal-readers.test.ts`): on a refused configuration the wait uses the default 60 and parks (closed); the settlement it waits for refuses the configuration by name.
- **The harness** wires the memory store's `now` to the test clock (`entered_at`), and its stub git answers `pollPlan: () => null`.

**Sentences falsified** (grep: "five times", "about two minutes", "30 seconds", "Hand back", "MAX_GATE_CHECKS", "two and a half", "could not be decided after", ci_gate in the runbook and the guides):
- **Fixed**: `docs/first-local-test.md:341` (the row) and § 8's paragraph ("30 seconds, five times in all", "about two minutes", "with five fresh checks"); its WP-138 sentence "a process that has none cannot tell, and waits too" now names the timeout; `packages/integrations/src/providers/gitlab/setup-guide.md` ("The CI gate does not need the pipeline event (it asks GitLab for the head's pipeline itself)" — true only with a bound, now stated); `docs/operator-guide.md` § 4 (a paragraph on the wait); technical/02 (the empty-diff pending "until `MAX_GATE_CHECKS`"); technical/12; `jobs.ts` (`GATE_RECHECK_MS`'s "two and a half minutes", the escalate outcome's comment), `ci-settle.ts:141`, `ready-head.ts:59`.
- **Still true, left**: `docs/first-local-test.md:100` and `:396` (finished pipelines are webhook-only), `:333–335` (generic hand-backs), `docs/user-guide.md` (no sentence about the gate's re-check count), `TD-028:78` (a gate pending when the runner stopped never escalates — still so; a decision record, not this row's), PROGRESS history.

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed).
- **The timeout is measured between two clocks**: `entered_at` is the database's `clock_timestamp()` and the fire's "now" is the process clock, so a skew between the database host and the runner shifts the timeout by the skew (seconds on one host; unmeasured across hosts).
- **The CI timeout is not shown on the task page while the gate waits** (only in the brief at the end); a person watching a task at `ci_gate` cannot see how long it will wait.

**Residuals.**
- Nothing was measured on gitlab.com: the status mapping is the adapter's table, and the wait's provider reads (at most sixty an hour per waiting task) are not checked against gitlab.com's rate limit for a project with many waiting tasks.
- No e2e drives the wait (the server's clock is real time); the unit tier drives it on the harness clock and the contract and integration tiers hold `stageAttemptEntry` on both stores.

**Decisions and assumptions.**
- **The capability is `project.pipeline.write` (maintainer), not `project.settings.write`.** The ruling names `project.settings.write` *and* says "a maintainer can change it" *and* criterion (2) is "403 below maintainer"; on this build `project.settings.write` is **admin** (`permissions.ts`), so the name would have made it an administrator's. The role decided over the name — the reading WP-94 made for the re-evaluate button. Stated in the route's docblock and technical/08.
- **"Prefilled when a binding is known"** — a new project has no binding at creation (bindings are per project and come after the create), so the create field is **required and empty**; the prefill is the change control shown in step 1 once the git integration is bound (and on the settings page). No provider read happens at creation.
- **A provider read from an HTTP GET.** `GET …/repository` makes one executor read per request (audited, rate-limited, keyed to the binding) — the second HTTP-triggered outbound call after the probe. The screen's query is `staleTime: ∞` and is invalidated by a bindings save and a branch change.
- **The PUT does not check the branch exists on the provider** — the read shows the provider's answer beside it; a branch GitLab does not have fails at the next run's clone (named in the runbook's § 8 row).
- **The presence read** is the one widening of `RepositoryFileSource`'s exact-path list, and it reads no byte; `.gitlab-ci.yml` (in the list since WP-94) still goes through the existing read so no stub changed behaviour.
- **An absent `ci_config_path` is `unknown`, never the default** — the default would read a custom-path project as "no CI" for a token that may not read code, which is this row's defect.

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed).
- **Intake does not take the project row's lock**, so a task created in the same instant as a default-branch change is not counted by the change's live-task check (stated at `writeProjectDefaultBranch`).
- **A change of default branch leaves the knowledge index and the repository configuration reading on the old branch** until the next index run or `default_branch.moved`; nothing re-reads on the change, and the index's recorded commit is not an ancestor of the new branch.
- **A custom CI path is not a protected path by default** (`protected_paths` names `.gitlab-ci.yml`); GoParking's `deploy/.gitlab-ci.yml` is editable by an agent unless the project adds it. The tamper check could read the provider's location.
- **The readiness re-check's R13 reads `.gitlab-ci.yml` only** (`READINESS_TREE_PATHS`), so a custom-path project's secret-scanning CI is not seen.

**Residuals.**
- Nothing was measured on a GitLab instance: `ci_config_path`'s shape on gitlab.com or `gitlab.fontai.org`, whether a Maintainer's token sees it (it should: `read_code`), and the 633 MB first clone against the 10-minute create bound (the figure is the review's, not measured).
- `GET …/repository` answers 500 when the binding fails to **load** (a decryption fault), as every other binding read does (rule 20); only a provider `IntegrationError` becomes `provider_unavailable`.

**Decisions and assumptions.**

- **`StaticRunCredentialSupport.scopeProofHint` carries the provider's words** for the `2xx` refusal, so the prober names no provider (BD-017).

#### WP-141 — review round 1 (REQUEST CHANGES), addressed

1. **[major] Any 403 passed the scope proof.** A proxy or firewall in front of gitlab.com, or GitLab's terms-of-service block, answers 403 to a token that may call the API. `runTokenApiAccess` now sets `refusedForScope` only for a `403` whose `error` is `insufficient_scope` (`INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, the documented body), and the prober refuses any other 403 by name with its code (*"answered 403 with no error code, not a refusal for the token's scope"*). Fixture: an **inferred** 403 (the status documented, the body guessed) `{"message":"403 Forbidden"}` for `FAKE-run-token-blocked-by-proxy-…` in `run-token-scope.json` (SOURCES.md says so; the GitLab corpus requires a vendor URL, which an `invented` label forbids). Cases: `test/contract/integrations/gitlab-run-token-probe.contract.test.ts` › "refuses a 403 that is not a refusal for the token’s scope, naming what it was"; the shared suite's scope-proof case gains `runTokens.blockedElsewhere` (fake and replay). Consequence, stated in `docs/TODO.md`: if gitlab.com's real body differs from the documented one, a genuine repository-only token is **refused** (fail closed) and the detail names the code seen.
2. **[major] Only the exact rule was read.** GitLab applies *"the most permissive rule"* of every rule matching a branch, wildcards included (the protected-branches page, cited). `branchPushProtection` now lists `GET /projects/:id/protected_branches` (paged, new `client.protectedBranches`, action `list_protected_branches`), filters with `gitlabBranchRuleMatches` (`*` = any run of characters including `/`, case-sensitive) and combines: nobody pushes only if every push entry of every matching rule is `0` with no user/group/deploy key; force push if any rule allows it; a wildcard's pushers are named with their rule. The single-rule fixtures were replaced by one list fixture: `release` exact No one loosened by `rel*` Maintainers, `stable` exact No one with force push off loosened by `st*` force push, `*-hotfix` force push. Cases: the probe contract file's protection `it.each` (`release` → *"lets No one, Maintainers (rule rel*) push"*, `main-hotfix` → force push); the `gitlabBranchRuleMatches (WP-141)` table in the GitLab provider's unit tests (the page's own examples, regex metacharacters escaped). The wildcard's `includes('*')`/`split('*')` is admitted in `scripts/source-scanner.test.ts`'s allow-list of comment-stripper shapes, with its reason. **Not read**: group-level protected branches (Premium), stated in the guide and technical/05.

**A readiness warning when the CI rules give an `agentic/` merge request no test job** — rulings (a)–(e) of the row (plan § "Milestone M8"), Q114, backlog 442's CI-path half. Implementer, session 11, on `97e3d669`. Migration **0079**.

- **(a)/(b)/(c) the evaluator** — `packages/domain/src/readiness/ci-rules.ts`, pure: `evaluateCiExpression` (`==`, `!=`, `=~`, `!~`, `&&` over `||`, parentheses, `null`, `$VAR`/`${VAR}`, three-valued), `evaluateCiRules` (two contexts — `pushContextFor`/`mergeRequestContextFor` of `agentic/X-1` into the stored default branch — over `workflow:rules`, job `rules:` and `only`/`except`; per job `runs`/`skipped`/`unknown` with the deciding rule) and `ciRulesNotice` (the warning `ci_rules_skip_agent_branch`, the note `ci_rules_not_seen`, or `null`). A rule whose match is unknown adds its outcome and the list goes on; a job is decided when its possible outcomes agree (so `$CI_COMMIT_MESSAGE =~ /^WIP/ → manual` in front of rules that skip the branch still decides *skipped*). Unknown: `include:` (any kind — no evaluation), `extends`, `!reference` (anywhere in a job's `rules`/`only`/`except`/`when`, or `workflow:rules`), `changes:`, `exists:`, `trigger:`, mixed `rules`+`only`, a variable a context does not set, an RE2 pattern JavaScript cannot compile, an expression it cannot parse, an `only` key other than `refs`/`variables`, a `ref@project`. The YAML is parsed by `yamlCiParser` (`packages/infrastructure/src/config/ci-yaml-parser.ts`): `<<` merge keys resolved (Autix's templates carry `stage:`), `!reference` a custom tag kept as the `{'!reference': [...]}` marker, any other tag or parser warning a refusal, the codec's alias ceiling.
- **The reads** — `createCiRulesProbe` (`packages/application/src/onboarding/ci-rules.ts`): the provider's location through `gitReads.ciConfigLocation` (executor, outside any transaction); an external location is a *not read* note with no file read; a repository path is read from the mirror at the re-check's commit through a **new** `RepositoryFileRequest.ciConfigPath` (the one provider-named path whose bytes are read, `isPresencePath`, 64 KiB bound, answered as `ciConfig`; `git-vault.ts`). The file is **redacted with the git binding's redactor before it is parsed** (TD-012), and the path shown is the redacted one. A provider `IntegrationError` or a mirror refusal is a note; anything else propagates (rule 20).
- **(d) when the warning fires** — in **both** contexts no *counted* job runs and none is unknown, `workflow:rules` (when present) decided, no `include:`. Counted = the jobs in stage `test` (absent `stage:` is `test`), or every job when the file has none there. The message names the first counted job's deciding rule (a `when: never` rule that matched, else the first rule over a branch variable that evaluated false, else "no rule matched", else the `workflow` rule) and the fix (*admit agentic/*, e.g. `^(feature|bugfix|agentic)/`). Otherwise anything unknown among the counted jobs gives the note, listing what was not seen (four, then "and N more") and what runs where it is decided. Message ≤ 1 200 characters, each quoted name or expression ≤ 120.

- **(e) where it is computed** — the discovery record job (default branch's head) and the re-check after a merge (pinned to the index run's commit), both composed in `apps/server/src/onboarding.ts` with one probe. It never blocks anything and changes no level (BD-026).
- **UI** — `apps/web/src/features/readiness-notices.tsx` (`ReadinessNotices`), rendered on the wizard's discovery step (its readiness panel) and on the project settings page; a warning is a `role="alert"` item, the message through `UntrustedText`.

**Decisions and assumptions.**
- **"no job in stage `test` and no job at all"** is read as one test: the counted jobs are those in stage `test`, or every job when the file has none in `test`. Literal "no job at all" would miss a partial pipeline; "stage test" alone would warn on every file that names its stages otherwise.
- **"nothing is unknown"** is read as nothing unknown that could change the answer: the file (`include:`), `workflow:rules`, and the counted jobs. An unknown job outside the counted set (a `trigger:` deploy) cannot make a test run, so it does not block the warning — read strictly, Autix's `deploy:documan:hetzner` trigger alone would silence it forever.

- **`when: manual`, `never`, `on_failure` count as not running.** `CI_COMMIT_BRANCH` is null in the MR context (GitLab's variable page, retrieved 2026-10-04); a branch name or regex in `only:` never admits a merge-request pipeline (only `merge_requests` does — read off the deprecated-keywords page, not measured); `CI_COMMIT_REF_NAME` is the source branch in both contexts.

Proposed: *"Beside the criteria, an evaluation may carry a platform notice — today the CI-rules warning that the default branch's CI would give an `agentic/` branch no test job; it changes no level and blocks nothing."*
- **Every** CI-gate tamper check now makes one provider read (`ciConfigLocation`), and it fails closed: during a provider outage the gate answers `pending` even for a project whose CI is the root `.gitlab-ci.yml` (a behaviour change, bounded by the gate's own wait); the planner's write-time path guard does **not** add the custom CI path (it would need a provider read in the plan phase) — a run can still edit `deploy/.gitlab-ci.yml`, and the CI gate then returns it.

**Sentences falsified** (grep: `presence only`, `never a read`, `reads no byte`, `R13`, `.gitlab-ci.yml` in readiness/user-guide, `protected_paths`):

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed).
- The planner's write-time path guard does not protect a custom CI path (above); the tamper check does.
- `extends` and local `!reference` resolution would make the evaluator decide more jobs (Autix's `codeception`, `crawler-test`, `e2e:*`); filed as a possibility, not done.
- `changes:` in a merge-request rule is always unknown, which silences the warning on any project that filters MR jobs by path (Autix: six test jobs).

**Residuals.**
- Nothing was run against GitLab: the variable sets of both contexts, `only: refs` in an MR pipeline, and RE2-vs-JavaScript regex differences (a pattern both compile but read differently — e.g. RE2 has no lookaround, JS's `\d` vs RE2's — is evaluated as JavaScript reads it).
- The CI file now reaches the platform's memory at every discovery and re-check (64 KiB bound); nothing of it is stored but the notice's bounded, redacted names and one expression.
- A re-check whose mirror read failed still computes the notice (the probe reads separately); a provider outage gives a note that replaces a previous warning until the next re-check.

- **[minor]** the tamper check's provider read on every evaluation, failing closed, is stated above.
- **[nit]** a value nested past the depth bound now reads *"nests too deep or cyclically"*, not *"uses !reference"* (`unreadableIn`).

#### WP-144

**A run in flight when its `runner` stops is handed back and retried, bounded** (backlog 432). Built on `a4612368`.

**Measured first.** Through two `apps/server` processes on one database (`app` ROLE=all, `runner` ROLE=runner over the fake CLI, the session held open), `runner.stop()` — the `runtime.stop()` `main.ts` calls on SIGTERM — with the hand-back disabled (a temporary edit, reverted) had not returned when a 90 s bound killed the test (≥ ~84 s of stop; WP-133 read 60 s). With it: **16 ms**. Against a real daemon (`launcher-control-plane-check`, a CLI that never answers the interrupt): **5.7 s** from `stop({ reason: 'shutdown' })` to the outcome, including the launcher's removal of the container and network — the runner's 5 s interrupt grace is most of it; budget 10 s.

**Built.**
- `run_terminal_reason` gains `shutdown` (migration **0080**, zod enum, drizzle enum, schemas regenerated). `RunStop` gains `{ reason: 'shutdown' }`; the real runner maps it to `failed`/`shutdown` and reads the interrupted turn's result (unmeasured otherwise); the fake runner the same.
- `LiveRuns.stopAll(stop)` stops every live run and **closes** the register, so a run that registers after it is stopped as it registers. `createPipelineRuntime`'s `stop()` tells every worker to stop taking jobs (pg-boss sets the flag synchronously), then calls `liveRuns.stopAll({ reason: 'shutdown' })`, then awaits the drains; `apps/server/src/pipeline.ts` passes the register when the process runs agents.
- Stage executor: a `shutdown` outcome on a still-current entry ends the run `failed`/`shutdown` with what it measured (null cost columns when nothing — rule 16), adds the spend once, leaves the task untouched and returns `handed_back`; `stage.execute` re-enqueues the **same** entry (`task`, `stage`, `attempt`, overrides) after `SHUTDOWN_HAND_BACK_DELAY_MS` (30 s). Bound `MAX_SHUTDOWN_HAND_BACKS` = 2, counted by the new `RunRepository.shutdownEndings` (runs of the entry joined through `task_stage_id`, `terminal_reason = 'shutdown'`; SQL and memory adapters, contract case); the third escalates with a brief naming the stops. A task a person moved meanwhile is recorded onto (`recordOntoStoppedTask`), never re-run; a run another writer ended goes through `lostTheRun`'s late cost.
- Ask executor: the same for `task.ask` — run ended `shutdown`, the question stays `pending`, the job re-enqueued with `hand_backs` in its payload after `ASK_HAND_BACK_DELAY_MS`; the third ends the question `failed` by name. `asksWithEndedRun` leaves a `shutdown`-ended ask alone for an hour past its grace (the re-enqueued job waits for a runner).
- Docs: operator guide § upgrade (a stop is safe; twice per stage; measured), `docs/first-local-test.md`, `compose.yml`'s `runner` grace comment, technical/03 (`runs`), technical/04 (resume and take-over amendment), the launcher check's docblock.

**Criteria and tests.**
- (1) `test/e2e/topology/two-processes.e2e.test.ts` › "hands the run back inside 10 s, charges it once, and a runner that starts again runs the same stage" (canary: the register not passed to the runtime → the stop never returns; killed at 90 s). Real daemon: the `launcher-control-plane-check.mjs` record for WP-144 (a live run stopped for shutdown ends failed/shutdown inside 10 s, its workspace released; 55/55).
- (2) stage run — `packages/application/src/pipeline/shutdown-hand-back.test.ts` › "ends the run failed/shutdown, leaves the task at its stage, and re-enqueues the same entry 30 s later", "starts a new run of the same stage when the job fires, and the task never needs a human"; ask run — `packages/application/src/ask/ask-pipeline.test.ts` › "keeps the question pending, re-enqueues it, and answers it on the next run", "ends the question failed at its third stop, naming the stops"; a run already finished — `packages/application/src/pipeline/live-runs.test.ts` › "stops nothing for a run that finished on its own before the stop", and `shutdown-hand-back.test.ts` › "starts no second run when the entry ended before the handed-back job fires (TD-004)"; a cancelled run — `shutdown-hand-back.test.ts` › "does not re-run a stage whose task a person paused during the stop (a cancel stands)"; the third stop — `shutdown-hand-back.test.ts` › "escalates the third stop, with a brief naming the stops, and queues nothing more". Runner mapping: `packages/infrastructure/src/runner/claude-runner.test.ts` › "ends the run failed/shutdown with the interrupted turn’s measured cost", "says nothing was measured when the interrupted turn sent no result (rule 16)".
- (3) The real-daemon `docker compose stop runner` leg is **not built** (below); the launcher-check leg and the two-process e2e cover its halves.
- (4) Canaries — `shutdown-hand-back.test.ts` › "ends the first run before the second exists: the re-enqueued job finds no live run", "charges a handed-back run once, not late, and the next run separately", "writes no figure and no ledger row for a hand-back whose stop measured nothing (rule 16)"; the e2e asserts one `cost_entries` row, not late. Mutation canaries run: the bound raised to 3 and the re-enqueue removed → 6 of 9 cases fail.
- (5) Operator guide rewritten (above). Ask recovery: `test/integration/recovery/stranded-store.integration.test.ts` › "leaves a handed-back ask alone for an hour past the grace, then ends it (WP-144)" (fails without the predicate).

**Decisions and assumptions.**
- **The re-enqueue is after the run's ending commits, not in its transaction** as ruling (a) says: the `Jobs` port has no transactional enqueue (`Jobs.enqueue` does not join a transaction, CLAUDE.md) and the existing start-retry path has the same shape. A process that dies between the commit and the enqueue leaves an entry whose run ended — the stranded-stage recovery escalates it naming `shutdown` (ruling (d)'s crash class). Proposed correction to the plan row's wording.
- **"Releases its reservation … through the existing late-cost path"** is read as: the run's own ending (`runs.finish` with what it measured) releases the org/project reservation, as for every ending; the late-cost path is used only when another writer ended the row first. An unmeasured hand-back stays held at its reservation by the task cap (WP-131), unchanged.
- **The ask's bound rides the job payload** (`hand_backs`), because `task_asks` keeps one `run_id`; no column is added.
- **A run started after the stop** (a job fetched in the instant before the worker's flag) is handed back immediately and counts as one of the entry's two.
- The workers' drains are now awaited **concurrently** rather than one by one (each was already independent).

**Sentences falsified** (grep: `stops a run on SIGTERM`, `no agent run in progress`, `does not save the run`, `still waiting 60`, `nothing interrupts a run`, `interrupted by restart are resumed`):
- **Fixed**: `compose.yml` (`runner` grace comment); `docs/operator-guide.md` § upgrade; `docs/first-local-test.md` (stop bullet); technical/04 (the *"runs interrupted by restart are resumed … once"* sentence, never built — amended).
- **Left, judged still true**: `docs/operator-guide.md:` the WP-126 network upgrade's *"with no agent run in progress"* (a one-off `down`; a hand-back would survive it, the advice is merely cautious).
- **For the orchestrator**: CLAUDE.md's *"45/45 since WP-118"* for the launcher check is stale (55/55 now); backlog 432 can be closed.

**Verification.** `PASS: verify` (twice; 524 files, 10 596 tests, coverage ratchet PASS), `PASS: verify:integration` (81 files, 809), `PASS: verify:e2e` (64 files, 278), `PASS: launcher-control-plane-check (55/55)`. `verify:ui` not run (nothing under `apps/web`). Volume count 161 before and after the Docker check (one anonymous volume appeared during the e2e tier, belonging to another project's `registry:2` container). **Machine-rule breach, recorded**: `verify:integration` was started in the same command as its `uptime` reading, which read 28.5 (the spike from the `verify` that had just finished); the e2e tier then waited for three readings (26.9, 12.1, 7.7).

**Discovered work** (no numbers claimed).
- The real-daemon `docker compose stop runner` leg (criterion 3) needs a compose instance with a project, a ticket and a held run — no fake provider is reachable from a compose stack today; not built.
- The stranded-stage recovery escalates an entry whose newest run ended `shutdown` and whose re-enqueue was lost; it could re-enqueue once instead (inside the bound).
- `RunHandle.stop` for `shutdown` waits the full 5 s interrupt grace when the CLI does not answer; a real CLI's interrupt timing is unmeasured (WP-33's credential).

**Residuals.** A SIGKILL, an OOM kill, `docker kill` or the 45 s grace running out are still the lease sweep's (`lease_expired`, then *Needs human*). Work the interrupted run had not pushed is lost. With several stopping runners, the 10 s budget is per run in parallel, not summed (stops are issued together).

page: the field searches *"using their unique identifier or ID number"*, aliases `id`/`issue`/`key`,

as a duplicate, no fix) reports JQL naming a former key *"breaks"*. So
`test/fixtures/http/jira-cloud/search-jql-by-id-after-move.json` is **`inferred`**, both sources are in
`SOURCES.md`, and `docs/TODO.md`'s row keeps the three reads owed on a Cloud site. Nothing relies on an
old key resolving.

**Decisions.**
- **(a)** `recordTicketSignal` takes `ticketId`: with one, a task matches by id when it has one, by key
  only when it has none; without one, by key (as before). `ticket.updated` already carried the id
  (WP-134's `issueRef`) on the webhook and the poll.
- **(b)** new narrow writer `rekeyTicket` (compare-and-set on the old key, live rows, refused — not
  raised — while another task of the project holds the new key in the same mode); it sets

  stream, `PIPELINE_ACTOR`, appended in the handler's transaction after the writer's row lock and a
  re-load (conflict-warning's order); declared unconsumed. The MR is never retitled. Done/cancelled
  tasks are not re-keyed.
- **(c)** the port's `keys` rule gains `ids` (1–100 terms together); the poll store's
  `liveTicketKeys` became `liveTickets` (`{key, id}`, one row per issue); Jira builds

#### WP-146

**A project SSH deploy key as the run credential** — TD-028 decision 13b (BD-025's and TD-021's amendments of 2026-10-04) built, end to end, and run against a local SSH server standing in for `altssh.gitlab.com`. Migration **0081** (`runs.credential_source` gains `deploy_key`).

- **Setting** — `run_credential: deploy_key` on the GitLab integration (gitlab.com only), the secret `run_ssh_private_key` (an unencrypted OpenSSH Ed25519 key) and the account-only `run_ssh_public_key`. Provider-neutral: `StaticRunCredentialSupport.deployKey` (`modeValue`, the two fields, `sshRoute`) beside WP-137's declaration, registry-checked (fields in the schema, the private one sealed); `deployKeyConfigIssues` (folded into `staticRunCredentialConfigIssues`, so `configIssuesOf` and every write ask it), `deployKeyWriteIssues` (folded into `assertStaticRunCredentialWrite`), `deployKeyRunCredentialOf` (the loader → `GitBinding.deployKeyRunCredential`, with `redactedAs`), `declaresDedicatedRunCredential` (the one-binding rule's three sites), and `withoutRunOnlyFields` strips the private key from the adapter's input. The key half is `packages/application/src/integrations/ssh-deploy-key.ts`: an `openssh-key-v1` reader (refuses a passphrase, another type, a PEM key, two keys, unequal check integers, a container whose public halves are not the seed's), the public key **derived** from the seed through PKCS #8 (Node 24 refuses a JWK with `d` and no `x`, measured), and `signSshEd25519` (RFC 8709 blob). GitLab's route: `providers/gitlab/ssh-route.ts` — `altssh.gitlab.com:443`, `HostKeyAlias gitlab.com`, the three documented `known_hosts` lines; any other `base_url` is refused with decision 13b item 4's sentence.
- **Mint → run** — `runCredentialWrites.mint` answers `deploy_key` (shadow → `unavailable`; a fault or no route → `StaticRunCredentialRefusedError`, terminal, before the create); `apps/server/src/workspaces.ts` registers the key with the run's secrets (expiry = the run credential's TTL), records `credential_source = deploy_key` and hands it on the minted path as `source: 'deploy_key'` with `ssh: { publicKey, route }` (`password` carries the key text — decided, below). The provisioner parses the key into a `DeployKeySigner` (`launcher/deploy-key-signer.ts`: its own key blob only, ≤ 8 KiB data, ≤ 128 signatures, counts logged at release), puts the route on the spec (`WorkspaceRepo.ssh`, all public) and its CONNECT host on that run's egress list (`withGitSsh`), and wires `sshSigner` into the spawn. The wire refuses a deploy key without a route, a route without a key, a CONNECT host not on the list and port 22; the broker holds the key **with** its route and answers `cred.get` for it with `null`.
- **The container** — the launcher writes `/ctl/<run>/known_hosts` (the prepare helper), gives the shim `RUNLET_SSH_AGENT_SOCKET=/ctl/ssh-agent.sock` and `RUNLET_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`, and `cliEnvironment` answers `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` (new `WorkspaceCliEnvironment.gitSshCommand`, optional on the wire) and one `url.ssh://git@altssh.gitlab.com:443/.insteadOf = https://gitlab.com/` pair **instead of** the credential helper (the wire's key pattern admits exactly that subsection). `WorkspaceHandle.gitSsh` (optional) keeps `cliEnvironment` derived from the handle. `GIT_SSH` is a reserved project-variable prefix. The shim (`runlet/ssh-agent.ts`) answers `REQUEST_IDENTITIES` from its environment and relays `SIGN_REQUEST` as the new `ssh.sign` frame (`@platform/contracts`, with `ssh.sign.reply`), bounded (64 per run, the credential concurrency, only while the child runs), and answers every other request `SSH_AGENT_FAILURE`. `agentic-runlet connect --proxy <url> <host> <port>` is the `ProxyCommand` (`runlet/connect-helper.ts`). The launcher's mirror and export helpers write the key to `/tmp/agentic-ssh/key` (`umask 077`) on their own tmpfs and fetch/push over SSH directly (helper network), never through a credential helper.
- **Probe** — `GitProviderPort.deployKeyAccess(project, publicKey)` (GitLab `GET /projects/:id/deploy_keys`, paged, matched by type and base64; fake divergence 29; shared contract case; `deploy-keys.json` `documented-adapted`, SOURCES.md WP-146 section). The prober's `checkDeployKey`: `run_credential` (`check_deploy_key`, write access required) and `default_branch_protection` (push "No one", which admits no deploy key; `deployKeyProtectionFault`), both with the API token, both stating the platform cannot see the key's other projects; a self-managed host or no binding fails both, asking nothing.
- **Leak search** — `deployKeyNeedles`/`deployKeyLeaks` and `parkOnDeployKeyLeak` in `dependency-gate.ts`: the base64 body joined, each armour line from the third on (the first two are every Ed25519 key's shared header and its public key) and the redactor's placeholder; a hit parks the task with *"Replace it now"*, never printing it.

**Criteria → tests** (unit canaries by mutation through `/private/tmp/claude-501/wp146-implementer/canary.py`: copy aside to the scratch dir, mutate, run, restore, md5 asserted — **9 of 9 fired**: the broker's `cred.get` refusal, the adapter strip, the shadow check, the public-key comparison, the leak search, the signer's own-key check, the self-managed refusal, the agent's refusal of other requests, the passphrase refusal):

(7) is the product owner's.

**Decisions and assumptions.**
- **The key travels in the create request's `password`** (`source: 'deploy_key'`, `username: git`), not a new field: the launcher's credential already crosses that authenticated hop, and the launcher uses it for exactly its mirror and export helpers. The wire, the broker and the helpers all branch on `source`/`ssh`; `cred.get` is refused for it. A reviewer may prefer a field of its own — it is one schema change.
- **The route is a spec field** (`WorkspaceRepo.ssh`) and **a handle field** (`WorkspaceHandle.gitSsh`), both optional on the wire, so a launcher of an earlier build parses and `cliEnvironment(handle)` stays a function of the handle.
- **No protocol version bump** for `ssh.sign`/`ssh.sign.reply`: the shim and the runner are built from one tree, and a shim with no agent socket never sends `ssh.sign`.
- **`list identities` is answered by the shim** from its own environment (the public key is not a secret); only signing crosses to the runner — decision 13b's "a frame pair".
- **The default branch's protection is checked at the probe only**, not before each run (decision 13b item 6 names the probe; 13a item 2's per-run read is the operator's token's). The setup guide says so.
- **The deploy key's run-scoped redaction expires with the run credential's TTL**; the key is a sealed secret of the integration too, so every binding redactor knows it by exact value.
- **The probe of a broken declaration fails both checks, asking nothing**, as WP-141's does for an unconnected account.
- **The test fixture is side-effect free** (`testing/ssh-deploy-key-fixtures.ts`: `@__PURE__` buffers, getters for `FAKE_DEPLOY_KEY`): it is on `@platform/application`'s barrel, and with plain top-level calls the shim's bundle carried the fixture and the key reader (measured: `agentic-runlet.mjs` held the RFC seed). Now `agentic-runlet.mjs` is 716.6 kB against HEAD's 700.7 kB (`pnpm --filter @platform/runlet run build`, `assert-runlet-bundle.mjs` PASS): the agent socket, the `connect` helper and the two frames, and no key code.
- **The fragment the canaries search for is in the seed's base64** (`keyLines[4]`): the first run's fragment, from the third line, was mostly the container's fixed `ssh-ed25519` header — present in every Ed25519 key — and would have proven nothing about this key.

**Sentences falsified** (grep over `docs/`, `packages/`, `apps/`, `test/`, `scripts/`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` for *not in this build*, *`minted`, `static` or `none`*, *`minted | static`*, *(minted|static|none)*, the setup guide's *lands after the first test*):
- **Fixed**: setup guide `:225`–`:232` (form C *not in this build*, *lands after the first test*) and its config table's `run_credential` row (*`minted` or `static`*); `docs/first-local-test.md:72` and *Which today* (*C … lands later*); `docs/operator-guide.md:1269`; technical/03's check list; `db/schema/pipeline.ts`'s `credentialSource` docblock; `static-run-credential.ts`'s `modeField` docblock; the prober's `checks` docblock; the setup guide's *`runs.credential_source`: `minted`, `static` or `none`*; GitLab's static mint hint (now names `deploy_key`, its test updated).
- **Still true, left**: migration 0078's comment (migrations are never edited; 0081 says what changed); `gitlab/config.ts`'s `run_token_owner` docblock (*another `run_credential` value*, now named); TD-028 decisions 13/13a/13b (decisions, read only); research/10's `[unverified]` altssh line (research, not edited — the measurement is in `docs/TODO.md` and `ssh-route.ts`); PROGRESS history.

Docker objects: every container, network and volume the check made is removed by the check (asserted; `docker ps -a` empty of them after each run). **Machine-rule breach, recorded**: one 10-file vitest run was started in the same command as its load reading (load 5.9 read, 15.1 by the time it ran).

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed).
- **The agent owns `/ctl/known_hosts`** (the control directory is uid 1000's), so it can replace the pinned keys; that only lets it connect to a host the sidecar already admits, and a MITM would need the network path. A root-owned file needs the prepare helper to keep it out of the 1000-owned directory.
- **Self-managed GitLab SSH is filed, not built** (decision 13b item 4): it needs an SSH-capable egress path the sidecar does not have.

#### WP-146 — review round 1 (REQUEST CHANGES), addressed

1. **[major] The signer signed any 1–8192 bytes**, so a run could get `SSHSIG` signatures (`ssh-keygen -Y sign`, git commit signing) over data of its choosing — wider than decision 13b item 2's *"the same reach as a credential helper"*. `isGitUserauthRequest` (`launcher/deploy-key-signer.ts`) now admits only an RFC 4252 § 7 user-authentication request: `string session id` (1–64 bytes), `byte 50`, `string "git"`, `string "ssh-connection"`, `string "publickey"` — or OpenSSH's `publickey-hostbound-v00@openssh.com`, which appends the server's host key (PROTOCOL § 3.6) — `bool TRUE`, `string "ssh-ed25519"`, `string <our key blob>`, nothing after. Tests: `packages/infrastructure/src/launcher/deploy-key-signer.test.ts` › "signs a user-authentication request for git with its key, verifiably", and its `it.each` of refusals, each signing nothing (an SSHSIG, another user, another method, another key, trailing bytes, raw data); the agent's `-Y sign` case now expects refusal (signatures 0, refusals 1); the RFC 8032 vector is unchanged. `deploy-key-check.mjs` re-run: **PASS 11/11** (fetch and push still authenticate against `sshd`).
2. **[minor] Limits tested**: › "refuses another key blob, data past the cap, and every request past the run’s budget" (signer); `ssh-agent.test.ts` › "relays at most maxSignRequests per run, then answers FAILURE without asking the runner" and › "answers FAILURE past the in-flight cap while earlier requests wait on the runner" (shim).
3. **[nit]** `DeployKeyRunCredentialGrant.privateKey`'s docblock corrected: the run registry holds one value per run, so the whole key text is registered; the joined body is the leak search's needle, not a redaction.
4. **[nit]** A late `ssh.sign.reply` counts in its own `staleSignReplies`.

Canaries (`canary.py`, copy aside / mutate / run / restore, md5 asserted): accept-all signer, the shim's sign budget, its in-flight cap, the signer's budget — 4/4 fired.


#### WP-147

**A custom CI path is protected at write time, and a default-branch change moves the configuration and readiness reads at once** — rulings (a)/(b) of the row (plan § "Milestone M8"), backlog 442's last halves. Implementer, session 11, on `59401f48`. No migration.

- **(a) the write-time guard** — `createStageRunPlanner` takes a new **required** `ciConfigLocation(projectId, taskId)`; the planner protects `withCiConfigPath(effectiveProtectedPaths(settings), location)` — the CI gate's expression, moved beside `effectiveProtectedPaths` in `settings.ts` so both readers share one — applied **after** the project's own list replaced the default, so no project setting removes it. An `external` or `unknown` location adds nothing and the planner logs it at `info` (`ci_config`, never the provider's text). Production: `createCiConfigLocationReader` (`packages/application/src/pipeline/ci-config-location.ts`): one `get_repository_settings` read through the executor per planned run, between the executor's two transactions; a provider `IntegrationError` becomes `unknown` (reason redacted with the binding's redactor, bounded), anything else propagates (rule 20). `integrations.test.ts`'s door census declares the site.
- **(b) the branch change** — three pieces:
  - the change's transaction (`writeProjectDefaultBranch`) **deletes** the project's `project_repository_config` row (the old branch's reading), beside WP-142's poll-head clear;
  - after the commit the route calls `readNewDefaultBranch` (`packages/application/src/config/default-branch-reading.ts`, composed in `ProjectConfigCommands`): `refreshRepositoryConfig` from the stored (new) branch's head, then `enqueueReadinessRecheck` **pinned to the commit that reading answered**; a failure is logged and the change stands; WP-142's index request is kept;
  - **the refresher's "older reading" rule is branch-aware** (`git-vault.ts`): a read is `behindRecorded` only when the recorded commit is itself reachable from the branch read now. Measured cause: with Autix's shape (`main`'s head an ancestor of `develop`'s), `main`'s reading was refused as *stale* against `develop`'s recorded one, so even the index run left `develop`'s configuration standing.

**Criteria → tests** (canaries scripted, md5 restored, rule 88 — `/private/tmp/claude-501/wp147/canary.py`, seven canaries, each failed its test):
- (1) `packages/application/src/pipeline/planner.test.ts` › "protects deploy/.gitlab-ci.yml when the provider names it, beside the default list" (canary: the planner back to `effectiveProtectedPaths(settings)` → fails, with the next), › "keeps the CI path when the project’s own protected_paths replaced the default list", › "adds nothing for the root path the list already names", › "adds nothing for an external or unknown location, and says so". Reader: `packages/application/src/pipeline/ci-config-location.test.ts` › "refuses the plan on a provider refusal, redacted, so the stage is retried rather than run unprotected (canary: the planted credential is absent)" (renamed at review round 1; canary: redaction removed → fails), › "lets anything that is not a provider refusal escape (rule 20)", › "answers the provider’s custom CI path", › "answers null for a project with no git binding".
- (2) `test/integration/server/default-branch-reads.integration.test.ts` (real PostgreSQL, real mirror over a `file://` origin, `develop` ahead of `main`) › "drops the old branch’s configuration reading in the change’s transaction" (canary: the delete replaced by a select → fails), › "reads main’s configuration and asks for a readiness re-check pinned to main’s head, before any index run", › "records main even when a reading of develop lands after the change" (canary: the vault's new reachability condition removed → fails). `packages/infrastructure/src/knowledge/git-vault.test.ts` › "does not call a read of the new default branch older than a reading of the previous one" (same canary → fails). `packages/application/src/config/default-branch-reading.test.ts` › "reads the configuration and pins a readiness re-check to the commit that reading answered" (canary: the enqueue removed → fails), › "requests no re-check when nothing was recorded, or when the process holds no job client". Route: `apps/server/src/routes/project-repository.test.ts` › "reads the new branch’s configuration and readiness at once after the change, and nothing for a refused one (WP-147)" (canary: the call removed → fails), › "keeps a committed change when the new branch cannot be read now (WP-147)".
- (3) `docs/first-local-test.md` § 1 GoParking (`deploy/.gitlab-ci.yml` protected at write time) and *Moving the default branch* step 3; technical/05 (file guards; configuration read after a branch change); technical/03 (`projects.default_branch`, `project_repository_config`); technical/08 (the PUT).

**Decisions and assumptions.**
- **A provider refusal at plan time does not stop the run**: the guard protects the effective list alone, says so, and the CI gate's tamper check (fail closed on the same read since WP-143) stays the backstop. Stopping every run during a GitLab outage would protect nothing the gate does not.
- **"Invalidated by the change" is a delete**, so between the commit and the reading (and for as long as the mirror cannot be read) the project has **no repository layer** — the state of a never-read project, which may be looser than `develop`'s file. Accepted because the change is refused while any task is live and the runbook moves the project at Observe; refusing runs until the new branch is read would need a fourth status (a migration). Stated in the runbook.
- **The readiness re-check is pinned to the configuration reading's commit**, not to a separate head read: one mirror read, and the configuration and readiness describe the same commit. Nothing new triggers a re-check of a never-evaluated project (the job skips it by name).
- The harness and the other test planners pass `ciConfigLocation: async () => null` (the harness has no fake provider read per run; adding one would add an audit row to every harness run).
- Every planned run now makes one `get_repository_settings` provider read (rate budget: one per stage run, beside the gate's one per tamper check).

**Sentences falsified** (grep: `nothing else`, `re-reads the repository configuration`, `two places`, `write-time path guard does not`, `no row means`):
- **Fixed**: the PUT's OpenAPI description (*"Writes `projects.default_branch` … and nothing else"*); `project-repository.ts`'s docblock (*"asks for a knowledge index of the new branch, which also re-reads the repository configuration there"*); `docs/first-local-test.md:126-127` (same sentence); `repository-config.ts` (*"Refreshed from two places"*); technical/03 (`project_repository_config`: *"no row means never read"*, its writers); technical/05:36 (the protected list); technical/08 (the PUT); `recheck.ts` (the trigger is the index run alone).
- **Still true, left**: WP-143's note *"the planner's write-time path guard does **not** add the custom CI path"* (PROGRESS history); BD-024 (`docs/decisions/**`, not touched — proposed sentence below); technical/12:171 (`.gitlab-ci.yml` in the default `protected_paths` — still the default list).

**Proposed for BD-024** (not written; the brief forbids `docs/decisions/**`): *"Beside the effective `protected_paths`, the platform protects the CI configuration path the git provider names when it is a repository path (GitLab's `ci_config_path`), at write time and in the CI gate; a project cannot narrow it away (WP-147)."*

**Discovered work** (for the refiner; no numbers claimed).
- After a default-branch change with an unreachable mirror the project has no repository layer until a reading succeeds; a `stale` status refusing runs until the new branch is read would close it (a migration and a fourth status).
- The knowledge index's own recorded commit (`kb_index_state`) still describes the old branch until the requested index run; the context pack serves the old branch's vault in that window (the ruling keeps the index request; nothing stale-marks it).

**Residuals.**
- An index run that read `develop` before the change and records after it puts `develop`'s reading back; the next reading of `main` (the requested index run, or a re-read) replaces it — no longer refused as older (the integration case above).
- Nothing was run against GitLab.

#### WP-148

**Re-saving bindings keeps the poll state, a webhook binding hears a push to the stored default branch, and a ticket comment finds its task by issue id** — rulings (a)/(b)/(c) of the row; backlog **444** and WP-145's discovered `ask/commands.ts` item. GitLab's `normalisePush` compares `ref` with it and no longer reads the hook's `project.default_branch` (a push with none is no longer `malformed_payload`); the fake git normaliser applies the same rule.
